short_description.id: Gamayun adalah burung mitos bernubuat dari budaya Rusia, lambang kebijaksanaan dan pengetahuan yang menyampaikan ramalan lewat nyanyiannya.
short_description.en: Gamayun is a prophetic mythical bird of Russian culture, a symbol of wisdom and knowledge that delivers prophecies through its song.

long_description.id: Gamayun dikenal sebagai burung pembawa nubuat dan lambang kebijaksanaan serta pengetahuan. Ia dikatakan tinggal di sebuah pulau di timur yang mitis, tidak jauh dari surga, dan menurut satu sumber dianggap sebagai pembawa kabar para dewa Slavia. Biasanya ia digambarkan sebagai burung hitam besar berkepala perempuan yang menyebarkan pesan ilahi dan ramalan melalui lagu-lagunya.
long_description.en: Gamayun is known as a bird of prophecy and an emblem of wisdom and knowledge. It is said to live on an island in the mythical east, near paradise, and one source calls it a herald of the Slavic gods. It is usually shown as a large black bird with a woman's head that spreads divine messages and prophecies through its songs.

long_description.id: Kesusastraan Rusia abad pertengahan membedakan Gamayun, burung surga yang seumur hidup berada di udara, dari burung mitos lain seperti Alkonost dan Sirin. Dalam buku-buku abad ke-17 sampai ke-19 ia digambarkan tanpa kaki dan tanpa sayap, terus terbang dengan bantuan ekornya, dan jatuhnya menandakan kematian para negarawan. Pada masa itu sosoknya juga dihias pada benda seni terapan, meriam, dan panji.
long_description.en: Medieval Russian writing set Gamayun, a bird of paradise that spends its whole life aloft, apart from other mythical birds such as the Alkonost and the Sirin. Books of the 17th to 19th centuries describe it as having neither legs nor wings, flying endlessly with the help of its tail, its fall foretelling the death of statesmen. In that period its figure also decorated applied-art objects, cannons and banners.

long_description.id: Namanya kemungkinan berasal dari Persia, karena burung Huma dikenal dalam mitologi Persia, dan citranya ditelusuri ke burung humay dari cerita rakyat Iran. Wujud visualnya berubah seiring waktu: mula-mula ia mendapat sayap dan kaki, kemudian wajah perempuan. Satu sumber menyebutnya bagian dari cerita rakyat Rusia, tetapi sumber lain menegaskan tidak ada bukti keberadaannya dalam folklor tradisional Rusia.
long_description.en: Its name may come from Persia, since the Huma bird appears in Persian mythology, and its image is traced to the humay bird of Iranian folklore. Its visual form changed over time: first it gained wings and legs, and later a woman's face. One source places it in Russian folklore, while another stresses that there is no evidence of it in traditional Russian folklore.

long_description.id: Dalam satu sumber, kepakan sayapnya memicu badai mematikan dari timur, dan kehadirannya ditakuti karena penglihatannya hanya meramalkan malapetaka. Popularitasnya meningkat pada akhir abad ke-19 dan awal abad ke-20 berkat sebuah lukisan, dan pada masa Zaman Perak puisi Rusia ia sering tampil sebagai sumber nubuat tragis, misalnya dalam sajak Alexander Blok. Gamayun juga tampil pada lambang kota Smolensk.
long_description.en: In one source, its flight unleashes a deadly storm from the east, and its presence is feared because its visions foretell only disaster. Its popularity grew in the late 19th and early 20th centuries thanks to a painting, and in the Silver Age of Russian poetry it often served as a source of tragic prophecy, as in a poem by Alexander Blok. Gamayun also appears on the coat of arms of Smolensk.

short_description.id: Goldhorn atau Zlatorog adalah chamois jantan putih bertanduk emas dalam folklor Slovenia yang menguasai ketinggian Gunung Triglav dan menjaga harta tersembunyi.
short_description.en: Goldhorn, or Zlatorog, is a white chamois buck with golden horns in Slovene folklore, ruling the heights of Mount Triglav and guarding a hidden treasure.

long_description.id: Dalam folklor Slovenia, Goldhorn atau Zlatorog adalah chamois jantan putih yang legendaris, atau menurut versi lain seekor ibex Alpen, yang wilayahnya berada di ketinggian Gunung Triglav, gunung tertinggi di Slovenia dan puncak tertinggi Pegunungan Alpen Julian. Ia bertanduk emas, memiliki taman di puncak Triglav, dan menjaga sebuah harta tersembunyi. Legenda ini terkenal di seluruh Slovenia, juga di Carinthia Austria dan Friuli-Venezia Giulia Italia.
long_description.en: In Slovene folklore, Goldhorn or Zlatorog is a legendary white chamois buck, or in another version an Alpine ibex, whose realm lay on the heights of Mount Triglav, the tallest mountain in Slovenia and highest peak of the Julian Alps. He had golden horns, kept a garden high on Triglav and guarded a hidden treasure. The legend is well known across Slovenia and also in Austrian Carinthia and Italian Friuli-Venezia Giulia.

long_description.id: Dalam versi yang ditulis Karl Deschmann, tanduk emas Goldhorn adalah kunci harta di pegunungan sekitar Triglav. Seorang pemburu muda dari Lembah Trenta, yang ditolak gadis pujaannya karena seorang saudagar kaya dari Venesia, dibujuk "pemburu hijau" untuk memburu Goldhorn. Hewan itu tertembak, tetapi memakan bunga ajaib Triglav yang tumbuh dari darahnya dan mendapat daya hidup yang luar biasa; ketika ia menyerbu, sang pemburu silau oleh kilau tanduk emasnya, kehilangan pijakan, dan jatuh dari gunung, lalu jasadnya dihanyutkan Sungai Soča.
long_description.en: In the version written by Karl Deschmann, Goldhorn's golden horns were the key to a treasure in the mountains around Triglav. A young hunter from the Trenta Valley, spurned by his sweetheart for a rich merchant from Venice, was talked by the "green hunter" into hunting Goldhorn. The animal was shot but ate a magic Triglav flower sprung from its blood and gained tremendous life power; as it charged, the hunter, dazzled by its golden horns, lost his footing and fell from the mountain, and the river Soča carried his body down.

long_description.id: Versi lain menuturkan bahwa dari darah chamois yang terbunuh tumbuh bunga ajaib yang menghidupkannya kembali; dengan murka Zlatorog membunuh si pemburu, lalu menghancurkan taman gunungnya dan tidak pernah terlihat lagi. Namanya dalam bahasa Slovenia berarti "tanduk emas".
long_description.en: Another version tells that a wonder flower sprang from the slain chamois's blood and brought it back to life; in fury Zlatorog killed the hunter, then destroyed his mountain garden and was never seen again. In Slovene the name means "golden horn".

long_description.id: Kisah Zlatorog pertama kali ditulis, disesuaikan dengan gaya Romantik akhir, dan diterbitkan oleh Karl Deschmann di Laibacher Zeitung pada 21 Februari 1868. Rudolf Baumbach menggubahnya menjadi puisi yang terbit pada 1877, dan Camilla serta Eduard Lucerna menjadikannya opera. Film panjang pertama berbahasa Slovenia, rekaman Janko Ravnik tahun 1931, berjudul In the Kingdom of the Goldhorn, dan Zlatorog juga menjadi merek bir dari pabrik bir Laško.
long_description.en: The Zlatorog story was first written down, recast in a late Romantic style and published by Karl Deschmann in the Laibacher Zeitung on 21 February 1868. Rudolf Baumbach turned it into verse published in 1877, and Camilla and Eduard Lucerna made it an opera. The first full-length Slovene-language film, shot by Janko Ravnik in 1931, was called In the Kingdom of the Goldhorn, and Zlatorog is also a beer brand of the Laško Brewery.

did_you_know.id: Film panjang pertama berbahasa Slovenia, dari tahun 1931, berjudul In the Kingdom of the Goldhorn.
did_you_know.en: The first full-length Slovene-language film, from 1931, was titled In the Kingdom of the Goldhorn.

description.id: Bunga ajaib yang tumbuh dari darahnya memberinya daya hidup kembali.
description.en: A magic flower sprung from his blood restores his life.

summary.id: Pemburu muda yang patah hati memburu Goldhorn demi hartanya; hewan itu hidup kembali berkat bunga ajaib, dan si pemburu jatuh dari gunung.
summary.en: A heartbroken young hunter hunts Goldhorn for its treasure; the animal revives through a magic flower and the hunter falls from the mountain.

description.id: Gunung tertinggi di Slovenia, wilayah kekuasaan Goldhorn.
description.en: The highest mountain in Slovenia, Goldhorn's realm.

description.id: Sungai yang menghanyutkan jasad sang pemburu ke lembah.
description.en: The river that carried the hunter's body to the vale.

description.id: Karl Deschmann menuliskan dan menerbitkan kisah Zlatorog di Laibacher Zeitung.
description.en: Karl Deschmann wrote down and published the Zlatorog story in the Laibacher Zeitung.

description.id: Rudolf Baumbach menerbitkan kisah ini dalam bentuk puisi.
description.en: Rudolf Baumbach published the story in verse.

description.en: The first full-length Slovene film took up the Goldhorn story.

learning_questions.id: Apa pesan legenda Goldhorn tentang keserakahan manusia?
learning_questions.en: What does the Goldhorn legend say about human greed?

claims.quote: is a legendary white chamois buck, or alternatively, an Alpine ibex, that had his realm in the heights of Mount Triglav, the highest mountain in Slovenia and the highest peak of the Julian Alps.

statement.id: Goldhorn adalah chamois jantan putih legendaris, atau menurut versi lain ibex Alpen, yang wilayahnya di ketinggian Gunung Triglav, gunung tertinggi di Slovenia dan puncak tertinggi Alpen Julian.
statement.en: Goldhorn is a legendary white chamois buck, or alternatively an Alpine ibex, whose realm was the heights of Mount Triglav, Slovenia's highest mountain and the highest peak of the Julian Alps.

claims.quote: The legend is well known throughout Slovenia (specifically Carinthia), as well as in Austrian Carinthia, and Italian Friuli-Venezia Giulia.

statement.id: Legenda ini dikenal luas di seluruh Slovenia (khususnya Carinthia), juga di Carinthia Austria dan Friuli-Venezia Giulia Italia.
statement.en: The legend is well known throughout Slovenia (especially Carinthia), and in Austrian Carinthia and Italian Friuli-Venezia Giulia.

claims.quote: The story about Zlatorog was first written down, adapted to the late Romantic style and published by Karl Deschmann (Karel Dežman) in the Laibacher Zeitung, no. 43, on 21 February 1868.

statement.id: Kisah Zlatorog pertama kali ditulis, disesuaikan dengan gaya Romantik akhir, dan diterbitkan oleh Karl Deschmann (Karel Dežman) di Laibacher Zeitung no. 43 pada 21 Februari 1868.
statement.en: The Zlatorog story was first written down, adapted to late Romantic style and published by Karl Deschmann (Karel Dežman) in the Laibacher Zeitung no. 43 on 21 February 1868.

claims.quote: Goldhorn's golden horns were the key to a treasure hidden in the mountains around Triglav.
claims.locator: Summary of the story as written by Karl Deschmann

statement.id: Tanduk emas Goldhorn adalah kunci menuju harta yang tersembunyi di pegunungan sekitar Triglav.
statement.en: Goldhorn's golden horns were the key to a treasure hidden in the mountains around Triglav.

claims.quote: A young and brave hunter from the Trenta Valley fell in love with a beautiful girl and managed to win her heart by bringing her beautiful flowers. However, one day, a rich merchant from Venice came by and tried to gain her attention by giving her golden jewelry and dancing with her.
claims.locator: Summary of the story as written by Karl Deschmann

statement.id: Seorang pemburu muda pemberani dari Lembah Trenta memenangkan hati gadis cantik dengan bunga, tetapi suatu hari saudagar kaya dari Venesia merebut perhatiannya dengan perhiasan emas dan tarian.
statement.en: A brave young hunter from the Trenta Valley won a beautiful girl's heart with flowers, but one day a rich merchant from Venice courted her with golden jewellery and dancing.

claims.quote: Persuaded by another hunter, called the green hunter, who was said to have brought about the fate of several honest boys, he decided to go that very night to find Goldhorn and claim his treasure.
claims.locator: Summary of the story as written by Karl Deschmann

statement.id: Dibujuk pemburu lain, si "pemburu hijau" yang konon telah mencelakai beberapa pemuda jujur, ia memutuskan malam itu juga mencari Goldhorn dan merebut hartanya.
statement.en: Persuaded by another hunter, the "green hunter", said to have doomed several honest lads, he decided that very night to seek Goldhorn and claim its treasure.

claims.quote: The green hunter forced him on to catch the Goldhorn before it ate the magic Triglav flowers that grew from its blood, but it was too late. The Goldhorn had already eaten one and the flower gave it tremendous life power.
claims.locator: Summary of the story as written by Karl Deschmann

statement.id: Pemburu hijau mendesaknya menangkap Goldhorn sebelum hewan itu memakan bunga ajaib Triglav yang tumbuh dari darahnya, tetapi terlambat: Goldhorn sudah memakan satu dan bunga itu memberinya daya hidup yang luar biasa.
statement.en: The green hunter pushed him to catch Goldhorn before it ate the magic Triglav flowers growing from its blood, but too late: Goldhorn had eaten one, gaining tremendous life power.

claims.quote: It ran towards the hunter, who being blinded by the bliss of its golden horns, lost balance and fell from the mountain. The river Soča brought his corpse to the vale.
claims.locator: Summary of the story as written by Karl Deschmann

statement.id: Goldhorn berlari ke arah si pemburu, yang silau oleh kilau tanduk emasnya, kehilangan keseimbangan, dan jatuh dari gunung; Sungai Soča membawa jasadnya ke lembah.
statement.en: It ran at the hunter, who, dazzled by its golden horns, lost his balance and fell from the mountain; the river Soča carried his body to the vale.

claims.quote: The story of Goldhorn was put into verses by Rudolf Baumbach and published in 1877, becoming his most popular work. It was turned into an opera by Camilla and Eduard Lucerna.

statement.id: Kisah Goldhorn digubah menjadi puisi oleh Rudolf Baumbach dan terbit pada 1877, menjadi karyanya yang paling populer; Camilla dan Eduard Lucerna menjadikannya opera.
statement.en: The Goldhorn story was put into verse by Rudolf Baumbach, published in 1877 and his most popular work; Camilla and Eduard Lucerna turned it into an opera.

claims.quote: The first Slovene-language, full-length film, recorded in 1931 by Janko Ravnik, was titled In the Kingdom of the Goldhorn.

statement.id: Film panjang pertama berbahasa Slovenia, direkam Janko Ravnik pada 1931, berjudul In the Kingdom of the Goldhorn.
statement.en: The first full-length Slovene-language film, recorded by Janko Ravnik in 1931, was titled In the Kingdom of the Goldhorn.

claims.quote: Zlatorog is also a brand of beer produced by the Laško Brewery.

statement.id: Zlatorog juga merupakan merek bir produksi pabrik bir Laško.
statement.en: Zlatorog is also a beer brand produced by the Laško Brewery.

claims.quote: Zlatorog (deutsch: Goldhorn) ist eine Sagengestalt aus den slowenischen Alpen.

statement.id: Zlatorog (bahasa Jerman: Goldhorn) adalah tokoh legenda dari Pegunungan Alpen Slovenia.
statement.en: Zlatorog (German: Goldhorn) is a legendary figure from the Slovenian Alps.

claims.quote: Er hatte goldene Hörner, besaß hoch oben am Triglav einen Garten und war Hüter eines verborgenen Schatzes.

statement.id: Ia bertanduk emas, memiliki taman tinggi di Triglav, dan menjadi penjaga harta tersembunyi.
statement.en: He had golden horns, owned a garden high on Triglav and was guardian of a hidden treasure.

claims.quote: Aus dem Blut des getöteten Gamsbocks wuchs auf der Stelle eine Wunderblume, die Zlatorog das Leben zurückgab. In rasender Wut tötete Zlatorog den Übeltäter. Hernach zerstörte er seinen Gebirgsgarten und ward nie mehr gesehen.

statement.id: Dari darah chamois yang terbunuh seketika tumbuh bunga ajaib yang menghidupkan Zlatorog kembali; dengan murka ia membunuh si penjahat, lalu menghancurkan taman gunungnya dan tak pernah terlihat lagi.
statement.en: From the slain chamois's blood a wonder flower sprang up at once and gave Zlatorog back his life; in a rage he killed the wrongdoer, then destroyed his mountain garden and was never seen again.

claims.quote: ズラトロクとは、スロベニア語で「金の角」を意味する。この伝説は、スロベニア、特にコロシュカ地方で有名であり

statement.id: Zlatorog (ズラトロク) dalam bahasa Slovenia berarti "tanduk emas"; legendanya terkenal di Slovenia, terutama wilayah Koroška.
statement.en: Zlatorog means "golden horn" in Slovene; the legend is famous in Slovenia, especially the Koroška region.

claims.quote: In Slovene folklore, Goldhorn or Goldenhorn

statement.id: Dalam folklor Slovenia ia disebut Goldhorn atau Goldenhorn.
statement.en: In Slovene folklore he is called Goldhorn or Goldenhorn.

summary.id: Versi Karl Deschmann: pemburu silau oleh tanduk emas dan jatuh dari gunung.
summary.en: Karl Deschmann's version: the hunter, dazzled by the golden horns, falls from the mountain.

summary.id: Sumber lain: Zlatorog yang murka membunuh si pemburu.
summary.en: Another source: the enraged Zlatorog kills the hunter.

summary.id: Umumnya chamois jantan putih.
summary.en: Usually a white chamois buck.

summary.id: Versi lain: ibex Alpen.
summary.en: Alternatively: an Alpine ibex.

short_description.id: Grand'Goule, "Mulut Besar", adalah naga legenda Poitiers yang memangsa biarawati di ruang bawah tanah Biara Sainte-Croix sampai diusir Santa Radegonda.
short_description.en: The Grand'Goule, 'Big Mouth', is a legendary dragon of Poitiers that devoured nuns in the cellars of the Abbey of Sainte-Croix until St Radegund drove it out.

long_description.id: Grand'Goule, "Mulut Besar" dalam dialek Poitevin, adalah naga cerita rakyat Poitiers, semacam versi lokal tarasque. Pada masa Santa Radegonda (abad ke-6) ia tinggal di dasar sungai Clain, masuk ke ruang bawah tanah saat air naik, dan memangsa biarawati Biara Sainte-Croix. Radegonda mengusirnya dengan salib kecil, air suci, dan doa, atau menurut versi lain dengan serpihan Salib Sejati, ke sungai.
long_description.en: The Grand'Goule, 'Big Mouth' in Poitevin, is a folk dragon of Poitiers, a sort of local tarasque. In St Radegund's time (6th century) it lived at the bottom of the Clain, entered the cellars when the water rose, and devoured the nuns of the Abbey of Sainte-Croix. Radegund drove it off with a small cross, holy water and prayer, or in another version with the piece of the True Cross, into the river.

long_description.id: Sebuah piagam tahun 1466 mencatat naga dalam prosesi Hari Rogasi di Poitiers. Patung kayu karya Jean Gargot (1677) diarak dalam prosesi itu sementara anak-anak melemparkan kue casse-museau dan berseru "Boune sainte veurmine"; prosesi ini berhenti pada abad ke-19 dan patungnya kini di Musée Sainte-Croix.
long_description.en: A charter of 1466 records a dragon in the Rogation procession at Poitiers. Jean Gargot's wooden statue (1677) was paraded while children threw casse-museau cakes and cried 'Boune sainte veurmine'; the procession ended in the 19th century and the statue is now in the Musée Sainte-Croix.

famous_for.id: Prosesi Hari Rogasi dan kue casse-museau.
famous_for.en: The Rogation procession and casse-museau cakes.

description.id: Ruang bawah tanahnya dihantui Grand'Goule.
description.en: Its cellars were haunted by the Grand'Goule.

description.id: Museum yang menyimpan patung tahun 1677.
description.en: The museum holding the 1677 statue.

description.id: Naga tercatat dalam prosesi Hari Rogasi.
description.en: A dragon is recorded in the Rogation procession.

description.id: Biara Sainte-Croix memesan patung naga.
description.en: The Abbey of Sainte-Croix commissions the dragon statue.

note.en: The dragon it parallels.
The saint who drove it out.

claims.quote: The Grande Goule or Grande-Goule (Poitevin dialect: Grand'Goule ... is a folklore dragon that continues to be celebrated in the Poitou region (city of Poitiers) in France.

statement.id: Grande Goule atau Grand'Goule (dialek Poitevin) adalah naga cerita rakyat yang masih dirayakan di Poitou (kota Poitiers), Prancis.
statement.en: The Grande Goule or Grand'Goule (Poitevin dialect) is a folk dragon still celebrated in Poitou (the city of Poitiers), France.

claims.quote: The Grand'Goule is considered to be a local version of the tarasque.

statement.id: Grand'Goule dianggap versi lokal tarasque.
statement.en: The Grand'Goule is considered a local version of the tarasque.

claims.quote: La bête, décrite comme un dragon monstrueux, aurait vécu au temps de sainte Radegonde, donc au VIe siècle de notre ère. Elle vivait au fond du Clain, et, lors de la montée des eaux, entrait dans les caves labyrinthiques qui traversaient le sol poitevin.

statement.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Prancis, binatang ini naga mengerikan dari masa Santa Radegonda (abad ke-6) yang tinggal di dasar sungai Clain dan saat air naik memasuki ruang bawah tanah berliku di bawah Poitiers.
statement.en: According to the French article, the beast was a monstrous dragon of the time of St Radegund (6th century) that lived at the bottom of the Clain and, when the water rose, entered the maze of cellars under Poitiers.

claims.quote: According to legend, the monster haunted the cellars of the Abbey of Sainte-Croix at Poitiers, and used to devour the nuns who descended there, until St. Radegund expelled it.

statement.id: Menurut legenda, monster itu menghantui ruang bawah tanah Biara Sainte-Croix di Poitiers dan memangsa para biarawati yang turun ke sana sampai Santa Radegonda mengusirnya.
statement.en: By legend the monster haunted the cellars of the Abbey of Sainte-Croix at Poitiers and devoured the nuns who went down there until St Radegund drove it out.

claims.quote: Désireuse d'en finir avec la bête, Radegonde s'arma d'une petite croix, puis d'eau bénite, et, une fois face à face avec la bête, l'aspergea, dit une prière, et la bête disparut dans d'atroces souffrances.

statement.id: Radegonda membawa salib kecil dan air suci, memercikkannya kepada binatang itu sambil berdoa, dan binatang itu lenyap dalam kesakitan hebat.
statement.en: Radegund armed herself with a small cross and holy water, sprinkled the beast and prayed, and it vanished in terrible agony.

claims.quote: She harnessed the power of the piece of the True Cross held by the Abbey, and by making a sign of the cross, drove the monster out of the cellar into the river.

statement.id: Versi lain menyebut ia memakai kuasa serpihan Salib Sejati milik biara dan dengan tanda salib mengusir monster itu dari ruang bawah tanah ke sungai.
statement.en: Another version says she used the power of the abbey's piece of the True Cross and, with a sign of the cross, drove the monster from the cellar into the river.

claims.quote: What has been claimed to be an early attestation to the Grande Goule is a charter dated 1466 noting that a "dragon" was among the banners and ensigns being promenaded through the streets of Poitiers for the Rogation days procession.

statement.id: Bukti awal yang diajukan adalah piagam tahun 1466 yang mencatat "naga" di antara panji yang diarak di Poitiers saat prosesi Hari Rogasi.
statement.en: A claimed early attestation is a charter of 1466 noting a 'dragon' among the banners paraded through Poitiers in the Rogation days procession.

claims.quote: A sculpture by cabinetmaker Jean Gargot in 1677, commissioned  by the Abbey of Sainte-Croix at Poitiers, has survived into the modern age, and now housed in the Musée Sainte-Croix, in Poitiers.

statement.id: Patung karya tukang kayu Jean Gargot tahun 1677, pesanan Biara Sainte-Croix, masih ada dan kini disimpan di Musée Sainte-Croix, Poitiers.
statement.en: A sculpture by the cabinetmaker Jean Gargot from 1677, commissioned by the Abbey of Sainte-Croix, survives and is now in the Musée Sainte-Croix, Poitiers.

claims.quote: Le dragon était promené dans les rues, et la tradition voulait que les enfants lui jettent des petits gâteaux – appelés casse-museaux – en disant cette prière : « Boune sainte veurmine, priez pour nous ! »

statement.id: Naga itu diarak di jalan, dan anak-anak melemparkan kue kecil yang disebut casse-museau kepadanya sambil berdoa "Boune sainte veurmine, priez pour nous!".
statement.en: The dragon was paraded through the streets, and children threw little cakes called casse-museaux at it, praying 'Boune sainte veurmine, priez pour nous!'

claims.quote: Cette procession s'est arrêtée au XIXe siècle

statement.id: Prosesi ini berhenti pada abad ke-19.
statement.en: The procession ended in the 19th century.

claims.quote: グラン・グール（ポワトゥー方言: Grand'Goule、「大口」・「大きな獣の口」の意。 Grande Goule、Grande-Gouleとも）は、フランス・ポワトゥー州（ポワティエ市）の伝承におけるドラゴン。

statement.id: Artikel bahasa Jepang juga menyebut Grand'Goule, "mulut besar", naga dalam tradisi Poitou (Poitiers), Prancis.
statement.en: The Japanese article also calls the Grand'Goule, 'big mouth', a dragon of the lore of Poitou (Poitiers), France.

summary.id: Salib kecil, air suci, dan doa; binatang itu lenyap.
summary.en: A small cross, holy water and prayer; the beast vanished.

summary.id: Serpihan Salib Sejati; monster diusir ke sungai.
summary.en: The piece of the True Cross; the monster was driven into the river.

short_description.id: Graoully adalah naga legenda Metz yang tinggal di amfiteater Romawi dan meracuni kota sampai dikalahkan Santo Klemens, uskup pertama Metz.
short_description.en: Graoully is a legendary dragon of Metz that lived in the Roman amphitheatre and poisoned the city until Saint Clement, its first bishop, overcame it.

long_description.id: Graoully adalah naga dalam cerita rakyat Metz yang tinggal di amfiteater Romawi bersama banyak ular; napas berbisa mereka membuat kota tak bisa dimasuki. Santo Klemens mengangkat salib, mengikat Graoully dengan stolanya, dan menuntunnya ke Sungai Seille, tempat menurut satu versi monster itu ditelan bumi; versi lain menyebut Klemens menusuknya dengan tombak. Versi pertama legenda ini dari akhir abad ke-10 dan melambangkan kemenangan Kristen atas paganisme.
long_description.en: Graoully is a dragon of Metz folklore that lived in the Roman amphitheatre with many serpents whose venomous breath sealed off the city. Saint Clement raised his cross, bound Graoully with his stole and led it to the River Seille, where in one version the earth swallowed it; other versions have him spear it. The legend's first version dates from the late 10th century and symbolises Christianity's victory over paganism.

long_description.id: Namanya mungkin dari grouiller, "berkerumun", atau dari bahasa Jerman gräulich, "mengerikan". Patungnya diarak di Metz sampai abad ke-19, nama Rue Taison dikaitkan dengan peringatan tentangnya, dan ia menjadi lambang kota serta klub FC Metz sampai 2021.
long_description.en: Its name may come from grouiller, 'to swarm', or German gräulich, 'horrible'. Its effigy was paraded in Metz until the 19th century, the Rue Taison is linked to a warning about it, and it became a city symbol and the FC Metz emblem until 2021.

who.en: The dragon of the Metz amphitheatre.

role.en: Poisoned the city until driven out.

famous_for.en: Defeated by Saint Clement.

description.id: Arena Romawi tempat Graoully tinggal.
description.en: The Roman arena where Graoully lived.

description.id: Tempat Graoully dibawa pergi.
description.en: Where Graoully was led away.

note.en: The bishop who overcame it.

claims.quote: In French folklore, Graoully (spelled as Graouli, Graouilly, Graouille or Graully) is a creature with the appearance of a dragon. According to legend, it lived in the arena of the Roman amphitheater in Metz, France. Legends state that Saint Clement of Metz fought against Graoully and vanquished the beast.

statement.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Prancis, Graoully (juga Graouli, Graouilly, Graouille, atau Graully) adalah makhluk berwujud naga yang menurut legenda tinggal di arena amfiteater Romawi di Metz, dan Santo Klemens dari Metz melawan serta mengalahkannya.
statement.en: In French folklore Graoully (also Graouli, Graouilly, Graouille or Graully) is a dragon-like creature that by legend lived in the arena of the Roman amphitheatre at Metz, and Saint Clement of Metz fought and overcame it.

claims.quote: Mais des serpents installés dans l'amphithéâtre empoisonnent l'air de leur souffle venimeux et interdisent ainsi l'accès à la ville.

statement.id: Ular-ular di amfiteater meracuni udara dengan napas berbisa sehingga orang tidak bisa memasuki kota.
statement.en: Serpents in the amphitheatre poisoned the air with their venomous breath and so barred access to the city.

claims.quote: The bishop went to the serpents pit, held up his cross and captured Le Graoully with his stole – the long wide band worn over the shoulders. He then led the dragon away and made sure it disappeared over the Seille River along with the rest of the serpents.

statement.id: Sang uskup pergi ke sarang ular, mengangkat salibnya, menangkap Graoully dengan stolanya, lalu menuntun naga itu pergi hingga lenyap di seberang Sungai Seille bersama ular-ular lainnya.
statement.en: The bishop went to the serpents' pit, raised his cross, caught Graoully with his stole, and led the dragon away until it vanished across the River Seille with the other serpents.

claims.quote: However, in many depictions and versions of the story, Saint Clément instead slew the dragon by piercing it with a polearm.

statement.id: Namun dalam banyak gambaran dan versi, Santo Klemens justru membunuh naga itu dengan menusuknya memakai tombak bergagang panjang.
statement.en: In many depictions and versions, however, Saint Clement instead killed the dragon by piercing it with a polearm.

claims.quote: Dort wurde das Ungeheuer vom Erdboden verschluckt. Clemens verschloss das Loch mit einem Felsen, der angeblich noch heute zu sehen ist.

statement.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Jerman, di sebuah pulau di Seille monster itu ditelan bumi, dan Klemens menutup lubangnya dengan batu yang konon masih terlihat sampai kini.
statement.en: According to the German article, on an island in the Seille the monster was swallowed by the earth, and Clement sealed the hole with a rock said still to be visible.

claims.quote: It is believed that the word Graoully derives from the French word "grouiller" meaning "swarm".

statement.id: Kata Graoully diyakini berasal dari kata Prancis grouiller, "berkerumun".
statement.en: The word Graoully is believed to come from French grouiller, 'to swarm'.

claims.quote: Der Name soll sich von „gräulich“ (schrecklich) ableiten.

statement.id: Artikel bahasa Jerman menyebut namanya mungkin dari kata gräulich, "mengerikan".
statement.en: The German article says the name may come from gräulich, 'horrible'.

claims.quote: La première version de la légende de Saint Clément de Metz date de la fin du Xe siècle.

statement.id: Versi pertama legenda Santo Klemens dari Metz berasal dari akhir abad ke-10.
statement.en: The first version of the legend of Saint Clement of Metz dates from the late 10th century.

claims.quote: Cette légende représente symboliquement la destruction des religions païennes — traditionnellement représentées par la figure du serpent et du dragon — et leur remplacement par le christianisme.

statement.id: Legenda ini melambangkan hancurnya agama pagan, yang biasa digambarkan sebagai ular dan naga, dan penggantiannya oleh agama Kristen.
statement.en: The legend symbolises the destruction of pagan religions, traditionally shown as serpent and dragon, and their replacement by Christianity.

claims.quote: A procession with an effigy of the dragon was held in the city until the nineteenth century.

statement.id: Prosesi dengan patung naga itu diadakan di kota sampai abad ke-19.
statement.en: A procession with an effigy of the dragon was held in the city until the 19th century.

claims.quote: Der Name der Rue Taison, einer Straße unweit der Kathedrale, wird auf eine Warnung vor dem Graoully zurückgeführt: „Taisons, taisons nous, voilà le Graoully qui passe“

statement.id: Nama Rue Taison dekat katedral konon berasal dari peringatan tentang Graoully: "Taisons, taisons nous, voilà le Graoully qui passe" (diamlah, Graoully sedang lewat).
statement.en: The name of the Rue Taison near the cathedral is traced to a warning about Graoully: 'Taisons, taisons nous, voilà le Graoully qui passe' (hush, the Graoully is passing).

claims.quote: Eine Figur des Graoully befindet sich in der Krypta der Kathedrale; eine Kopie davon hängt in einem Saal der Hohkönigsburg. Bis 2021 war das Fabeltier auch auf dem Wappen des Fußballclubs FC Metz zu sehen.

statement.id: Patung Graoully ada di kripta katedral Metz, salinannya tergantung di Hohkönigsburg, dan sampai 2021 makhluk ini muncul di lambang klub sepak bola FC Metz.
statement.en: A figure of Graoully is in the cathedral crypt, a copy hangs in a hall of the Hohkönigsburg, and until 2021 the beast featured on the crest of FC Metz.

summary.id: Dituntun dengan stola dan lenyap di seberang Seille.
summary.en: Led away with the stole and vanished across the Seille.

summary.id: Ditusuk tombak oleh Santo Klemens.
summary.en: Speared by Saint Clement.

short_description.id: Guajona adalah nenek bertudung hitam dari tradisi Cantabria yang pada malam hari mengisap darah anak-anak yang tidur dengan satu giginya yang panjang.
short_description.en: The Guajona is a black-hooded hag of the tradition of Cantabria who sucks the blood of sleeping children at night with her single long tooth.

long_description.id: Guajona atau Lumia adalah monster dari tradisi lisan Cantabria, nenek kurus berjubah hitam berkaki burung, berwajah kuning berkutil, bermata kecil berkilau, dengan satu gigi hitam panjang sampai bawah dagu. Ia hanya keluar pada malam hari, diam-diam masuk ke rumah, dan mengisap darah anak serta remaja yang tidur tanpa membunuh mereka, sehingga mereka bangun lemah dan pucat.
long_description.en: The Guajona or Lumia is a monster of the oral tradition of Cantabria, a thin black-cloaked hag with bird's feet, a yellow warty face, small bright eyes and one long black tooth reaching below her chin. She only comes out at night, slips into houses and drinks the blood of sleeping children and youths without killing them, so they wake weak and pale.

long_description.id: Ia salah satu dari sedikit mitos vampir Spanyol; sumber berbeda apakah ia juga menyerang orang dewasa. Namanya bentuk pembesar dari Guaja (Asturias: Guaxa), mungkin dari bahasa Arab wahsh, "binatang buas", atau dari bahasa Latin hostem, "musuh". Miguel de Unamuno pernah mengutipnya.
long_description.en: She is one of Spain's few vampire myths; sources differ on whether she also attacks adults. Her name is an augmentative of Guaja (Asturian Guaxa), perhaps from Arabic wahsh, 'wild beast', or from Latin hostem, 'enemy'. Miguel de Unamuno quoted her.

famous_for.en: Her long black tooth.

claims.quote: La Guajona o Lumia es un monstruo mitológico de la tradición oral de Cantabria.

statement.id: Guajona atau Lumia adalah monster mitologis dari tradisi lisan Cantabria.
statement.en: The Guajona or Lumia is a mythological monster of the oral tradition of Cantabria.

claims.quote: La creencia estima que es una vieja delgada tapada de la cabeza a los pies con un manto negro; sus manos son sarmentosas y los pies patas de ave; su cara es amarilla, consumida, rugosa, peluda y con verrugas; sus ojos son diminutos y brillantes como estrellas

statement.id: Ia nenek kurus yang tertutup jubah hitam dari kepala sampai kaki, bertangan kurus berbonggol dan berkaki burung, berwajah kuning, kisut, berbulu, dan berkutil, bermata kecil berkilau seperti bintang.
statement.en: She is a thin old woman covered head to foot in a black cloak, with gnarled hands and bird's feet, a yellow, wasted, wrinkled, hairy, warty face, and tiny eyes bright as stars.

claims.quote: la nariz aquilina y la boca provista de un único diente negro, largo y afilado que le llega hasta debajo de la barbilla y utiliza para sorber sangre.

statement.id: Hidungnya bengkok dan mulutnya bergigi tunggal hitam, panjang, dan tajam sampai ke bawah dagu, yang dipakai untuk mengisap darah.
statement.en: Her nose is hooked and her mouth holds a single long, sharp black tooth reaching below her chin, used to suck blood.

claims.quote: Sólo sale de noche ocultándose entre las sombras y se desconoce dónde duerme de día, aunque se sospecha que se esconde bajo tierra.

statement.id: Ia hanya keluar pada malam hari, bersembunyi dalam bayangan, dan tidak diketahui di mana ia tidur pada siang hari, meski diduga bersembunyi di bawah tanah.
statement.en: She only comes out at night, hiding in the shadows; where she sleeps by day is unknown, though she is thought to hide underground.

claims.quote: Entra en las casas sin hacerse notar y se acerca en silencio a los niños y jóvenes sanos dormidos para chuparles la sangre clavándoles en vena su diente, aunque no los mata, sino que los deja casi exangües

statement.id: Ia masuk ke rumah tanpa ketahuan, diam-diam mendekati anak dan remaja sehat yang tidur, lalu menancapkan giginya ke pembuluh darah untuk mengisap darah, tanpa membunuh mereka tetapi membuat mereka hampir kehabisan darah.
statement.en: She slips into houses unnoticed, quietly approaches healthy sleeping children and youths and sinks her tooth into a vein to suck their blood, not killing them but leaving them almost bloodless.

claims.quote: No ataca a los viejos o adultos. Se trata de uno de los escasos mitos o leyendas sobre vampiros que existen en España.

statement.id: Ia tidak menyerang orang tua atau dewasa; ini salah satu dari sedikit mitos vampir di Spanyol.
statement.en: She does not attack the old or adults; it is one of Spain's few vampire myths.

claims.quote: Guajona also attacks adults. This is one of the few myths or legends about vampires that exist in Spain, along with the Conde Estruch.

statement.id: Artikel bahasa Inggris justru menyebut Guajona juga menyerang orang dewasa, dan bersama Conde Estruch menjadi salah satu dari sedikit legenda vampir di Spanyol.
statement.en: The English article instead says the Guajona also attacks adults and, with the Conde Estruch, is one of Spain's few vampire legends.

claims.quote: Guajona es un aumentativo de Guaja, presente también en la vecina mitología asturiana como Guaxa. El origen de Guaja o Guaxa podría estar en el árabe clásico وحش wahsh, con el significado de "fiera", como sostiene Xosé Lluis García Arias.

statement.id: Guajona adalah bentuk pembesar dari Guaja, yang dalam mitologi Asturias disebut Guaxa; menurut Xosé Lluis García Arias asalnya mungkin bahasa Arab klasik wahsh, "binatang buas".
statement.en: Guajona is an augmentative of Guaja, known in neighbouring Asturian mythology as Guaxa; according to Xosé Lluis García Arias it may come from Classical Arabic wahsh, 'wild beast'.

claims.quote: Xulio Concepción, por su parte, lo relaciona con el latín hostem: "enemigo", a su vez derivado del indoeuropeo ghos-ti: "extranjero, huésped".

statement.id: Xulio Concepción mengaitkannya dengan bahasa Latin hostem, "musuh", dari akar Indo-Eropa ghos-ti, "orang asing, tamu".
statement.en: Xulio Concepción links it instead to Latin hostem, 'enemy', from Indo-European ghos-ti, 'stranger, guest'.

claims.quote: It is also quoted by Miguel de Unamuno.

statement.id: Ia juga dikutip oleh Miguel de Unamuno.
statement.en: It is also quoted by Miguel de Unamuno.

claims.quote: Ĝi estas ekzemplo de vampireca estaĵo, kio estas malabunda en la mitaroj de Hispanio.

statement.id: Artikel bahasa Esperanto juga menyebutnya contoh makhluk mirip vampir yang jarang dalam mitologi Spanyol.
statement.en: The Esperanto article also calls it an example of a vampire-like being, rare in Spanish mythologies.

summary.en: Does not attack the old or adults.

summary.en: Also attacks adults.

short_description.id: Guivre atau vouivre adalah naga berwujud ular bernapas racun dari legenda Prancis abad pertengahan, agresif tetapi takut pada manusia telanjang.
short_description.en: The guivre or vouivre is a serpentine, venom-breathing dragon of medieval French legend, aggressive yet afraid of naked humans.

long_description.id: Guivre, givre, atau vouivre adalah nama Prancis untuk makhluk mitis berwujud ular yang setara dengan lindworm atau wyvern; namanya berasal dari kata Latin vipera, dan kata Inggris wyvern berasal darinya. Ia bertubuh panjang seperti ular dan berkepala naga, kadang bertanduk, bernapas racun, dan tinggal di kolam, danau, hutan, dan tempat lembap. Ia sangat agresif tetapi tersipu dan memalingkan muka bila melihat manusia telanjang.
long_description.en: Guivre, givre or vouivre is the French name for a serpentine mythical creature equivalent to a lindworm or wyvern; the name comes from Latin vipera, and English wyvern comes from it. It has a long serpentine body and dragon's head, sometimes horns, venomous breath, and lives in pools, lakes, forests and damp places. It is highly aggressive yet blushes and looks away on seeing a naked human.

long_description.id: Dalam heraldik vouivre disebut guivre, dan di Lorraine, Bourgogne, Franche-Comté, Jura, serta Swiss ia naga berkaki dua atau ular bersayap yang membawa batu merah delima di dahinya. Dalam kisah Santo Samson dari Dol, Santo Suliao mengeluarkan seekor guivre kecil dari jubah imam yang tamak, lalu mengusirnya.
long_description.en: In heraldry the vouivre is called guivre, and in Lorraine, Burgundy, Franche-Comté, the Jura and Switzerland it is a two-legged dragon or winged serpent bearing a carbuncle on its brow. In the tale of Samson of Dol, Saint Suliao pulls a small guivre from a greedy priest's robe and exorcises it.

famous_for.en: Fear of naked humans.

description.id: Guivre bernapas racun.
description.en: The guivre has venomous breath.

description.id: Guivre takut pada manusia telanjang dan memalingkan muka.
description.en: The guivre fears naked humans and looks away.

summary.id: Seekor guivre muncul di jubah imam yang menyembunyikan roti, lalu diusir oleh Santo Suliao.
summary.en: A guivre appears in the robe of a priest who hid bread and is exorcised by Saint Suliao.

note.en: The word wyvern comes from vouivre.

claims.quote: Guivre (or givre) and vouivre are French names for a type of serpentine mythical creature, by extension a dragon, by some accords, equivalent to a lindworm or wyvern.

statement.id: Guivre (atau givre) dan vouivre adalah nama Prancis untuk sejenis makhluk mitis berwujud ular, lebih luas lagi naga, yang menurut sebagian pihak setara dengan lindworm atau wyvern.
statement.en: Guivre (or givre) and vouivre are French names for a serpentine mythical creature, by extension a dragon, by some accounts equivalent to a lindworm or wyvern.

claims.quote: In legend they are portrayed as serpentine creatures who possessed venomous breath and prowled the countryside of Medieval France.

statement.id: Dalam legenda mereka digambarkan sebagai makhluk mirip ular bernapas racun yang berkeliaran di pedesaan Prancis abad pertengahan.
statement.en: In legend they are serpentine creatures with venomous breath that prowled the countryside of medieval France.

claims.quote: The English wyvern (a type of dragon) derives from Old French "vouivre".

statement.id: Kata Inggris wyvern berasal dari kata Prancis Kuno vouivre.
statement.en: The English word wyvern derives from Old French vouivre.

claims.quote: Guivres (alternatively givres) were said to possess a long, serpentine body and a dragon's head. The hind feet are not as visible if present at all. The guivre had horns in its forehead in some accounts, as well.

statement.id: Guivre bertubuh panjang seperti ular dan berkepala naga, kaki belakangnya hampir tak terlihat kalaupun ada, dan dalam sebagian kisah bertanduk di dahi.
statement.en: Guivres had a long serpentine body and a dragon's head, hind feet barely visible if present at all, and in some accounts horns on the forehead.

claims.quote: Locally in France, it was known as an extremely aggressive creature that would sometimes attack without being provoked. They were afraid of naked humans, and when saw them, blushed and looked away.

statement.id: Di Prancis ia dikenal sangat agresif dan kadang menyerang tanpa sebab, tetapi takut pada manusia telanjang: bila melihatnya, guivre tersipu dan memalingkan muka.
statement.en: Locally in France it was known as extremely aggressive, sometimes attacking unprovoked, yet it feared naked humans and would blush and look away on seeing one.

claims.quote: Documentation points to their residence as being in small bodies of water like pools and lakes, forests, and any damp place.

statement.id: Guivre tinggal di perairan kecil seperti kolam dan danau, di hutan, dan di tempat lembap.
statement.en: Guivres lived in small bodies of water like pools and lakes, in forests and in any damp place.

claims.quote: Samson of Dol was present at an encounter between a small dragon-like creature, known as La Guivre ("the guivre"), and a priest.

statement.id: Santo Samson dari Dol menyaksikan pertemuan seorang imam dengan makhluk kecil mirip naga yang disebut La Guivre.
statement.en: Samson of Dol witnessed an encounter between a priest and a small dragon-like creature called La Guivre.

claims.quote: He admonished the priest and removed a hideous serpentine creature from the robe. There, he exorcised it and then compelled another man to throw it from the roof of a building in Garot.

statement.id: Santo Suliao menegur imam yang menyembunyikan roti di jubahnya, mengeluarkan makhluk ular yang mengerikan dari jubah itu, mengusirnya, lalu menyuruh orang lain melemparkannya dari atap sebuah bangunan di Garot.
statement.en: Saint Suliao rebuked the priest who had hidden bread in his robe, pulled a hideous serpentine creature from it, exorcised it and had another man throw it from a roof in Garot.

claims.quote: La vouivre est une créature légendaire présente dans plusieurs pays européens, ayant généralement la forme d'un dragon bipède ou d'un serpent ailé. Elle est souvent censée porter une escarboucle sur le front. En héraldique, elle est aussi appelée guivre.

statement.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Prancis, vouivre adalah makhluk legenda di beberapa negara Eropa, biasanya berupa naga berkaki dua atau ular bersayap yang sering membawa batu merah delima di dahinya, dan dalam heraldik disebut guivre.
statement.en: According to the French article, the vouivre is a legendary creature of several European countries, usually a two-legged dragon or winged serpent often bearing a carbuncle on its brow, called guivre in heraldry.

claims.quote: Ce mot est un régionalisme linguistique propre à la Lorraine, la Bourgogne, la Franche-Comté, le Jura et la Suisse.

statement.id: Kata vouivre adalah regionalisme khas Lorraine, Bourgogne, Franche-Comté, Jura, dan Swiss.
statement.en: The word vouivre is a regionalism of Lorraine, Burgundy, Franche-Comté, the Jura and Switzerland.

claims.quote: Todas estas formas se derivan en última instancia del latín Vipera, como es el Español víbora.

statement.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Spanyol, semua bentuk ini akhirnya berasal dari kata Latin vipera, seperti kata Spanyol víbora.
statement.en: According to the Spanish article, all these forms ultimately come from Latin vipera, like Spanish víbora.

short_description.id: Hercinia adalah burung legendaris dari Hutan Hercynia yang bulunya bersinar seperti api pada malam hari, dicatat Plinius Tua dan bestiari abad pertengahan.
short_description.en: The hercinia is a legendary bird of the Hercynian Forest whose feathers shine like fire at night, recorded by Pliny the Elder and the medieval bestiaries.

long_description.id: Hercinia adalah burung legendaris Hutan Hercynia di Germania kuno. Plinius Tua pada abad ke-1 menulis bahwa bulunya bersinar seperti api pada malam hari, dan pada abad ke-7 Isidorus dari Sevilla menyebut bulu yang diletakkan di tanah memancarkan cahaya penunjuk jalan. Ia digambarkan dalam bestiari abad pertengahan.
long_description.en: The hercinia is a legendary bird of the Hercynian Forest of ancient Germany. In the 1st century Pliny the Elder wrote that its feathers shine like fire at night, and in the 7th century Isidore of Seville said feathers laid on the ground give light to show the way. It appears in medieval bestiaries.

long_description.id: Laporan ini mungkin berasal dari burung berbulu warna-warni yang memantulkan cahaya bulan, seperti burung hantu serak. Legenda ini mengilhami puisi Thomas Moore A Dream of Antiquity.
long_description.en: The reports may come from iridescent birds reflecting moonlight, such as the barn owl. The legend inspired Thomas Moore's poem A Dream of Antiquity.

origin.en: Pliny the Elder and the bestiaries.

description.id: Hutan kuno tempat hercinia tinggal.
description.en: The ancient forest where the hercinia lived.

claims.quote: Hercinia is a legendary bird with glowing feathers that inhabited the Hercynian Forest of ancient Germany.

statement.id: Hercinia adalah burung legendaris berbulu bercahaya yang menghuni Hutan Hercynia di Germania kuno.
statement.en: The hercinia is a legendary bird with glowing feathers that lived in the Hercynian Forest of ancient Germany.

claims.quote: The hercinia is depicted in Medieval bestiaries and was recorded in the 1st century by Pliny the Elder, who wrote, "In the Hercynian Forest, in Germany, we hear of a singular kind of bird, the feathers of which shine at night like fire".

statement.id: Hercinia digambarkan dalam bestiari Abad Pertengahan dan dicatat pada abad ke-1 oleh Plinius Tua: "Di Hutan Hercynia, di Germania, terdengar kabar tentang sejenis burung aneh yang bulunya bersinar seperti api pada malam hari."
statement.en: The hercinia appears in Medieval bestiaries and was recorded in the 1st century by Pliny the Elder: 'In the Hercynian Forest, in Germany, we hear of a singular kind of bird, the feathers of which shine at night like fire.'

claims.quote: Writing in the 7th century, Isidore of Seville notes, "Their feathers sparkle so much in the shade that, however dark the night is with thick shadows, these feathers, when placed on the ground, give off light that helps to mark the way, and the sign of the glittering feathers makes clear the direction of the path".

statement.id: Pada abad ke-7 Isidorus dari Sevilla menulis bahwa bulunya begitu berkilau sehingga, segelap apa pun malam, bulu yang diletakkan di tanah memancarkan cahaya penunjuk jalan.
statement.en: Writing in the 7th century, Isidore of Seville notes that its feathers sparkle so that, however dark the night, feathers laid on the ground give off light that marks the path.

claims.quote: It is possible that the reports of the hercinia were based on sightings of birds with iridescent feathers that reflected moonlight, a phenomenon that has been reported of a number of species of birds, including the barn owl and the bittern.

statement.id: Laporan tentang hercinia mungkin berasal dari burung berbulu warna-warni yang memantulkan cahaya bulan, gejala yang dilaporkan pada beberapa spesies seperti burung hantu serak dan burung bittern.
statement.en: Reports of the hercinia may come from birds with iridescent feathers reflecting moonlight, as reported of several species including the barn owl and the bittern.

claims.quote: La légende de ces oiseaux lumineux présents dans la forêt Hercynienne a inspiré de nombreuses œuvres d’art, notamment le célèbre poème de Thomas Moore : A Dream of Antiquity.

statement.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Prancis, legenda burung bercahaya ini mengilhami banyak karya seni, termasuk puisi Thomas Moore A Dream of Antiquity.
statement.en: According to the French article, the legend inspired many works of art, notably Thomas Moore's poem A Dream of Antiquity.

claims.quote: Ellos se encontraban en el bosque Hercínico, en el sur de Alemania, donde sus plumas brillantes mantenían sendas encendidas en la espesura del bosque.

statement.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Spanyol, burung-burung ini tinggal di Hutan Hercynia di Jerman selatan, tempat bulu bercahayanya menerangi jalan setapak di hutan lebat.
statement.en: According to the Spanish article, they lived in the Hercynian Forest in southern Germany, where their glowing feathers lit the paths through the thick forest.

short_description.id: Herensuge adalah naga atau ular raksasa mitologi Basque, sering berkepala tujuh, yang tinggal di gua dan menuntut korban sampai dikalahkan Santo Mikael atau seorang pahlawan.
short_description.en: Herensuge is the dragon or giant serpent of Basque mythology, often seven-headed, that lives in caves and demands victims until Saint Michael or a hero defeats it.

long_description.id: Herensuge adalah naga mitologi Basque yang sering berwujud ular; namanya beragam tetapi selalu berakhiran suge, "ular". Ia kadang berkepala tujuh, yang dipercaya anak-anaknya sendiri, dan menurut sebagian sumber dapat terbang. Ia menghuni gua, gunung, dan jurang, menarik manusia dan hewan ke guanya dengan napasnya, dan meneror gembala.
long_description.en: Herensuge is the Basque dragon, often in serpent form; its names vary but always end in suge, 'snake'. It sometimes has seven heads, thought to be its own offspring, and some sources say it can fly. It lives in caves, mountains and chasms, draws people and animals into its lair with its breath, and terrorises shepherds.

long_description.id: Dalam legenda Aralar, ksatria Teodosio de Goñi yang sedang menebus dosa diselamatkan Santo Mikael, yang datang bersama Allah dan memenggal naga itu; kisah ini terkait biara San Miguel de Aralar dan peralihan ke agama Kristen. Dalam dongeng lain, seorang pangeran membunuh Herensuge berkepala tujuh dengan bantuan raksasa bermata satu Tartalo.
long_description.en: In the Aralar legend, the penitent knight Teodosio de Goñi is saved by Saint Michael, who comes with God and beheads the dragon; the tale is tied to the monastery of San Miguel de Aralar and the turn to Christianity. In another tale a prince kills the seven-headed Herensuge with the help of the one-eyed giant Tartalo.

who.id: Naga atau ular raksasa berkepala tujuh.

famous_for.en: Defeated by Saint Michael at Aralar.

role.en: The dragon beheaded by Saint Michael.

summary.id: Ksatria Teodosio de Goñi menyelamatkan perempuan tebusan naga di Aralar; ketika terdesak ia berdoa, dan Santo Mikael datang bersama Allah memenggal naga itu.
summary.en: The knight Teodosio de Goñi rescues the dragon's ransomed woman at Aralar; cornered, he prays, and Saint Michael comes with God and beheads the dragon.

description.id: Biara yang terkait legenda Teodosio.
description.en: The monastery tied to the Teodosio legend.

note.en: The god linked with it.
The giant who helps a prince kill it.

claims.quote: Herensuge is the name for a mythical dragon in the Basque language. In Basque mythology, dragons appear sparingly, sometimes with seven heads. Herensuge often also appear in the form of a serpent.

statement.id: Herensuge adalah nama naga mitis dalam bahasa Basque; dalam mitologi Basque naga jarang muncul, kadang berkepala tujuh, dan Herensuge sering juga berwujud ular.
statement.en: Herensuge is the Basque name for a mythical dragon; dragons appear rarely in Basque mythology, sometimes with seven heads, and Herensuge often also takes the form of a serpent.

claims.quote: The seven heads were believed to be the offspring of the Herensuge dragon. When the little dragons were fully grown, they would fall off their mother's head.

statement.id: Ketujuh kepala itu dipercaya anak-anak Herensuge; setelah dewasa, naga-naga kecil itu lepas dari kepala induknya.
statement.en: The seven heads were believed to be the Herensuge's offspring; when grown, the little dragons fell off their mother's head.

claims.quote: Only the god Sugaar is associated with this creature but more often with a serpent.

statement.id: Hanya dewa Sugaar yang dikaitkan dengan makhluk ini, meski lebih sering dengan ular.
statement.en: Only the god Sugaar is linked with this creature, though more often with a serpent.

claims.quote: ist in der Folklore des Baskenlands ein teuflischer Höhlengeist, der in der Gestalt einer Schlange erscheint. Der Überlieferung zufolge hat er sieben Köpfe und kann fliegen (die Quellen variieren in dieser Aussage).

statement.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Jerman, ia roh gua jahat yang muncul berwujud ular, berkepala tujuh, dan dapat terbang, meski sumber berbeda soal ini.
statement.en: According to the German article it is a devilish cave spirit appearing as a serpent, with seven heads and able to fly, though sources differ on this.

claims.quote: Mit seinem Atem lockt er Menschen und Tiere in seine Höhle, um sie zu verschlingen.

statement.id: Dengan napasnya ia menarik manusia dan hewan ke guanya untuk dilahap.
statement.en: With its breath it draws people and animals into its cave to devour them.

claims.quote: Herensuge habite cavernes, montagnes et gouffres, et ses attaques terrifient les bergers et troupeaux ; il est au centre de nombreux récits héroïques.

statement.id: Herensuge menghuni gua, gunung, dan jurang, serangannya menakutkan gembala dan ternak, dan ia menjadi pusat banyak kisah kepahlawanan.
statement.en: Herensuge lives in caves, mountains and chasms, its attacks terrify shepherds and flocks, and it is at the heart of many heroic tales.

claims.quote: Ses noms varient, mais la permanence du suffixe « suge » (couleuvre, serpent) suffit à justifier sa nature. C'est en effet un serpent.

statement.id: Namanya beragam, tetapi akhiran suge ("ular") yang selalu ada menunjukkan sifatnya sebagai ular.
statement.en: Its names vary, but the constant suffix suge ('snake') shows its serpent nature.

claims.quote: On trouve les noms de Erensugue, Erensuge, Iraunsuge, Lerensuge, Herainsuge, Errensuge, Hensuge, Edensugue, Edeinsuge, Edaansuge, Igensuge, Iraunsuge.

statement.id: Nama-nama lainnya antara lain Erensugue, Iraunsuge, Lerensuge, Herainsuge, Errensuge, Edensugue, dan Igensuge.
statement.en: Other names include Erensugue, Iraunsuge, Lerensuge, Herainsuge, Errensuge, Edensugue and Igensuge.

claims.quote: A legend describes a Navarrese knight, Teodosio de Goñi, who while making penance for double parricide in the Aralar Range rescues a woman that had been given as ransom to the dragon.

statement.id: Sebuah legenda menceritakan ksatria Navarra Teodosio de Goñi, yang saat menjalani penebusan dosa karena membunuh kedua orang tuanya di Pegunungan Aralar menyelamatkan seorang perempuan yang diserahkan sebagai tebusan kepada naga.
statement.en: A legend tells of the Navarrese knight Teodosio de Goñi who, doing penance in the Aralar range for killing both parents, rescues a woman given to the dragon as ransom.

claims.quote: the knight prays to Saint Michael to save him. In Heaven, the archangel is notified, but refuses to enter the fight without God. The archangel arrives with God over his head and decapitates the dragon, liberating Teodosio from his chains and ending his penance.

statement.id: Ksatria itu berdoa kepada Santo Mikael; sang malaikat agung menolak bertarung tanpa Allah, lalu datang dengan Allah di atas kepalanya, memenggal naga itu, dan membebaskan Teodosio dari rantai serta penebusannya.
statement.en: The knight prays to Saint Michael; the archangel refuses to fight without God, then arrives with God above his head, beheads the dragon and frees Teodosio from his chains and his penance.

claims.quote: This legend is associated to the monastery of San Miguel de Aralar. It has been interpreted as a way of justifying the break from the religion and customs of pagan Basques and the adoption of Christianity and, specifically, the veneration for St. Michael.

statement.id: Legenda ini terkait biara San Miguel de Aralar dan ditafsirkan sebagai pembenaran peralihan dari agama pagan Basque ke agama Kristen, khususnya pemujaan Santo Mikael.
statement.en: The legend is tied to the monastery of San Miguel de Aralar and has been read as justifying the shift from pagan Basque religion to Christianity, especially the cult of St Michael.

claims.quote: With the help of the Tartalo, the disguised prince, is able to kill the creature after three battles.

statement.id: Dalam kisah Tartalo yang berterima kasih, seorang pangeran yang menyamar membunuh Herensuge berkepala tujuh setelah tiga kali bertarung dengan bantuan Tartalo.
statement.en: In the tale of the Grateful Tartalo, a disguised prince kills the seven-headed Herensuge after three battles with the Tartalo's help.

short_description.id: Hiiden hirvi adalah rusa besar mitos dalam mitologi Finlandia yang harus diburu dengan ski; mitosnya menceritakan asal-usul ski dan rusa besar.
short_description.en: Hiiden hirvi is a mythical moose of Finnish mythology that must be hunted on skis; its myth tells the origin of skis and of the moose.

long_description.id: Hiiden hirvi, "rusa besar milik Hiisi", adalah rusa besar mitos dalam mitologi Finlandia yang harus diburu dengan bermain ski; mitosnya menceritakan penciptaan ski dan asal-usul rusa besar. Dalam epos Kalevala ia hewan gaib yang sulit ditangkap, cepat, dan kuat, dan Louhi menugaskan para pelamar putrinya menangkapnya hidup-hidup. Padanannya di Estonia adalah Hiiehobune, "kuda milik Hiis".
long_description.en: Hiiden hirvi, "Hiisi's moose", is a mythical moose of Finnish mythology that must be hunted on skis; its myth tells the creation of skis and the origin of the moose. In the Kalevala epic it is a supernatural animal, hard to catch, swift and strong, and Louhi sets her daughters' suitors the task of catching it alive. Its Estonian counterpart is Hiiehobune, "Hiis's horse".

long_description.id: Dalam versi Karelia Putih dan Olonets, sang tokoh tiba di tempat perempuan tertawa, anak-anak menangis, dan anjing menggonggong karena rusa itu baru lewat dan merusak makanan, lalu memburunya hingga skinya patah dan rusa itu lolos. Dalam versi Karelia Ladoga tokohnya biasanya seorang Sami bernama Lauri, dan dalam satu versi Väinämöinen berhasil memburunya.
long_description.en: In White Karelian and Olonets versions the hero reaches a place where women laugh, children cry and dogs bark because the moose has just passed and spoiled the food, then chases it until a ski breaks and it escapes. In Ladoga Karelian versions the hero is usually a Sámi named Lauri, and in one version Väinämöinen succeeds in the hunt.

who.id: Hiiden hirvi adalah rusa besar mitos.
who.en: Hiiden hirvi is a mythical moose.

role.en: It must be hunted on skis.

famous_for.en: Its myth explains the origin of skis.

did_you_know.id: Mitos Hiiden hirvi sekaligus menceritakan penciptaan ski.
did_you_know.en: The Hiiden hirvi myth also tells of the creation of skis.

summary.id: Seorang tokoh membuat ski dan memburu rusa besar yang merusak makanan; dalam sebagian versi rusa itu lolos karena ski patah, dalam versi lain Väinämöinen berhasil menangkapnya.
summary.en: A hero makes skis and hunts the moose that spoiled the food; in some versions it escapes when a ski breaks, in another Väinämöinen catches it.

note.en: Its Estonian counterpart.
Sets the suitors the task of catching it.

learning_questions.id: Mengapa mitos perburuan sering sekaligus menjelaskan asal-usul alat seperti ski?
learning_questions.en: Why do hunting myths often also explain the origin of tools like skis?

claims.quote: Hiiden hirvi (lit. 'Hiisi's moose') is a mythical moose in Finnish mythology which must be hunted by skiing. This myth describes the creation of skis and the origin of the moose.

statement.id: Hiiden hirvi ("rusa besar milik Hiisi") adalah rusa besar (moose) mitos dalam mitologi Finlandia yang harus diburu dengan bermain ski; mitos ini menceritakan penciptaan ski dan asal-usul rusa besar.
statement.en: Hiiden hirvi ("Hiisi's moose") is a mythical moose of Finnish mythology that must be hunted on skis; the myth describes the creation of skis and the origin of the moose.

claims.quote: The Estonian equivalent of Hiiden hirvi is Hiiehobune (lit. 'Hiis's horse').

statement.id: Padanan Estonia dari Hiiden hirvi adalah Hiiehobune ("kuda milik Hiis").
statement.en: The Estonian equivalent of Hiiden hirvi is Hiiehobune ("Hiis's horse").

claims.quote: The protagonist arrives at a location where women laugh, children cry and dogs bark. They tell the protagonist this is because Hiiden hirvi just passed through the area and ruined the food. The protagonist starts their chase of the moose but one of the skis break and the moose escapes.

statement.id: Dalam versi Karelia Putih dan Olonets, sang tokoh tiba di tempat perempuan tertawa, anak-anak menangis, dan anjing menggonggong, karena Hiiden hirvi baru saja lewat dan merusak makanan; ia mulai memburu rusa itu, tetapi salah satu skinya patah dan rusa itu lolos.
statement.en: In White Karelian and Olonets versions the hero reaches a place where women laugh, children cry and dogs bark, because Hiiden hirvi has just passed through and spoiled the food; the hero begins the chase, but one ski breaks and the moose escapes.

claims.quote: In Ladoga Karelian versions, the protagonist is usually "Lappalainen" (a Sámi person). He might be given the name Lauri. In one version, the protagonist is Väinämöinen and in this case, he succeeds in hunting the moose.

statement.id: Dalam versi Karelia Ladoga, tokohnya biasanya "Lappalainen" (orang Sami), kadang bernama Lauri; dalam satu versi tokohnya Väinämöinen, yang berhasil memburu rusa itu.
statement.en: In Ladoga Karelian versions the hero is usually "Lappalainen" (a Sámi person), sometimes named Lauri; in one version the hero is Väinämöinen, who succeeds in hunting the moose.

claims.quote: Hiie põder (ka hiie hirv; soome keeles hiiden hirvi) on üleloomulik loom soome eeposes "Kalevala". Seda looma on kirjeldatud kui raskesti püütavat, kiiret ja tugevat.

statement.id: Hiie põder (juga hiie hirv; bahasa Finlandia hiiden hirvi) adalah hewan gaib dalam epos Finlandia Kalevala, yang digambarkan sulit ditangkap, cepat, dan kuat.
statement.en: Hiie põder (also hiie hirv; Finnish hiiden hirvi) is a supernatural animal of the Finnish epic Kalevala, described as hard to catch, swift and strong.

claims.quote: Eeposes annab Louhi oma tütarde kosilastele ülesandeks püüda hiie põder kinni elavana.

statement.id: Dalam epos itu, Louhi memberi para pelamar putrinya tugas menangkap hiie põder hidup-hidup.
statement.en: In the epic, Louhi sets her daughters' suitors the task of catching the hiie põder alive.

short_description.id: Hircocervus atau tragelaphos adalah makhluk khayalan setengah kambing setengah rusa yang dipakai Platon dan Aristoteles sebagai contoh sesuatu yang dapat dibayangkan tetapi tidak ada.
short_description.en: The hircocervus or tragelaph is an imaginary half-goat, half-stag that Plato and Aristotle used as an example of something imaginable but non-existent.

long_description.id: Hircocervus, dari bahasa Latin hircus "kambing jantan" dan cervus "rusa jantan", atau tragelaphos dalam bahasa Yunani, adalah makhluk khayalan setengah kambing setengah rusa. Dalam Republik, Sokrates menyamakan pemikirannya dengan pelukis kambing-rusa, dan Aristoteles memakainya sebagai contoh hal yang dapat dijelaskan tetapi tidak ada; Boethius menerjemahkannya menjadi hircocervus. Diodorus Siculus justru menganggapnya hewan nyata.
long_description.en: The hircocervus, from Latin hircus 'billy goat' and cervus 'stag', or tragelaphos in Greek, is an imaginary half-goat, half-stag. In the Republic Socrates compares his thinking to painters of goat-stags, and Aristotle used it as an example of something describable yet non-existent; Boethius translated it as hircocervus. Diodorus Siculus, though, treated it as a real animal.

long_description.id: Kata ini masuk bahasa Inggris pada 1398, dipakai Martin Luther pada 1540 untuk hukum yang tidak menghukum, dan kemudian menjadi kiasan untuk hal yang mustahil. Buffon mengenali tragelaphos Plinius sebagai rusa tua bersurai panjang.
long_description.en: The word entered English in 1398, was used by Martin Luther in 1540 for a law that does not condemn, and later became a figure for anything absurd. Buffon identified Pliny's tragelaph as an old long-maned stag.

origin.id: Filsafat Yunani dan naskah abad pertengahan.

famous_for.en: Used by Aristotle.

description.id: Kata hircocervus pertama muncul dalam bahasa Inggris.
description.en: The word hircocervus first appears in English.

claims.quote: The hircocervus (Latin: hircus, "billy goat" + cervus, "stag") or tragelaph (Greek: τράγος, romanized: tragos, "billy goat" + έλαφος, elaphos, "stag"), also known as a goat-stag, was a legendary creature imagined to be half-goat, half-stag.

statement.id: Hircocervus (Latin: hircus, "kambing jantan" + cervus, "rusa jantan") atau tragelaphos (Yunani), juga disebut kambing-rusa, adalah makhluk legendaris yang dibayangkan setengah kambing setengah rusa.
statement.en: The hircocervus (Latin hircus, 'billy goat' + cervus, 'stag') or tragelaph (Greek), also called goat-stag, was a legendary creature imagined as half goat, half stag.

claims.quote: In Plato's Republic, Socrates speaks of his own image-making as similar to that of painters who paint goat-stags, combining the features of different things together (488a).

statement.id: Dalam Republik karya Platon, Sokrates menyamakan caranya membuat gambaran dengan pelukis yang melukis kambing-rusa, menggabungkan ciri berbagai hal (488a).
statement.en: In Plato's Republic, Socrates likens his image-making to painters who paint goat-stags by combining features of different things (488a).

claims.quote: In his work De Interpretatione, Aristotle utilized the idea of a fabulous goat-stag to express the philosophical concept of something that is describable even though it does not really exist. His Greek "τραγέλαφος" was rendered into Latin "hircocervus" by Boethius.

statement.id: Dalam De Interpretatione, Aristoteles memakai kambing-rusa dongeng untuk menjelaskan konsep sesuatu yang dapat dijelaskan walau tidak benar-benar ada; Boethius menerjemahkan kata Yunaninya menjadi hircocervus.
statement.en: In De Interpretatione Aristotle used the fabulous goat-stag to express something describable though non-existent; Boethius rendered his Greek word into Latin as hircocervus.

claims.quote: On the other hand, Diodorus Siculus treats the tragelaphos as an existing animal, and there are references in Greek literature to other hybrid creatures such as the hippelaphos (horse-stag).

statement.id: Sebaliknya, Diodorus Siculus memperlakukan tragelaphos sebagai hewan yang benar-benar ada, dan sastra Yunani juga menyebut hibrida lain seperti hippelaphos (kuda-rusa).
statement.en: Diodorus Siculus, by contrast, treats the tragelaphos as a real animal, and Greek literature mentions other hybrids such as the hippelaphos (horse-stag).

claims.quote: The word hircocervus first appears in the English language in a medieval manuscript dating from 1398 (now at the Bodleian Library).

statement.id: Kata hircocervus pertama muncul dalam bahasa Inggris pada naskah abad pertengahan tahun 1398 yang kini di Bodleian Library.
statement.en: The word hircocervus first appears in English in a medieval manuscript of 1398, now in the Bodleian Library.

claims.quote: Martin Luther uses the term "tragelaphus" in his Theses Against the Antinomians (1540, Sixth Set) to describe "a law that does not condemn".

statement.id: Martin Luther memakai istilah tragelaphus dalam Tesis Melawan Kaum Antinomian (1540) untuk menggambarkan "hukum yang tidak menghukum".
statement.en: Martin Luther used 'tragelaphus' in his Theses Against the Antinomians (1540) for 'a law that does not condemn'.

claims.quote: Quant à Pline, il parle d'un tragélaphe qui est sans doute le même animal. Buffon a reconnu sous ces deux noms un vieux cerf dont le cou finit par se couvrir de longs crins et le fait ressembler de loin à un cheval.

statement.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Prancis, Plinius menyebut tragelaphos yang mungkin hewan yang sama dengan hippelaphos Aristoteles, dan Buffon mengenalinya sebagai rusa tua yang lehernya tertutup surai panjang sehingga dari jauh mirip kuda.
statement.en: According to the French article, Pliny's tragelaph is probably the same as Aristotle's hippelaphos, and Buffon identified both as an old stag whose neck grows long hair so that from afar it looks like a horse.

claims.quote: Col tempo l'uso letterale del termine è stato abbandonato in favore di quello metaforico per riferirsi a cose assurde ed irreali.

statement.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Italia, lama-kelamaan istilah ini dipakai secara kiasan untuk hal yang mustahil dan tidak nyata.
statement.en: According to the Italian article, the term came to be used figuratively for absurd and unreal things.

summary.id: Contoh makhluk yang tidak ada (Aristoteles).
summary.en: An example of a non-existent creature (Aristotle).

summary.id: Hewan yang ada (Diodorus Siculus).
summary.en: A real animal (Diodorus Siculus).

short_description.id: Humbaba adalah tokoh mitologi Mesopotamia.
short_description.en: Humbaba is a figure in Mesopotamian mythology.

long_description.id: Humbaba adalah tokoh mitologi Mesopotamia. Humbaba digambarkan sebagai sosok mirip manusia yang dibandingkan dengan ogre atau raksasa.
long_description.en: Humbaba is a figure in Mesopotamian mythology. Humbaba is depicted as an anthropomorphic figure comparable to an ogre or giant.

long_description.id: Asal dan arti nama Humbaba tidak diketahui. Nama Humbaba pertama ditemukan sebagai nama pribadi dalam dokumen masa Ur III. Humbaba menjaga Hutan Aras dan dibunuh Gilgamesh serta Enkidu dalam eposnya. Humbaba digambarkan berbulu, bercakar singa, dan berwajah monster.
long_description.en: The origin and meaning of Humbaba’s name are unknown. Humbaba first occurs as a personal name in documents from the Ur III period. Humbaba guards the Cedar Forest and is killed by Gilgamesh and Enkidu in the epic. Humbaba is depicted as hairy, with lion’s claws and a monstrous face.

sources.title: The Mesopotamian Pantheon: The Ancient Gods and Goddesses of the Near East - World History Encyclopedia

short_description.id: Hydrus adalah ular air dari bestiari abad pertengahan yang menyusup ke mulut buaya yang tidur lalu merobek perutnya dari dalam, lambang Kristus yang keluar dari neraka.
short_description.en: The hydrus is a water snake of medieval bestiaries that slips into a sleeping crocodile's mouth and tears its belly from inside, an emblem of Christ breaking out of Hell.

long_description.id: Hydrus, juga disebut Enhydros atau Ydrus, adalah makhluk bestiari Abad Pertengahan yang biasanya dianggap ular air, tetapi juga digambarkan sebagai burung, naga, atau luwak. Menurut Aberdeen Bestiary namanya berasal dari kata Yunani untuk air karena ia hidup di Sungai Nil. Plinius Tua menyebut bisanya paling kuat di antara ular, dengan hati sebagai penawarnya, dan Thomas dari Cantimpré menyebut gigitannya menimbulkan "penyakit boa".
long_description.en: The hydrus, also called Enhydros or Ydrus, is a creature of Medieval bestiaries usually taken as a water snake but also shown as a bird, dragon or mongoose. The Aberdeen Bestiary derives its name from the Greek for water because it lives in the Nile. Pliny the Elder called its venom the strongest of any snake, its liver the cure, and Thomas of Cantimpré said its bite causes the 'boa sickness'.

long_description.id: Hydrus membenci buaya: ia berlumur lumpur, menyelinap ke mulut buaya yang tidur, lalu merobek perutnya dari dalam. Tradisi Kristen menjadikannya lambang Kristus yang turun ke dunia orang mati dan bangkit, seperti dalam Bestiaire de Gervaise. Ia kadang dicampuradukkan dengan Hydra dari mitos Yunani.
long_description.en: The hydrus hates crocodiles: it coats itself in mud, slips into a sleeping crocodile's mouth and rips open its belly from inside. Christian tradition made it a symbol of Christ descending to the dead and rising, as in the Bestiaire de Gervaise. It is sometimes confused with the Hydra of Greek myth.

famous_for.en: An emblem of Christ's resurrection.

description.id: Bisanya lebih kuat dari ular mana pun; hatinya menjadi penawar.
description.en: Its venom is stronger than any snake's; its liver is the antidote.

note.en: Sometimes confused with it.

claims.quote: The Hydrus (also known as Enhydros, Enidros, Hildris, Hydra, Hidri, Idra, Idres, Ydre, Ydris, and Ydrus) is a creature from Medieval bestiaries.

statement.id: Hydrus (juga Enhydros, Enidros, Hildris, Hydra, Hidri, Idra, Idres, Ydre, Ydris, dan Ydrus) adalah makhluk dari bestiari Abad Pertengahan.
statement.en: The Hydrus (also Enhydros, Enidros, Hildris, Hydra, Hidri, Idra, Idres, Ydre, Ydris and Ydrus) is a creature of Medieval bestiaries.

claims.quote: A hydrus has no set appearance. Normally it is considered to be a water snake. Other animals the hydrus has been thought of as include a bird, a dragon, and a mongoose.

statement.id: Wujud hydrus tidak tetap; biasanya ia dianggap ular air, tetapi juga digambarkan sebagai burung, naga, atau luwak.
statement.en: The hydrus has no fixed look; it is usually taken to be a water snake, but also shown as a bird, a dragon or a mongoose.

claims.quote: Pliny the Elder described the hydrus as a amphibious serpent with stronger venom than any other snake. He also says that the hydrus' liver can be used as an antidote to its bite.

statement.id: Plinius Tua menggambarkan hydrus sebagai ular amfibi dengan bisa lebih kuat dari ular mana pun, dan hatinya dapat dipakai sebagai penawar gigitannya.
statement.en: Pliny the Elder described the hydrus as an amphibious serpent with venom stronger than any other snake's, whose liver can serve as an antidote to its bite.

claims.quote: They were said to be found in the Nile River. It is said that the hydrus hated crocodiles, and would intentionally roll in the mud and seek out a crocodile while it slept with its mouth open.

statement.id: Hydrus konon hidup di Sungai Nil dan membenci buaya; ia sengaja berguling di lumpur lalu mencari buaya yang tidur dengan mulut terbuka.
statement.en: They were said to live in the Nile and to hate crocodiles; the hydrus would roll in mud on purpose and seek out a crocodile sleeping with its mouth open.

claims.quote: Once inside the crocodile's stomach, the hydrus would burst free from the stomach lining, ripping out the crocodile's entrails and leaving it to die. In medieval Christian tradition, this bursting free from the crocodile became an emblem of the resurrection of Christ bursting free from Hell.

statement.id: Di dalam perut buaya, hydrus merobek dinding perut dan isi perut buaya itu hingga mati; dalam tradisi Kristen abad pertengahan, hal ini menjadi lambang kebangkitan Kristus yang keluar dari neraka.
statement.en: Inside the crocodile's stomach the hydrus tears free through the lining and entrails, leaving it to die; in medieval Christian tradition this became an emblem of Christ's resurrection breaking out of Hell.

claims.quote: Selon Thomas de Cantimpré, au XIIIe siècle, la morsure cause un effet de sidération, nommée la "maladie du boa".
