short_description.id: Sântoaderi adalah sekelompok makhluk gaib cerita rakyat Rumania berwujud pemuda berkuku kuda yang datang ke desa dengan nyanyian dan genderang, membawa penyakit dan menculik orang yang berada di luar rumah.
short_description.en: The Sântoaderi are a group of supernatural beings of Romanian folklore, hoofed young men who come to villages with song and drums, bringing illness and abducting anyone caught outdoors.

long_description.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Rumania, Sântoaderi adalah rombongan tujuh atau sembilan pemuda berkaki panjang dan berkuku kuda yang mengenakan jubah. Mereka datang secara misterius ke desa, bernyanyi dan menabuh genderang, lalu membuat orang sakit dengan membelitnya dengan rantai hingga terkena rematik atau menginjak-injak tubuhnya.
long_description.en: In Romanian folklore the Sântoaderi are a band of seven or nine long-footed, hoofed young men wearing capes. They arrive mysteriously in a village, singing and beating drums, and make people ill by wrapping them in chains, causing rheumatism, or by stamping on their bodies.

long_description.id: Orang yang mendengar musik dan derap kuku mereka dianjurkan tetap di dalam rumah, karena di sana mereka aman. Orang yang tertinggal di luar bisa diculik dan dibawa ikut arak-arakan; sebagian kembali sehat dengan membawa hadiah, sebagian lagi kembali sakit, sekarat, atau gila.
long_description.en: People who heard their music and hoofbeats were advised to stay indoors, where they were safe. Anyone left outside could be abducted into the procession; some returned healthy with gifts, others sick, dying or insane.

long_description.id: Namanya berasal dari sebutan daerah untuk Santo Theodorus, dan mereka dipercaya lebih sering muncul pada hari rayanya. Mircea Eliade membandingkan Sântoaderi dengan zâne, yang juga berkelana pada malam hari dalam arak-arakan penari, dan konon pada hari ke-24 setelah Paskah kedua kelompok itu bertemu untuk bermain dan bertukar karangan bunga.
long_description.en: Their name derives from a regional name for Saint Theodore, and they were thought most likely to appear on his feast day. Mircea Eliade compared the Sântoaderi with the zâne, who also travel by night in a procession of dancers, and on the 24th day after Easter the two groups are said to meet to play and exchange bouquets.

literal_meaning.id: Dari sebutan daerah untuk Santo Theodorus
literal_meaning.en: From a regional name for Saint Theodore

who.id: Sântoaderi adalah rombongan pemuda gaib berkuku kuda.
who.en: The Sântoaderi are a band of supernatural hoofed young men.

origin.id: Mereka berasal dari cerita rakyat Rumania.

role.id: Mereka datang ke desa membawa penyakit dan menculik orang yang berada di luar rumah.
role.en: They come to villages bringing illness and abducting people caught outdoors.

famous_for.id: Mereka dikenal lewat musik genderang dan derap kuku yang menandai kedatangannya.
famous_for.en: They are known for the drumming and hoofbeats that announce their arrival.

did_you_know.id: Nama Sântoaderi berasal dari sebutan daerah untuk Santo Theodorus, dan mereka paling mungkin muncul pada hari rayanya.
did_you_know.en: The name Sântoaderi comes from a regional name for Saint Theodore, and they were most likely to appear on his feast day.

description.id: Berlindung di dalam rumah ketika terdengar musik dan derap kuku mereka dianggap aman.
description.en: Sheltering indoors when their music and hoofbeats are heard was considered safe.

note.id: Mircea Eliade mencatat kemiripan keduanya; konon mereka bertemu pada hari ke-24 setelah Paskah.
note.en: Mircea Eliade noted their resemblance; they are said to meet on the 24th day after Easter.

learning_questions.id: Mengapa rumah dianggap tempat aman dari makhluk gaib dalam banyak cerita rakyat?
learning_questions.en: Why is the home considered a place of safety from supernatural beings in many folk traditions?

claims.quote: The Sântoaderi were a group of supernatural entities found in Romanian folklore. Viewed as either seven or nine young men with long feet and hooves, they were also thought of as wearing capes.

statement.id: Sântoaderi adalah sekelompok makhluk gaib dalam cerita rakyat Rumania, dibayangkan sebagai tujuh atau sembilan pemuda berkaki panjang dan berkuku kuda (hooves), yang juga dianggap mengenakan jubah.
statement.en: The Sântoaderi were a group of supernatural beings of Romanian folklore, pictured as seven or nine young men with long feet and hooves, also thought to wear capes.

claims.quote: It was believed that they would mysteriously appear in a village, where they would sing, beat their drums, and cause illness for people; wrapping them up in chains causing rheumatism or stamping on their bodies.

statement.id: Diyakini mereka muncul secara misterius di sebuah desa, bernyanyi, menabuh genderang, dan membuat orang sakit: membelit mereka dengan rantai sehingga terkena rematik, atau menginjak-injak tubuh mereka.
statement.en: They were believed to appear mysteriously in a village, singing and beating drums, and to cause illness: wrapping people in chains, causing rheumatism, or stamping on their bodies.

claims.quote: Upon hearing their music and the sound of hooves, people were advised to stay indoors, which was considered safe. Those that did not retreat indoors, could be kidnapped by the Sântoaderi and made part of the procession.

statement.id: Begitu mendengar musik dan derap kuku mereka, orang dianjurkan tetap di dalam rumah, yang dianggap aman; yang tidak masuk rumah bisa diculik Sântoaderi dan dijadikan bagian dari arak-arakan mereka.
statement.en: On hearing their music and hoofbeats, people were advised to stay indoors, which was thought safe; those who did not could be kidnapped by the Sântoaderi and made part of their procession.

claims.quote: The victims of such kidnappings would sometimes return in healthy condition and carrying gifts; other times, they would return sick, dying, or insane.

statement.id: Korban penculikan itu kadang kembali dalam keadaan sehat sambil membawa hadiah, kadang kembali dalam keadaan sakit, sekarat, atau gila.
statement.en: Victims of such kidnappings sometimes came back healthy and carrying gifts, and at other times sick, dying or insane.

claims.quote: The name "Sântoader" derives from a regional name for Saint Theodore, with folklore suggesting that the creatures were more likely to appear on his feast day.

statement.id: Nama "Sântoader" berasal dari sebutan daerah untuk Santo Theodorus, dan menurut cerita rakyat makhluk ini lebih mungkin muncul pada hari rayanya.
statement.en: The name "Sântoader" derives from a regional name for Saint Theodore, and folklore holds that the creatures were more likely to appear on his feast day.

claims.quote: The Sântoaderi share some similarities with the fairies of Irish folklore. The Romanian historian Mircea Eliade also noted a similarity between the Sântoaderi and the zîne, the Romanian equivalent of the fairy godmother

statement.id: Sântoaderi memiliki beberapa kemiripan dengan peri dalam cerita rakyat Irlandia; sejarawan Rumania Mircea Eliade juga mencatat kemiripan antara Sântoaderi dan zîne, padanan Rumania untuk ibu peri.
statement.en: The Sântoaderi share some similarities with the fairies of Irish folklore; the Romanian historian Mircea Eliade also noted a resemblance between the Sântoaderi and the zîne, the Romanian equivalent of the fairy godmother.

claims.quote: Sântoaderii sunt un grup de entități supranaturale din folclorul românesc.

statement.id: Artikel Rumania menyebut Sântoaderi sebagai sekelompok entitas gaib dalam folklor Rumania.
statement.en: The Romanian article describes the Sântoaderi as a group of supernatural entities in Romanian folklore.

claims.quote: Există, de asemenea, credința că în a 24-a zi după Paște, zânele și Sântoaderii se întâlnesc pentru a se juca și a-și oferi buchete de flori.

statement.id: Ada pula kepercayaan bahwa pada hari ke-24 setelah Paskah (a 24-a zi după Paște), zânele și Sântoaderii, yaitu para zâne dan Sântoaderi, bertemu untuk bermain dan saling memberi karangan bunga.
statement.en: There is also a belief that on the 24th day after Easter (a 24-a zi după Paște) the zânele și Sântoaderii, that is the zâne and the Sântoaderi, meet to play and give each other bouquets of flowers.

claims.quote: Istoricul român al religiilor Mircea Eliade a remarcat o asemănare între Sântoaderi și zâne, despre care se credea că, de asemenea, călătoresc noaptea într-un cortegiu de dansatoare.

statement.id: Sejarawan agama Rumania Mircea Eliade mencatat kemiripan antara Sântoaderi dan zâne, yang juga dipercaya berkelana pada malam hari dalam arak-arakan penari.
statement.en: The Romanian historian of religions Mircea Eliade noted a resemblance between the Sântoaderi and the zâne, who were also believed to travel by night in a procession of dancers.

short_description.id: Sárkány ("naga") adalah monster legendaris dalam mitologi Hungaria, biasanya berupa makhluk reptil bersisik dan bersayap, yang dikaitkan dengan badai, hujan es, dan harta.
short_description.en: The sárkány ("dragon") is a legendary monster of Hungarian mythology, usually a scaly, winged reptile, linked with storms, hail and treasure.

long_description.id: Sárkány, "naga", adalah monster legendaris dalam mitologi Hungaria. Ia biasanya tampil sebagai binatang reptil bersisik dan bersayap, tetapi kadang merupakan campuran makhluk lain. Dalam kebudayaan Hungaria ia juga digambarkan sebagai monster ilahi purba dan penjaga harta.
long_description.en: The sárkány, "dragon", is a legendary monster of Hungarian myth. It usually takes the form of a scaly, winged reptile, though at times it blends features of other beings. Hungarian tradition also casts it as an ancient divine monster and a keeper of treasure.

long_description.id: Menurut Magyar néprajzi lexikon, kepercayaan rakyat mengenal tarajos kígyó, "ular berjengger", ular menakutkan berkekuatan gaib yang bersayap, bagian depannya mirip kuda dan belakangnya mirip ular, bersisik keras, berkuku dan bergigi panjang, berjengger menyala, meniup percikan dan memuntahkan api. Sárkány juga kuda tunggangan garabonciás dan berhubungan dengan badai, hujan es, dan harta; ia lahir dari ikan atau ular yang tujuh tahun tersembunyi dari pandangan manusia di rawa atau tebing batu.
long_description.en: According to the Hungarian ethnographic lexicon, folk belief knows the tarajos kígyó, the "crested serpent", a dreadful, supernaturally strong winged snake, horse-like in front and serpent-like behind, hard-scaled, long-clawed and long-toothed, with a flaming crest, blowing sparks and spewing flame. The sárkány is also the steed of the garabonciás and is tied to storms, hail and treasure; it grows from a fish or snake hidden from human eyes for seven years in a marsh or rock cleft.

long_description.id: Kata sárkány dianggap serapan dari bahasa Turkik Oghur šaragan, "naga", dan mungkin berakar sama dengan kata Hungaria sárga, "kuning". Badai petir yang merusak sering dikaitkan dengan kemunculan naga, dan gemuruh guntur dianggap amukan naga di langit.
long_description.en: The word sárkány is thought to be borrowed from Oghuric Turkic šaragan, "dragon", and may share a root with Hungarian sárga, "yellow". Destructive thunderstorms were often linked with dragons, the thunder being the dragons raging in the sky.

short_description.id: Sazakan adalah roh badai dalam mitologi Turkik dan Altai, berwujud naga atau burung pemangsa, yang membawa hujan, hujan es, dan angin puting beliung.
short_description.en: Sazakan is a storm spirit of Turkic and Altai mythology, shaped like a dragon or bird of prey, that brings rain, hail and whirlwinds.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Turkik, Sazakan adalah naga, elang, alap-alap, atau kurcaci api yang menjelma angin puting beliung dan menimbulkan badai; sumber lain menyebutnya jin badai bertubuh besar mirip naga dengan tanduk bercabang. Ia membawa hujan dan hujan es: kadang hujan yang menyuburkan ladang, kadang kekeringan, hujan deras, atau hujan es, dan ia menguasai angin untuk memperkuat badai.
long_description.en: Turkic myth pictures the Sazakan as a dragon, hawk, falcon or fiery dwarf that whirls itself into a storm-wind; another source calls it a huge, dragon-like storm jinn with branching horns. It brings rain and hail: sometimes rain that helps the fields, sometimes drought, downpours or hail, and it commands the wind to strengthen storms.

long_description.id: Sazakan tinggal di bukit, gunung, belantara, dan kadang di awan, dan dalam cerita rakyat Nogai menjadi pelindung awan. Bila badai salju atau hujan deras datang tiba-tiba, orang berkata "Sazakan sedang bermain".
long_description.en: Sazakans live on hills and mountains, in the wilderness and sometimes in the clouds, and in Nogai folklore are patrons of the clouds. When a sudden snowstorm or downpour strikes, people say "Sazakan is playing".

short_description.id: Scitalis adalah ular bestiari abad pertengahan yang corak punggungnya memukau mangsa dan tubuhnya begitu panas sehingga berganti kulit di musim dingin.
short_description.en: The Scitalis is a serpent of medieval bestiaries whose dazzling back markings stun its prey and whose body is so hot it sheds its skin in winter.

long_description.id: Scitalis atau Scytale adalah ular dalam bestiari abad pertengahan seperti Aberdeen Bestiary. Corak punggungnya begitu indah sehingga orang yang melihatnya terpana dan melambat; karena merayap pelan dan tak dapat mengejar mangsa, ia memakai penampilannya untuk memikat. Tubuhnya begitu panas sehingga ia berganti kulit bahkan di musim dingin, seperti sudah ditulis Lucanus dalam Pharsalia.
long_description.en: The Scitalis or Scytale is a serpent of medieval bestiaries such as the Aberdeen Bestiary. Its back markings are so beautiful that viewers are stunned and slowed; since it creeps slowly and cannot chase prey, it uses its looks to ensnare. Its body is so hot it sheds its skin even in winter, as Lucan already wrote in the Pharsalia.

long_description.id: Namanya mungkin berasal dari kata Latin scitus, "indah". Ia juga muncul di portal gereja dalam novel Il nome della rosa karya Umberto Eco.
long_description.en: Its name probably comes from Latin scitus, 'beautiful'. It also appears on the church portal in Umberto Eco's novel Il nome della rosa.

famous_for.en: Its dazzling markings.

description.id: Scitale muncul di antara hewan pada portal gereja.
description.en: The scitale appears among the animals on the church portal.

claims.quote: The Scitalis or Scytale is a serpent from Medieval bestiaries, such as the Aberdeen Bestiary, supposed to have such marvelous markings on its back that its appearance would stun the viewer, slowing the person down so that they could be caught.

statement.id: Scitalis atau Scytale adalah ular dalam bestiari abad pertengahan seperti Aberdeen Bestiary, yang punggungnya bercorak begitu indah sehingga orang yang melihatnya terpana dan melambat hingga dapat ditangkap.
statement.en: The Scitalis or Scytale is a serpent of medieval bestiaries such as the Aberdeen Bestiary, whose back markings were so marvellous that viewers were stunned and slowed down enough to be caught.

claims.quote: Its bodily heat was so great that it shed its skin even in the winter.

statement.id: Tubuhnya begitu panas sehingga ia berganti kulit bahkan pada musim dingin.
statement.en: Its body heat was so great that it shed its skin even in winter.

claims.quote: Lucan wrote in the 1st century AD, in his Pharsalia, book 9, verse 841-842, that "Sole of all serpents Scytale to shed / In vernal frosts his slough...".

statement.id: Lucanus pada abad ke-1 M menulis dalam Pharsalia buku 9, baris 841-842, bahwa Scytale satu-satunya ular yang berganti kulit di tengah embun beku musim semi.
statement.en: Lucan wrote in the 1st century AD, in Pharsalia book 9, lines 841-842, that the Scytale alone of all serpents sheds its slough in the spring frosts.

claims.quote: It creeps slowly and cannot pursue its prey, so it stupifies with its marvelous appearance.

statement.id: Menurut Isidorus dari Sevilla, ia merayap pelan dan tak dapat mengejar mangsa, sehingga melumpuhkannya dengan penampilannya yang menakjubkan.
statement.en: According to Isidore of Seville it creeps slowly and cannot chase its prey, so it stupefies it with its marvellous appearance.

statement.en: Its name (Latin scitalis or scytale) probably comes from scitus, 'graceful, beautiful'.

statement.id: Scitale termasuk hewan nyata dan legendaris yang menghiasi bingkai portal gereja dalam novel Il nome della rosa karya Umberto Eco.
statement.en: The scitale is among the real and legendary animals framing the church portal in Umberto Eco's novel Il nome della rosa.

short_description.id: Biarawan laut adalah makhluk laut mirip biarawan berjubah yang konon ditangkap dekat Zealand, Denmark, pada 1546 dan tercatat dalam buku sejarah alam Belon, Rondelet, dan Gesner.
short_description.en: The sea monk is a sea creature resembling a monk in his habit, supposedly caught off Zealand, Denmark, in 1546 and recorded in the natural histories of Belon, Rondelet and Gesner.

long_description.id: Biarawan laut adalah "ikan" yang dari luar mirip biarawan berjubah, konon ditangkap dekat Zealand, Denmark, sekitar 1546; Christian III mengirim gambarnya kepada Kaisar Charles V, dan panjangnya dicatat 4 ell. Belon, Rondelet, dan Gesner memasukkannya ke dalam buku sejarah alam; Rondelet menggolongkannya manusia laut tetapi meragukan gambarnya.
long_description.en: The sea monk is a 'fish' outwardly like a monk in his habit, supposedly caught off Zealand, Denmark, around 1546; Christian III sent its picture to Emperor Charles V, and it was recorded as 4 ells long. Belon, Rondelet and Gesner put it in their natural histories; Rondelet classed it as a merman but doubted the pictures.

long_description.id: Artikel bahasa Jerman menyebut biarawan laut sudah disebut Alexander Neckam sekitar 1200, dan Gesner juga mencatat makhluk serupa di Firth of Forth dan Polandia. Japetus Steenstrup menafsirkannya sebagai cumi-cumi, sedangkan tafsiran lain menyebut ikan sungut ganda atau anjing laut.
long_description.en: The German article says the sea monk was already mentioned by Alexander Neckam around 1200, and Gesner also recorded similar creatures in the Firth of Forth and Poland. Japetus Steenstrup read it as a squid, while others suggest anglerfish or seals.

famous_for.id: Gambar yang dikirim kepada Charles V.
famous_for.en: The picture sent to Charles V.

description.id: Biarawan laut konon ditangkap dekat Zealand.
description.en: The sea monk is supposedly caught off Zealand.

claims.quote: The sea monk (also monk-fish or monkfish) was a sea creature found off the eastern coast of the Danish island of Zealand in 1546. It was described as a "fish" that outwardly resembled a human monk in his habit.

statement.id: Biarawan laut adalah makhluk laut yang ditemukan di lepas pantai timur pulau Zealand, Denmark, pada 1546, digambarkan sebagai "ikan" yang dari luar mirip biarawan berjubah.
statement.en: The sea monk was a sea creature found off the east coast of the Danish island of Zealand in 1546, described as a 'fish' outwardly like a monk in his habit.

claims.quote: The creature was called "monk fish" (Latin: piscis monachus) by Belon (1553), and piscis monachi habitu ("fish [wearing] the habit of a monk") by Rondelet (1554).

statement.id: Belon (1553) menyebutnya piscis monachus, "ikan biarawan", dan Rondelet (1554) piscis monachi habitu, "ikan berjubah biarawan".
statement.en: Belon (1553) called it piscis monachus, 'monk fish', and Rondelet (1554) piscis monachi habitu, 'fish in a monk's habit'.

claims.quote: Christian III of Denmark sent an illustration of it to Charles V, Holy Roman Emperor. The creature is recorded in Vedel's Den danske Krønicke (1575) as measuring 4 ells long (15 ft; 4.6 m).

statement.id: Christian III dari Denmark mengirim gambarnya kepada Kaisar Charles V, dan Den danske Krønicke karya Vedel (1575) mencatat panjangnya 4 ell (4,6 m).
statement.en: Christian III of Denmark sent a picture of it to Emperor Charles V, and Vedel's Den danske Krønicke (1575) records it as 4 ells (4.6 m) long.

claims.quote: Rondelet (1554) called it "the fish with the habit of a monk (piscis monachi habitu), and classed it as a merman (homo maris). But he did not think the pictorial representations he obtained could be taken at face value

statement.id: Rondelet menggolongkannya sebagai manusia laut (homo maris), tetapi meragukan bahwa gambar yang ia terima bisa dipercaya begitu saja.
statement.en: Rondelet classed it as a merman (homo maris) but doubted that the pictures he received could be taken at face value.

claims.quote: Erstmals erwähnt wird er um 1200 bei Alexander Neckam. In der Folge wurden verschiedene Sichtungen des Meermönches dokumentiert, unter anderem soll um 1550 ein Exemplar dem König von Dänemark zugeschickt worden sein.

statement.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Jerman, biarawan laut pertama disebut sekitar 1200 oleh Alexander Neckam, dan berbagai penampakan kemudian dicatat, termasuk spesimen yang dikirim kepada Raja Denmark sekitar 1550.
statement.en: According to the German article, the sea monk was first mentioned around 1200 by Alexander Neckam, and later sightings were recorded, including a specimen sent to the King of Denmark around 1550.

claims.quote: Japetus Steenstrup interpretierte ihn 1855 als Tintenfisch, neuere Deutungen gehen zum Beispiel von Seeteufeln, Meerengeln oder Robben aus.

statement.id: Japetus Steenstrup pada 1855 menafsirkannya sebagai cumi-cumi, sedangkan tafsiran baru mengusulkan ikan sungut ganda, hiu malaikat, atau anjing laut.
statement.en: Japetus Steenstrup in 1855 read it as a squid, while newer readings suggest anglerfish, angelsharks or seals.

claims.quote: Éste también hizo referencia a un monstruo similar encontrado en el Fiordo de Forth, citando al historiador escocés Hector Boece, y a un avistamiento en la costa de Polonia en 1531.

statement.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Spanyol, Gesner juga menyebut monster serupa di Firth of Forth menurut sejarawan Skotlandia Hector Boece, serta penampakan di pantai Polandia pada 1531.
statement.en: According to the Spanish article, Gesner also cited a similar monster in the Firth of Forth from the Scottish historian Hector Boece, and a sighting off Poland in 1531.

short_description.id: Shellycoat adalah roh air jahil dalam folklor Skotlandia dan Inggris Utara yang menghantui sungai dan aliran air, berselimut cangkang.
short_description.en: A shellycoat is a prankster water spirit of Scottish and Northern English folklore that haunts rivers and streams, covered in shells.

long_description.id: Dalam folklor Skotlandia dan Inggris Utara, shellycoat (juga spellycoat) adalah roh air jahil yang menghantui sungai dan aliran air, terutama di pesisir timur Skotlandia. Tubuhnya berbulu panjang dan berkaki selaput; bulunya tertutup cangkang dan sampah laut yang berderak saat ia bergerak. Ia relatif tak berbahaya dibanding kelpie: ia menyesatkan pengembara tanpa niat jahat, sering berteriak seperti orang tenggelam lalu tertawa seperti kuda.
long_description.en: In Scottish and Northern English folklore the shellycoat (also spellycoat) is a mischievous water spirit haunting rivers and streams, mostly on Scotland's east coast. It has long hair over its whole body and webbed feet, the hair hung with shells and sea debris that clatter as it moves. Compared with the kelpie it is fairly harmless: it leads wanderers astray without malice, often crying out as if drowning and then laughing like a horse.

long_description.id: Shellycoat konon tak dapat menyeberangi air mengalir dan membiarkan perempuan yang membawa anak. Shellycoat dari Leith digambarkan roh jahat besar yang dapat terbang, menyembunyikan mantel cangkangnya di bawah batu; seorang bernama English Dick yang menantangnya ditemukan dengan kaki patah. Batunya hancur saat pembangunan dermaga awal 1900-an. Jacob Grimm dalam Deutsche Mythologie menyamakannya dengan Schellenrock Jerman, "mantel lonceng".
long_description.en: It is believed unable to cross running water and to leave women with children alone. The shellycoat of Leith was described as a large, evil spirit able to fly, hiding its magic coat of shells under a rock; a man called English Dick who challenged it was found with broken legs. Its rock was destroyed in dock building in the early 1900s. Jacob Grimm in his Deutsche Mythologie equated it with the German Schellenrock, 'bell-coat'.

famous_for.en: Shellycoat of Leith.

did_you_know.id: Cangkang pada bulu shellycoat berderak saat ia bergerak, sehingga kehadirannya terdengar.
did_you_know.en: The shells on a shellycoat's hair clatter as it moves, betraying its presence.

short_description.id: Shtriga adalah penyihir vampir dalam mitologi Albania yang mengisap darah bayi saat malam lalu berubah menjadi serangga terbang.
short_description.en: The shtriga is a vampiric witch of Albanian mythology who sucks the blood of infants at night and then turns into a flying insect.

long_description.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Albania, shtriga adalah penyihir vampir yang malam-malam mengisap darah bayi yang sedang tidur, lalu menjelma serangga terbang, biasanya ngengat, lalat, atau lebah. Hanya shtriga itu sendiri yang dapat menyembuhkan korbannya, sering dengan meludah ke mulut mereka; yang tidak disembuhkan akan sakit lalu mati.
long_description.en: In Albanian folklore the shtriga is a vampire witch who drinks the blood of sleeping babies by night and then becomes a flying insect, usually a moth, fly or bee. Only the shtriga herself can heal her victims, often by spitting into their mouths; those left uncured fall ill and die.

long_description.id: Ia sering digambarkan sebagai perempuan bertatapan penuh benci, kadang berjubah, dengan wajah rusak mengerikan, tinggal di tempat tersembunyi di hutan dan punya kekuatan gaib. Kata shtriga juga berarti "penyihir" secara umum; bentuk laki-lakinya shtrigu atau shtrigan. Menurut cerita rakyat Albania utara, perempuan tidak lahir sebagai penyihir, melainkan menjadi penyihir, sering karena tidak punya anak atau karena iri hati.
long_description.en: She is often pictured as a woman with a hate-filled gaze, sometimes caped, with a dreadfully disfigured face, hiding in the forest and wielding supernatural powers. The word also means "witch" in general; the male form is shtrigu or shtrigan. Northern Albanian folklore holds that a woman is not born a witch but becomes one, often through childlessness or envy.

long_description.id: Kata shtrigë berasal dari bahasa Latin strīga, "roh jahat, penyihir", yang berkerabat dengan strega dalam bahasa Italia dan strzyga dalam bahasa Polandia.
long_description.en: The word shtrigë comes from Latin strīga, "evil spirit, witch", akin to Italian strega and Polish strzyga.

short_description.id: Sihuanaba adalah roh pengubah wujud dalam cerita rakyat Amerika Tengah yang tampil sebagai perempuan cantik berambut panjang, lalu menampakkan wajah tengkorak atau kepala kuda.
short_description.en: The Sihuanaba is a shapeshifting spirit of Central American folklore that appears as a beautiful long-haired woman, then reveals a skull or horse face.

long_description.id: Sihuanaba, juga disebut Siguanaba, Cigua, atau Cegua, adalah roh pengubah wujud dalam cerita rakyat Amerika Tengah, dengan varian di sebagian Meksiko. Ia tampil sebagai perempuan menarik berambut panjang yang sering terlihat mencuci atau mandi di sungai. Ia memikat pria yang sendirian ke tempat terpencil, lalu menampakkan wajah aslinya, tengkorak tanpa daging atau kepala kuda, yang membuat korban mati ketakutan atau menjadi gila.
long_description.en: The Sihuanaba, also called Siguanaba, Cigua or Cegua, is a shapeshifting spirit of Central American folklore with variants in parts of Mexico. She appears as an attractive long-haired woman, often seen washing or bathing in rivers. She lures lone men to remote places, then reveals her true face, a fleshless skull or a horse's head, which makes victims die of fright or go mad.

long_description.id: Para ahli menduga legenda ini berasal dari Spanyol dan dibawa ke Amerika Latin pada masa kolonial, ketika penjajah memakainya sebagai alat kendali sosial atas penduduk pribumi dan mestizo.
long_description.en: Scholars suggest the legend came from Spain in the colonial period, when colonists used it as a tool of social control over Indigenous and mestizo people.

short_description.id: Sirin adalah makhluk legenda dalam cerita rakyat Rusia, berkepala perempuan cantik dan bertubuh burung, yang nyanyiannya bisa membuat orang melupakan segalanya.
short_description.en: The Sirin is a legendary creature of Russian folklore with a beautiful woman's head and a bird's body, whose song can make people forget everything.

long_description.id: Sirin adalah makhluk legenda dari cerita rakyat Rusia. Ia berkepala perempuan cantik dan bertubuh burung, biasanya burung hantu, dan sering disamakan dengan siren dalam mitologi Yunani. Menurut mitos, Sirin tinggal di Iriy atau di sekitar Sungai Efrat. Satu sumber menyebut legendanya mungkin berasal dari Persia.
long_description.en: The Sirin is a legendary creature of Russian folklore. She is pictured as a bird, usually an owl, bearing a lovely woman's head, and is often equated with the sirens of Greek mythology. Myth places her home in Iriy or near the Euphrates River. One source suggests her legend may be of Persian origin.

long_description.id: Berbeda dari siren yang memikat pelaut menuju maut, Sirin memakai suaranya untuk mengganjar orang saleh. Ia menyanyikan lagu indah bagi para santo dan meramalkan kebahagiaan yang akan datang. Namun bagi manusia biasa ia berbahaya: laki-laki yang mendengarnya melupakan segala hal duniawi, mengikutinya, dan akhirnya mati. Orang berusaha mengusirnya dengan tembakan meriam, dentang lonceng, dan bunyi keras lainnya.
long_description.en: Unlike the sirens who lure sailors to death, the Sirin uses her voice to reward the virtuous. She sang lovely songs to the saints, foretelling joys to come. To ordinary mortals, however, she was dangerous: men who heard her forgot everything earthly, followed her and finally died. People tried to drive her off with cannon fire, ringing bells and other loud noises.

long_description.id: Sumber berbeda pendapat tentang sifatnya. Satu sumber menyebut Sirin burung kebahagiaan dan Alkonost burung kesedihan, sedangkan sumber lain justru menyebut Sirin burung duka yang cenderung berniat buruk kepada manusia, sementara Alkonost adalah burung kebahagiaan. Pada abad ke-17 hingga ke-18, citranya berubah menjadi lambang keselarasan dunia, dan orang percaya hanya orang bahagia yang dapat mendengarnya.
long_description.en: Sources disagree about her nature. One calls the Sirin the bird of happiness and the Alkonost the bird of sorrow, while another makes the Sirin the bird of grief, rather ill-disposed to humans, and the Alkonost the bird of happiness. In the 17th–18th centuries her image shifted to a symbol of world harmony, and people believed only the happy could hear her.

long_description.id: Sirin kadang dipandang sebagai kiasan firman Tuhan yang masuk ke jiwa manusia, kadang sebagai kiasan bidah yang menggoda orang lemah. Dalam cerita rakyat Rusia, Sirin dicampuradukkan dengan penulis religius Ephrem the Syrian, sehingga penyair petani memakai nama Sirin sebagai sinonim untuk penyair. Bersama Alkonost dan Gamayun, ia termasuk burung peramal dalam cerita rakyat Rusia. Pengarang Vladimir Nabokov pun pernah memakai Sirin sebagai nama samaran.
long_description.en: The Sirin is sometimes read as a metaphor for God's word entering a person's soul, and sometimes for heretics tempting the weak. In Russian folklore she became mixed up with the religious writer Ephrem the Syrian, so peasant poets used Sirin as another word for poet. With the Alkonost and Gamayun she is one of the prophetic birds of Russian folklore. The author Vladimir Nabokov even wrote under the pen name Sirin.

who.id: Sirin adalah burung legenda berkepala perempuan.

claims.quote: is a legendary creature in Russian folklore, with the head of a beautiful woman and the body of a bird (usually an owl), often equated with sirens in Greek mythology.

statement.en: The Sirin is a legendary creature in Russian folklore with a beautiful woman's head and a bird's body (usually an owl), often equated with the sirens of Greek mythology.

claims.quote: According to myth, the Sirin lived in Iriy or around the Euphrates River. The Sirin is considered the bird of happiness; it is related to the Alkonost, the bird of sorrow.

statement.id: Menurut mitos, Sirin tinggal di Iriy atau di sekitar Sungai Efrat; ia dianggap burung kebahagiaan dan berkaitan dengan Alkonost, burung kesedihan.
statement.en: According to myth the Sirin lived in Iriy or around the Euphrates; she is considered the bird of happiness, related to the Alkonost, the bird of sorrow.

claims.quote: The legend of the Sirin may have a Persian origin. The Pomors often depicted the Sirin on illustrations in the Book of Genesis as birds sitting in paradise trees.

statement.id: Legenda Sirin mungkin berasal dari Persia; orang Pomor sering menggambarkannya dalam ilustrasi Kitab Kejadian sebagai burung yang bertengger di pohon surga.
statement.en: The Sirin legend may be of Persian origin; the Pomors often drew her in Book of Genesis illustrations as birds sitting in paradise trees.

claims.quote: Later, in the 17th–18th centuries, the image of the Sirin changed and she started to symbolize world harmony (as she lives near paradise).

statement.id: Pada abad ke-17–18, citra Sirin berubah dan ia mulai melambangkan keselarasan dunia karena tinggal di dekat surga.
statement.en: In the 17th–18th centuries the image of the Sirin changed and she came to symbolize world harmony, as she lives near paradise.

claims.quote: People in those times believed only happy people could hear the Sirin, while only very few could see one because she is as fast and difficult to catch as human happiness.

statement.id: Orang pada masa itu percaya hanya orang bahagia yang dapat mendengar Sirin, dan sangat sedikit yang bisa melihatnya karena ia secepat dan sesulit ditangkap seperti kebahagiaan manusia.
statement.en: People then believed only happy people could hear the Sirin, and very few could see her, as she is as quick and elusive as human happiness.

claims.quote: However, instead of using its voice to lure sailors to their deaths, the Sirin uses it to reward the virtuous. She was usually portrayed wearing a crown or with a nimbus.

statement.id: Alih-alih memakai suaranya untuk memikat pelaut menuju maut, Sirin memakainya untuk mengganjar orang saleh; ia biasanya digambarkan bermahkota atau berlingkaran cahaya.
statement.en: Instead of using her voice to lure sailors to death, the Sirin uses it to reward the virtuous; she was usually shown wearing a crown or a nimbus.

claims.quote: The Sirin sang beautiful songs to the saints, foretelling future blisses. The bird was dangerous. Men who heard her would forget everything on earth, follow her, and ultimately die.

statement.id: Sirin menyanyikan lagu indah bagi para santo, meramalkan kebahagiaan mendatang; burung ini berbahaya, karena laki-laki yang mendengarnya melupakan segala hal di bumi, mengikutinya, dan akhirnya mati.
statement.en: The Sirin sang beautiful songs to the saints, foretelling future bliss; the bird was dangerous, for men who heard her forgot everything on earth, followed her and finally died.

claims.quote: People would attempt to save themselves from the Sirin by shooting cannons, ringing bells and making other loud noises to scare the bird off.

statement.id: Orang berusaha menyelamatkan diri dari Sirin dengan menembakkan meriam, membunyikan lonceng, dan membuat bunyi keras lain untuk mengusirnya.
statement.en: People tried to save themselves from the Sirin by firing cannons, ringing bells and making other loud noises to scare her off.

statement.en: The Sirin is sometimes seen as a metaphor for God's word entering a man's soul, and sometimes for heretics tempting the weak.

claims.quote: In Russian folklore, Sirin was mixed with the revered religious writer, Ephrem the Syrian. Thus, peasant lyrists such as Nikolay Klyuev often used the Sirin as a synonym for poet.

statement.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Rusia, Sirin dicampuradukkan dengan penulis religius Ephrem the Syrian, sehingga penyair petani seperti Nikolay Klyuev memakai Sirin sebagai sinonim untuk penyair.
statement.en: In Russian folklore the Sirin was mixed up with the religious writer Ephrem the Syrian, so peasant poets such as Nikolay Klyuev used Sirin as a synonym for poet.

short_description.id: Naga Slavia adalah sebutan untuk naga mana pun dalam mitologi Slavia, seperti zmei dari Rusia atau żmij dari Polandia, yang sering digambarkan sebagai ular bersayap.
short_description.en: Slavic dragon is the name for any dragon in Slavic mythology, such as the Russian zmei or the Polish żmij, often pictured as a winged serpent.

long_description.id: Naga Slavia mencakup semua naga dalam mitologi Slavia, termasuk żmij dari Polandia, zmei dari Rusia, dan padanannya di budaya Slavia lain. Istilah-istilah itu berasal dari kata Proto-Slavia *zmьjь, dan kebanyakan merupakan bentuk maskulin dari kata Slavia untuk "ular". Wujudnya memadukan naga klasik dan ular, sebagai ular bersayap, dan kadang digambarkan berkaki dua atau berkepala lebih dari satu.
long_description.en: The Slavic dragon covers every dragon of Slavic mythology, including the Polish żmij, the Russian zmei and their counterparts in other Slavic cultures. These terms descend from Proto-Slavic *zmьjь, and most are masculine forms of the Slavic word for "snake". In shape it blends the classical dragon with a snake, as a winged serpent, and is sometimes shown with two legs or several heads.

long_description.id: Zmei bisa berwujud binatang atau mirip manusia: berwujud naga di udara dan manusia di darat, kadang merayu perempuan, tetapi dalam sastra Rusia sering menjadi musuh utama. Motif umum tentang naga Slavia antara lain perannya sebagai penguasa cuaca atau sumber air, asal-usulnya sebagai ular, dan kisah cinta naga jantan maupun betina dengan manusia. Dalam kepercayaan Rusia, ular, kadal, ayam jantan, atau ikan mas yang mencapai umur tertentu dapat berubah menjadi zmei terbang.
long_description.en: A zmei may be beast-like or human-like, taking dragon form in the air and human form on the ground; it sometimes woos women but in Russian literature often plays the chief villain. Common motifs include its role as master of weather or water sources, its beginning as a snake, and love affairs between humans and male or female dragons. In Russian lore a snake, lizard, rooster or carp that reaches a certain age may turn into a flying zmei.

long_description.id: Di Balkan, zmei pada umumnya dianggap baik, sebagai naga roh penjaga yang melawan naga jahat seperti lamia. Di Bulgaria ia kadang digambarkan bersisik dengan empat kaki dan sayap kelelawar, kadang setengah manusia setengah ular dengan ekor seperti ikan. Sebaliknya, di Slovenia naga biasanya dianggap jahat, walaupun naga Ljubljana justru melindungi kota itu dan tampil di lambang kotanya.
long_description.en: In the Balkans the zmei is generally seen as benevolent, a guardian-spirit dragon set against evil dragons such as the lamia. In Bulgaria it is sometimes described as scaly, four-legged and bat-winged, sometimes as half man, half snake with a fish-like tail. In Slovenia, by contrast, dragons are usually held to be evil, though the Ljubljana dragon protects that city and appears on its coat of arms.

long_description.id: Bentuk-bentuk khusus naga Slavia antara lain Zmey Gorynych dari legenda Rusia dan Ukraina, yang berkepala tiga sampai dua belas (satu sumber menyebutnya berkepala tiga, hijau, dan dapat menyemburkan api), serta smok dari Polandia, Ukraina, dan Belarus, misalnya Naga Wawel dari Kraków. Ada pula gagasan, yang diduga diilhami angin puting beliung, tentang naga yang mencelupkan ekornya ke sungai atau danau dan menyedot airnya hingga menimbulkan banjir.
long_description.en: Particular forms include Zmey Gorynych of Russian and Ukrainian legend, with three to twelve heads (one source makes him three-headed, green and fire-breathing), and the Polish, Ukrainian or Belarusian smok, such as the Wawel Dragon of Kraków. There is also a notion, thought to be inspired by tornadoes, of a dragon that dips its tail into a river or lake and sucks up the water to cause floods.

literal_meaning.en: (masculine form of the word for) snake

short_description.id: Sooterkin adalah makhluk kecil dongeng mirip tikus mondok yang dahulu dipercaya dapat dilahirkan perempuan tertentu, dikaitkan dengan perempuan Belanda yang duduk di atas tungku.
short_description.en: The sooterkin is a fabled small mole-like creature that some women were once believed able to give birth to, blamed on Dutch women sitting over stoves.

long_description.id: Sooterkin adalah makhluk kecil dongeng mirip tikus mondok yang dahulu dipercaya dapat dilahirkan perempuan tertentu. Asal khayalan yang mula-mula bersifat lelucon ini berasal dari abad ke-18, dan sebagian dokter terkemuka masa itu menganggapnya nyata. Ia dikaitkan dengan kebiasaan perempuan Belanda (Dutch) yang sering duduk di atas tungku atau memakai penghangat di bawah rok mereka, yang konon membiakkan hewan kecil yang kemudian tumbuh dan lahir.
long_description.en: Folk belief once held that some women could give birth to a sooterkin, a small mole-like creature of fable. This at-first jokey fancy dates from the 18th century, and some leading physicians of the time took it as fact. It was blamed on Dutch women's habit of sitting on stoves or warming themselves with them under their petticoats, supposedly breeding a small animal that would grow and be born.

long_description.id: Dokter Inggris (English) John Maubray dalam The Female Physician menyatakan perempuan dapat melahirkan sooterkin; ia pendukung teori "maternal impression" dan terlibat dalam kasus Mary Toft, yang tampak membuktikan teorinya dengan "melahirkan" kelinci, meski seluruh perkara itu akhirnya terbongkar sebagai tipuan. Seseorang dengan nama samaran Dr Giovanni lalu menerbitkan The Sooterkin Dissected yang menyatakan percaya padanya adalah kebodohan. Menurut artikel de, John Cleveland pada 1654 menulis bahwa perempuan Belanda konon melahirkan sooterkin "tidak jauh berbeda dengan tikus" bersama anak-anak mereka, dan makhluk ini juga disebut Suyger.
long_description.en: The English physician John Maubray, in The Female Physician, held that women could bear sooterkins; he championed 'maternal impression' and was drawn into the case of Mary Toft, who seemed to prove his theory by 'giving birth' to rabbits, though the whole affair was finally exposed as a hoax. Someone under the alias Dr Giovanni then published The Sooterkin Dissected, calling belief in it stupidity. According to the de article John Cleveland wrote in 1654 that Dutch women were said to bear a sooterkin 'not unlike to a Rat' together with their children, and the creature is also called Suyger.

short_description.id: Soucouyant adalah nenek sihir pengubah wujud dalam cerita rakyat Karibia yang pada malam hari melepas kulitnya, terbang sebagai bola api, dan mengisap darah orang yang tidur.
short_description.en: The soucouyant is a shape-shifting hag of Caribbean folklore who sheds her skin at night, flies as a fireball and sucks the blood of sleepers.

long_description.id: Soucouyant adalah nenek sihir pengubah wujud dan pengisap darah dalam cerita rakyat Karibia; di Guyana, Belize, dan Jamaika ia disebut Ol' Higue. Pada siang hari ia tampak sebagai orang tua penyendiri. Pada malam hari ia melepas kulit keriputnya, menaruhnya di lesung, lalu terbang sebagai bola api untuk mengisap darah orang yang tidur, meninggalkan memar biru kehitaman. Darah itu ditukarnya dengan kekuatan jahat dari Bazil, iblis penghuni pohon kapuk.
long_description.en: The soucouyant is a shape-shifting, blood-sucking hag of Caribbean folklore, called Ol' Higue in Guyana, Belize and Jamaica. By day she looks like a reclusive old person. At night she sheds her wrinkled skin into a mortar and flies as a fireball to suck the blood of sleepers, leaving black and blue marks. She trades the blood for evil powers with Bazil, the demon of the silk cotton tree.

long_description.id: Untuk membongkarnya, orang menaburkan beras di sekitar rumah atau persimpangan desa, karena soucouyant terpaksa memungutinya butir demi butir. Di Trinidad dan Tobago, salib di jendela dipercaya melindungi rumah darinya.
long_description.en: To expose her, people heap rice around the house or the village crossroads, since the soucouyant must gather it grain by grain. In Trinidad and Tobago a cross in the window is believed to protect a house from her.

short_description.id: Stoor worm adalah ular laut raksasa yang jahat dalam folklor Orkney, yang napas busuknya meracuni tumbuhan dan membunuh hewan serta manusia.
short_description.en: The stoor worm is a gigantic evil sea serpent of Orcadian folklore whose putrid breath blights plants and kills animals and people.

long_description.id: Stoor worm atau Mester Stoor Worm adalah ular laut raksasa yang jahat dalam folklor Orkney, yang mampu meracuni tumbuhan dan membinasakan hewan serta manusia dengan napas busuknya. Ia kemungkinan varian Orkney dari Jörmungandr Norse, Ular Midgard, dan digambarkan sebagai naga laut. Namanya mungkin berasal dari Norse Kuno Storðar-gandr, nama lain Jörmungandr; "Mester" berarti tuan, karena ia "tuan dan bapak semua stoorworm".
long_description.en: The stoor worm, or Mester Stoor Worm, is a gigantic wicked sea serpent of Orkney folklore that could blight plants and kill animals and people with its rotten breath. It is probably an Orkney form of the Norse Jörmungandr, the Midgard Serpent, and has been called a sea dragon. The name may derive from Old Norse Storðar-gandr, another name for Jörmungandr, and 'Mester' means master, as it was the 'master and father of all stoorworms'.

long_description.id: Seorang raja yang negerinya terancam dinasihati mempersembahkan tujuh perawan setiap minggu; akhirnya ia menawarkan kerajaan, tangan putrinya dan pedang ajaib kepada siapa pun yang dapat membinasakan monster itu. Assipattle, putra bungsu seorang petani, mengalahkannya; saat ia mati, giginya rontok menjadi Kepulauan Orkney, Shetland dan Faroe, dan tubuhnya menjadi Islandia.
long_description.en: A king whose land it threatened was advised to feed it seven virgins every week; in the end he offered his kingdom, his daughter's hand and a magic sword to whoever could destroy it. Assipattle, a farmer's youngest son, overcame it; as it died its teeth dropped out to form Orkney, Shetland and the Faroes, and its body became Iceland.

famous_for.en: Its body became Iceland.

did_you_know.en: Legend says the stoor worm's teeth became Orkney, Shetland and the Faroes, and its body became Iceland.

short_description.id: Strzyga biasanya adalah iblis perempuan mirip vampir dalam mitologi Slavia, terutama dalam cerita rakyat Polandia dan Silesia, yang berasal dari Strix Romawi dan Yunani kuno.
short_description.en: The strzyga is usually a female vampire-like demon of Slavic mythology, chiefly in Polish and Silesian folklore, stemming from the Strix of ancient Rome and Greece.

long_description.id: Strzyga (jamak strzygi, laki-laki strzygoń) biasanya iblis perempuan dalam mitologi Slavia yang berasal dari Strix dalam mitologi Romawi dan Yunani kuno. Ia mirip vampir dan terutama ditemukan dalam cerita rakyat Polandia dan Silesia. Menurut Aleksander Brückner, kata ini berasal dari strix, burung hantu dalam bahasa Latin, makhluk mirip burung yang memakan daging dan darah manusia.
long_description.en: The strzyga (plural strzygi, male strzygoń) is usually a female demon of Slavic myth derived from the Strix of Roman and Greek antiquity. Vampire-like, she belongs mostly to Polish and Silesian folklore. Aleksander Brückner traced the word to strix, Latin for an owl, a bird-like being that fed on human flesh and blood.

long_description.id: Menurut kepercayaan Silesia, strzyga lahir sebagai strzyga: semasa hidup ia punya dua hati, dua jiwa, dan dua baris gigi. Setelah ia mati, satu jiwa meninggalkan tubuh, sementara jiwa lain tetap hidup di dalam jasad di peti. Agar ia tidak mencelakai orang, makamnya digali dan jantungnya ditusuk pasak kayu ek, atau kepalanya dipenggal; orang yang dicurigai akan menjadi strzyga dikuburkan telungkup dengan batu di bawah bibirnya. Strzyga kadang juga digambarkan sebagai burung hantu yang tinggal di hutan gelap.
long_description.en: Silesian belief held that a strzyga is born one: in life she has two hearts, two souls and two rows of teeth. When she dies one soul leaves while the other lives on in the body in the coffin. To stop her harming people, the grave was opened and her heart pierced with an oak stake, or her head cut off; someone suspected of becoming a strzyga was buried face down with a stone under the lips. Strzygi were also sometimes pictured as owls living in dark forests.

long_description.id: Strzyga tetap populer dalam cerita rakyat pedesaan Polandia hingga akhir abad ke-19 dan awal abad ke-20, seperti tampak dalam novel Chłopi karya Władysław Reymont. Setelah abad ke-18 dibedakan antara strzyga, yang lebih terkait dengan sihir, dan upiór, makhluk vampir yang terbang.
long_description.en: The strzyga stayed popular in rural Polish folklore into the late 19th and early 20th century, as Władysław Reymont's novel Chłopi shows. After the 18th century a line was drawn between the strzyga, tied more to witchcraft, and the upiór, a flying vampire.

claims.quote: Чтобы стрыга не могла вредить людям, нужно было выкопать её и проколоть ей сердце дубовым колышком ... либо отрезать ей голову и затем ударить её по ногам. Если кого-то при жизни могли заподозрить, что после смерти он станет стрыгой, то его хоронили ртом вниз и вставляли ему под губы камень

statement.id: Agar strzyga (Стрыга) tidak mencelakai orang, makamnya digali dan jantungnya ditusuk pasak kayu ek, atau kepalanya dipenggal; orang yang dicurigai akan menjadi strzyga dikuburkan telungkup dengan batu di bawah bibirnya.
statement.en: To stop a strzyga harming people she was dug up and her heart pierced with an oak stake, or her head cut off; someone suspected of becoming one was buried face down with a stone under the lips.

claims.quote: В отличие от вампиров, стрыгоем, согласно силезским поверьям, человек рождался сразу. При жизни стрыга имеет два сердца, две души и два ряда зубов ... Известны случаи, когда за стрыг принимали младенцев, рождавшихся с развитыми зубами. Считалось, что после смерти стрыги одна душа покидала тело, а другая оставалась в нём и продолжала жить в теле в гробу

statement.id: Menurut kepercayaan Silesia, strzyga lahir sebagai strzyga; semasa hidup ia punya dua hati, dua jiwa, dan dua baris gigi; bayi yang lahir dengan gigi kadang disangka strzyga; setelah mati satu jiwa pergi dan yang lain tetap hidup di dalam jasad di peti.
statement.en: In Silesian belief a person was born a strzyga; in life she has two hearts, two souls and two rows of teeth; babies born with developed teeth were sometimes taken for strzygi; after death one soul leaves and the other lives on in the body in the coffin.

claims.quote: Стрыги также изображались иногда и как совы, обитающие в тёмных лесах

statement.id: Strzyga kadang juga digambarkan sebagai burung hantu yang tinggal di hutan gelap.
statement.en: Strzygi were also sometimes depicted as owls living in dark forests.

short_description.id: Sugaar atau Maju adalah dewa ular atau naga dalam mitologi Basque, pasangan dewi Mari, yang bersatu dengannya setiap Jumat untuk menimbulkan badai.
short_description.en: Sugaar or Maju is a serpent or dragon god of Basque mythology, consort of the goddess Mari, who joins her every Friday to raise storms.

long_description.id: Sugaar, juga Sugar, Sugoi, atau Maju, "ular jantan", adalah separuh laki-laki dari dewa Basque pra-Kristen yang berkaitan dengan badai dan guntur. Wujud aslinya ular atau naga, kadang api atau petir. Ia pasangan Mari dan mengunjunginya di Anboto setiap Jumat; pertemuan mereka melahirkan badai dan hujan es dan melambangkan hujan yang menyuburkan bumi. Ia tinggal di gua dan gunung seperti Aralar dan ayah Mikelatz dan Atarrabi.
long_description.en: Sugaar, also Sugar, Sugoi or Maju, 'male serpent', is the male half of a pre-Christian Basque deity of storms and thunder. His true form is a serpent or dragon, sometimes fire or lightning. He is Mari's consort and visits her at Anboto every Friday; their union brings storms and hail and figures the rain that fertilises the earth. He lives in caves and mountains such as Aralar and fathered Mikelatz and Atarrabi.

long_description.id: Di Betelu ia dianggap roh jahat dan di Ataun momok. Legenda dari Dima menceritakan dua bersaudara yang menemukannya di gua Baltzola; si adik memotong ekornya, dan bertahun-tahun kemudian sabuk merah pemberian Sugaar membakar pohon kastanye. Mitos lain menjadikannya ayah Jaun Zuria, penguasa pertama Biscaya, dari seorang putri Skotlandia.
long_description.en: In Betelu he is an evil spirit and in Ataun a bogeyman. A legend from Dima tells of two brothers who found him in the Baltzola cave; the younger cut his tail, and years later a red belt from Sugaar set a chestnut tree ablaze. Another myth makes him father, by a Scottish princess, of Jaun Zuria, first lord of Biscay.

claims.quote: In Basque mythology, Sugaar (also Sugar, Sugoi, Suarra, Maju) is the male half of a pre-Christian Basque deity associated with storms and thunder. He shows may similarities to Herensuge, with Sugaar being much older.

statement.id: Dalam mitologi Basque, Sugaar (juga Sugar, Sugoi, Suarra, Maju) adalah separuh laki-laki dari dewa Basque pra-Kristen yang berkaitan dengan badai dan guntur, dan ia banyak mirip Herensuge meski jauh lebih tua.
statement.en: In Basque mythology Sugaar (also Sugar, Sugoi, Suarra, Maju) is the male half of a pre-Christian Basque deity of storms and thunder, much like Herensuge but far older.

claims.quote: Sugaar is sometimes said to take the form of pure fire or lightning, but his true form is usually represented as a serpent or dragon. He is Mari's consort, and is said to visit her at Anboto every Friday.

statement.id: Sugaar kadang berwujud api murni atau petir, tetapi wujud aslinya biasanya ular atau naga; ia pasangan Mari dan konon mengunjunginya di Anboto setiap Jumat.
statement.en: Sugaar sometimes takes the form of pure fire or lightning, but his true form is usually a serpent or dragon; he is Mari's consort and visits her at Anboto every Friday.

claims.quote: The visits are also considered sexual in nature, a reference to how the rain (Sugaar) fertilizes the earth and soil (Mari).

statement.id: Kunjungan itu juga dianggap bersifat seksual, melambangkan hujan (Sugaar) yang menyuburkan bumi dan tanah (Mari).
statement.en: The visits are also seen as sexual, a figure of the rain (Sugaar) fertilising the earth (Mari).

claims.quote: Like Mari, Sugar is said to live in various caves and mountains. One of his homes is said to be the Aralar Mountain Range.

statement.id: Seperti Mari, Sugaar tinggal di berbagai gua dan gunung, salah satunya Pegunungan Aralar.
statement.en: Like Mari he lives in various caves and mountains, one of them the Aralar range.

claims.quote: In Betelu, Sugaar is said to be an evil spirit, and in Ataun, he is used as a bogyman figure.

statement.id: Di Betelu Sugaar dianggap roh jahat, dan di Ataun ia dipakai sebagai momok untuk menakuti anak.
statement.en: In Betelu Sugaar is an evil spirit, and in Ataun a bogeyman.

claims.quote: The pair found Sugaar in a cave in Baltzola, and the younger of the two cut his tail with a stone.

statement.id: Dalam sebuah legenda, dua bersaudara dari Dima menemukan Sugaar di gua Baltzola, dan si adik memotong ekornya dengan batu.
statement.en: In one legend two brothers from Dima found Sugaar in the Baltzola cave, and the younger cut his tail with a stone.

claims.quote: When the brothers met again, the younger brother refused to put the belt on and tied it to a chestnut tree. The tree burst into flames, and they realized that the man must have been Sugaar.

statement.id: Bertahun-tahun kemudian si adik menolak memakai sabuk merah pemberian seorang lelaki misterius dan mengikatkannya ke pohon kastanye, yang langsung terbakar, sehingga mereka sadar lelaki itu Sugaar.
statement.en: Years later the younger brother refused a red belt from a mysterious man and tied it to a chestnut tree, which burst into flames, and they realised the man was Sugaar.

claims.quote: The name Suga(a)r is derived from suge (serpent) and -ar (male), thus "male serpent". The suggestions of a formation based on su (fire) and gar (flame), thus yielding "flame of fire" are considered folk etymology.

statement.id: Nama Sugaar berasal dari suge (ular) dan -ar (jantan), jadi "ular jantan"; tafsiran su (api) + gar (nyala), "nyala api", dianggap etimologi rakyat.
statement.en: Sugaar comes from suge (serpent) and -ar (male), 'male serpent'; the reading su (fire) + gar (flame), 'flame of fire', is considered folk etymology.

claims.quote: L'essentiel de son existence est de se joindre périodiquement (le vendredi, à deux heures de l'après-midi) à Mari dans les montagnes pour y engendrer des orages.

statement.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Prancis, tugas utamanya adalah bersatu secara berkala dengan Mari di gunung (hari Jumat pukul dua siang) untuk melahirkan badai.
statement.en: According to the French article, his main role is to join Mari periodically in the mountains (on Friday at two in the afternoon) to engender storms.

claims.quote: Additionnellement, il existe un mythe dans lequel il séduit une princesse écossaise dans le village de Mundaka, pour concevoir le mythique premier seigneur de Biscaye, Jaun Zuria.

statement.id: Ada pula mitos bahwa ia menggoda seorang putri Skotlandia di desa Mundaka dan menjadi ayah Jaun Zuria, penguasa pertama Biscaya yang mitis.
statement.en: There is also a myth that he seduced a Scottish princess at Mundaka and fathered Jaun Zuria, the mythical first lord of Biscay.

claims.quote: Maju est considéré comme un génie souterrain qui, en sortant de son antre, s’unit à Mari, provoquant alors une tempête accompagnée de grêle et de grêlons.

statement.id: Maju dianggap roh bawah tanah yang, ketika keluar dari sarangnya dan bersatu dengan Mari, menimbulkan badai disertai hujan es.
statement.en: Maju is considered an underground spirit who, leaving his lair to unite with Mari, brings a storm with hail.

claims.quote: Es una divinidad de carácter masculino, consorte de la diosa Mari (tiene, sin embargo, un papel mucho más oscuro que esta), y padre de Mikelatz (hijo perverso) y Atarrabi (hijo bondadoso).

statement.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Spanyol, ia dewa laki-laki, pasangan dewi Mari dengan peran yang lebih samar, dan ayah Mikelatz (anak jahat) serta Atarrabi (anak baik).
statement.en: According to the Spanish article, he is a male deity, consort of the goddess Mari though with a much dimmer role, and father of Mikelatz (the wicked son) and Atarrabi (the good son).

short_description.id: Şüräle adalah roh hutan dalam mitologi Tatar dan Bashkir, bertanduk dan berjari panjang, yang memikat orang ke semak dan menggelitiki korbannya sampai mati.
short_description.en: Şüräle is a horned, long-fingered forest spirit of Tatar and Bashkir mythology who lures people into thickets and tickles victims to death.

long_description.id: Şüräle adalah roh hutan dalam mitologi Turkik, terutama Tatar dan Bashkir, dan juga dikenal dalam cerita rakyat Chuvash dan Mari. Ia berjari panjang, bertanduk di dahi, dan berbulu lebat; ia memikat korban ke semak lalu menggelitikinya sampai mati. Ia dapat berubah wujud, misalnya menjadi petani bermata menyala dengan sepatu terbalik; orang yang berteman dengannya dapat mempelajari rahasia sihir.
long_description.en: Şüräle is a forest spirit of Turkic, especially Tatar and Bashkir, mythology, also known in Chuvash and Mari folklore. It is long-fingered and woolly, with a single horn on its brow, and lures victims into thickets to tickle them to death. It can change shape, for example into a glowing-eyed peasant with backward shoes; those who befriend it can learn the secrets of magic.

long_description.id: Ia dihormati sebagai roh hutan sekaligus dibenci sebagai makhluk yang menyerang manusia, dan mirip tokoh seperti Arçuri dari Chuvash dan Pitsen dari Tatar Siberia. Ghabdulla Tuqay menulis puisi Şüräle, yang menjadi dasar balet Tatar pertama karya Farit Yarullin.
long_description.en: It is both honoured as the forest spirit and hated as a creature that attacks people, and resembles figures such as the Chuvash Arçuri and the Siberian Tatar Pitsen. Ghabdulla Tuqay wrote the poem Şüräle, which became the basis of the first Tatar ballet by Farit Yarullin.

short_description.id: Tangie adalah roh laut pengubah wujud dalam cerita rakyat Orkney dan Shetland, berwujud kuda atau lelaki tua berselimut rumput laut.
short_description.en: The tangie is a shape-shifting sea spirit of Orkney and Shetland folklore, appearing as a horse or an old man covered in seaweed.

long_description.id: Tangie (atau tongie) adalah roh laut pengubah wujud dalam cerita rakyat Kepulauan Orkney dan Shetland di Skotlandia (Scotland). Sebagai kuda laut atau duyung lelaki, ia berwujud kuda atau lelaki tua. Biasanya ia digambarkan berselimut rumput laut, dan namanya berasal dari "tang", rumput laut genus Fucus. Ia terkenal meneror pelancong yang sendirian, terutama perempuan muda di jalan dekat danau (loch) pada malam hari, yang diculiknya dan dimakannya di bawah air.
long_description.en: Island lore from Orkney and Shetland in Scotland tells of the tangie (or tongie), a sea spirit that changes shape; as a sea horse or merman it appears as either a horse or an old man. It is usually said to be draped in seaweed, and its name comes from 'tang', seaweed of the genus Fucus. It is known for frightening lone travellers, above all young women on roads near the lochs at night, whom it carries off and devours underwater.

long_description.id: Mirip tetapi berbeda dari nuggle yang lebih kecil dan kurang berbahaya, tangie dapat membuat manusia dan hewan gila. Tangie berperan besar dalam legenda Shetland tentang Black Eric, pencuri domba: tangie yang ditungganginya memberinya bantuan gaib saat ia menyerbu pertanian sekitar. Dalam pertarungan terakhirnya dengan petani Sandy Breamer, Black Eric jatuh ke laut dan tewas, tetapi tangie terus meneror daerah itu. Menurut artikel ru, Танги juga disebut pengubah wujud laut yang dapat membuat orang atau hewan gila.
long_description.en: Similar to yet distinct from the smaller, milder nuggle, the tangie can drive people and animals mad. It plays a big part in Shetland's tale of Black Eric the sheep thief, whose tangie steed gave him supernatural help as he raided nearby crofts. In his last fight with the crofter Sandy Breamer, Black Eric fell into the sea and died, but the tangie went on terrorising the area. According to the ru article the Танги is likewise a sea shapeshifter able to drive a person or animal mad.

famous_for.en: Black Eric's mount.

did_you_know.en: The name tangie comes from 'tang', seaweed of the genus Fucus that covers its body.

short_description.id: Tarand atau parandrus adalah binatang legendaris sebesar lembu dengan kepala dan tanduk rusa yang dapat mengubah warna bulunya seperti bunglon, dari tulisan kuno dan bestiari.
short_description.en: The tarand or parandrus is a legendary ox-sized beast with a deer's head and antlers that changes its fur colour like a chameleon, from ancient writings and bestiaries.

long_description.id: Tarand, tarandus, atau parandrus adalah binatang legendaris mirip rusa kutub atau rusa besar, sebesar lembu dengan kepala rusa dan tanduk bercabang, yang mengubah warna bulunya menyerupai pohon dan tanah sehingga sulit ditangkap. Teks yang dikaitkan dengan Aristoteles, Plinius, dan Aelianus menempatkannya di Skithia, sedangkan Solinus di Aethiopia.
long_description.en: The tarand, tarandus or parandrus is a legendary reindeer- or moose-like beast, ox-sized with a deer's head and branching antlers, that changes its fur colour to match trees and ground, so it is hard to catch. Texts ascribed to Aristotle, Pliny and Aelian place it in Scythia, while Solinus puts it in Aethiopia.

long_description.id: Ia muncul lagi dalam York Mystery Cycle (1440) dan Pantagruel karya Rabelais (1552), kebenarannya dibahas Baron Cuvier, dan nama ilmiah rusa kutub, Rangifer tarandus, berasal darinya. Uraian "Aristoteles" berasal dari karya yang keliru dikaitkan kepadanya.
long_description.en: It reappears in the York Mystery Cycle (1440) and Rabelais's Pantagruel (1552), Baron Cuvier discussed whether it was real, and the reindeer's scientific name, Rangifer tarandus, comes from it. The 'Aristotle' account comes from a work wrongly attributed to him.

famous_for.id: Bulu yang berubah warna seperti bunglon.
famous_for.en: Fur that changes colour like a chameleon.

claims.quote: A tarand, also known as a tarandos, tarandus, parandrus, or parandros, is a legendary reindeer/moose-like creature with chameleon properties.

statement.id: Tarand, juga tarandos, tarandus, parandrus, atau parandros, adalah makhluk legendaris mirip rusa kutub atau rusa besar dengan kemampuan seperti bunglon.
statement.en: A tarand, also tarandos, tarandus, parandrus or parandros, is a legendary reindeer- or moose-like creature with chameleon-like powers.

claims.quote: It was also mentioned in Pliny's History of the Animals (Tarandus), Aelian's De Natura Animalium (Tarandos), Solinus (Parandrus) and Caesar, appearing again in key texts of the medieval period, such as  The York Mystery Cycle (1440) and Francois Rabelais' Pantagruel (1552).

statement.id: Ia disebut Plinius, Aelianus dalam De Natura Animalium, Solinus, dan Caesar, lalu muncul lagi dalam teks abad pertengahan seperti York Mystery Cycle (1440) dan Pantagruel karya François Rabelais (1552).
statement.en: It is mentioned by Pliny, Aelian in De Natura Animalium, Solinus and Caesar, and appears again in later texts such as the York Mystery Cycle (1440) and Rabelais's Pantagruel (1552).

claims.quote: Aristotle, Pliny and Aelian write that the animal (Tarandus) was living in Scythia, while Solinus write that the animal that he describes (Parandus) was living in Aethiopia.

statement.id: Aristoteles, Plinius, dan Aelianus menulis bahwa hewan ini hidup di Skithia, sedangkan Solinus menempatkannya di Aethiopia.
statement.en: Aristotle, Pliny and Aelian place the animal in Scythia, while Solinus puts it in Aethiopia.

claims.quote: Among the Scythians called Geloni they say that there is a beast, excessively rare, which is called tarandus; they say that it changes the colour of its hair according to the place it is in. For this reason it is difficult to catch; for it becomes the same colour as the trees and the ground

statement.id: Menurut teks Aristotelian, di kalangan suku Skithia Geloni ada binatang sangat langka bernama tarandus yang mengubah warna bulunya sesuai tempatnya, sehingga sulit ditangkap karena menyerupai warna pohon dan tanah.
statement.en: According to the Aristotelian text, among the Scythian Geloni there is a very rare beast called tarandus that changes the colour of its hair to suit its surroundings, so it is hard to catch, taking the colour of trees and ground.

claims.quote: But this animal is of the size of an ox. But its head is of the same kind as a deer.

statement.id: Binatang itu sebesar lembu dengan kepala seperti rusa.
statement.en: The animal is the size of an ox, with a deer-like head.

claims.quote: The veracity of the tarand was discussed by Jean Léopold Nicolas Frédéric, Baron Cuvier (1769–1832).

statement.id: Kebenaran keberadaan tarand dibahas oleh Baron Cuvier (1769–1832).
statement.en: The truth of the tarand was discussed by Baron Cuvier (1769–1832).

claims.quote: Es hat die Größe eines Ochsen, (teils langes) Fell, gespaltene Hufe und ein Geweih. Es kann, um sich zu tarnen, seine Fellfarbe ändern.

statement.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Jerman, ia sebesar lembu, berbulu (kadang panjang), berkuku belah, bertanduk cabang, dan dapat mengubah warna bulunya untuk menyamar.
statement.en: According to the German article it is ox-sized, furred (sometimes long-haired), cloven-hoofed and antlered, and can change its fur colour to camouflage itself.

claims.quote: Der wissenschaftliche Name des Rentiers (Rangifer tarandus) ist von seinem Namen abgeleitet.

statement.id: Nama ilmiah rusa kutub, Rangifer tarandus, berasal dari namanya.
statement.en: The reindeer's scientific name, Rangifer tarandus, comes from its name.

claims.quote: De mirabilibus auscultationibus (Sur les choses merveilleuses entendues) (en), ouvrage faussement attribué à Aristote, en fournit une description

statement.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Prancis, deskripsi "Aristoteles" itu berasal dari De mirabilibus auscultationibus, karya yang keliru dikaitkan dengan Aristoteles.
statement.en: According to the French article, the 'Aristotle' description comes from De mirabilibus auscultationibus, a work falsely attributed to Aristotle.

summary.id: Skithia (Aristoteles, Plinius, Aelianus).
summary.en: Scythia (Aristotle, Pliny, Aelian).

summary.id: Aethiopia (Solinus).
summary.en: Aethiopia (Solinus).

short_description.id: Tartalo atau Tartaro adalah raksasa bermata satu pemakan manusia dari mitologi Basque yang tinggal di gua pegunungan, mirip Kiklops Polifemos, dan memiliki cincin ajaib yang dapat berbicara.
short_description.en: Tartalo or Tartaro is a one-eyed man-eating giant of Basque mythology who lives in mountain caves, much like the Cyclops Polyphemus, and owns a talking magic ring.

long_description.id: Tartalo, Tartaro, atau Torto adalah raksasa bermata satu yang sangat kuat dari mitologi Basque, mirip Kiklops Polifemos, yang tinggal di gua pegunungan, beternak domba, dan menangkap orang muda untuk dimakan. Ukurannya dan nafsu makannya sangat besar, dan ia gemar melempar batu antargunung. Cerquand menduga namanya dari bangsa Tatar, dan tokoh bernama Tartari juga dikenal di Agenais.
long_description.en: Tartalo, Tartaro or Torto is an enormously strong one-eyed giant of Basque mythology, much like the Cyclops Polyphemus, who lives in mountain caves, keeps sheep and catches young people to eat. His size and appetite are huge, and he loves hurling stones between mountains. Cerquand derived his name from the Tartar people, and a figure called Tartari is known in the Agenais.

long_description.id: Dalam kisah terkenal, dua bersaudara dari Antimuño berlindung di gua Tartalo; ia memakan si kakak, lalu si adik mencuri cincinnya, membutakan matanya dengan tusuk panggangan, dan lolos berbalut kulit domba. Cincin ajaib itu berteriak memberi tahu tempatnya, maka si anak memotong jarinya dan melemparkannya ke jurang, dan Tartalo yang mengikuti suara cincin jatuh dari tebing.
long_description.en: In a well-known tale two brothers from Antimuño shelter in Tartalo's cave; he eats the elder, then the younger steals his ring, blinds him with a roasting spit and escapes in a sheepskin. The magic ring shouts out where he is, so the boy cuts off his finger and throws it into the ravine, and Tartalo, following the ring's voice, falls off the cliff.

famous_for.en: The shouting ring.

description.id: Satu-satunya matanya dapat dibutakan dengan tusuk panggangan.
description.en: His single eye can be blinded with a roasting spit.

summary.id: Tartalo memakan si kakak, dibutakan si adik, lalu jatuh dari tebing mengikuti teriakan cincinnya.
summary.en: Tartalo eats the elder brother, is blinded by the younger, then falls off a cliff following his ring's shouts.

note.id: Nama Anxo kadang dipakai untuk keduanya.
note.en: The name Anxo is sometimes used for both.

claims.quote: Tartaro, Tartalo, or Torto in Basque mythology, is an enormously strong one-eyed giant very similar to the Greek Cyclops that Odysseus faced in Homer's Odyssey. He is said to live in caves in the mountains and catches young people in order to eat them; in some accounts he eats sheep also.

statement.id: Tartaro, Tartalo, atau Torto dalam mitologi Basque adalah raksasa bermata satu yang sangat kuat, mirip Kiklops Yunani yang dihadapi Odisseus, yang tinggal di gua pegunungan dan menangkap orang muda untuk dimakan, kadang juga domba.
statement.en: Tartaro, Tartalo or Torto of Basque mythology is an enormously strong one-eyed giant much like the Greek Cyclops Odysseus faced, living in mountain caves and catching young people to eat, sometimes sheep too.

claims.quote: Torto, Anxo and Alarabi were the forms listed in Jose Migel Barandiaran's Basque Mythology, with "Tartalo" described as a local variant particular to the Zegama region.

statement.id: Torto, Anxo, dan Alarabi adalah bentuk nama yang dicatat Barandiaran, dengan "Tartalo" sebagai varian setempat daerah Zegama.
statement.en: Torto, Anxo and Alarabi are the forms listed by Barandiaran, with 'Tartalo' a local variant of the Zegama area.

claims.quote: Cerquand ... in his book "Légendes et récits populaires du Pays basque, volume 1" (1875) suggested in an annotation that the name "Tartaro" derived from the Tartar people

statement.id: Cerquand dalam bukunya (1875) menduga nama "Tartaro" berasal dari bangsa Tatar.
statement.en: Cerquand in his 1875 book suggested that the name 'Tartaro' came from the Tartar people.

claims.quote: A mystical ring is a common theme in the Tartalo/Tartaro tales.

statement.id: Cincin ajaib adalah tema umum dalam kisah-kisah Tartalo.
statement.en: A magic ring is a common theme in the Tartalo tales.

claims.quote: One day, while two brothers of the Antimuño baserri were hunting, a storm broke, so they decided to take refuge from the rain in a cave, which was Tartalo's cave.

statement.id: Suatu hari dua bersaudara dari pertanian Antimuño yang sedang berburu berlindung dari badai di sebuah gua, yang ternyata gua Tartalo.
statement.en: One day two brothers from the Antimuño farm, out hunting, sheltered from a storm in a cave that turned out to be Tartalo's.

claims.quote: While he was sleeping, the youngest brother stole Tartalo's ring and then he stuck the roasting spit in his only eye.

statement.id: Setelah Tartalo memakan si kakak dan tertidur, si adik mencuri cincinnya dan menusukkan tusuk panggangan ke satu-satunya matanya.
statement.en: After Tartalo ate the elder brother and fell asleep, the younger stole his ring and drove the roasting spit into his only eye.

claims.quote: He started to look for the boy among his sheep, but he put on a sheep's skin and escaped from Tartalo.

statement.id: Tartalo mencari si anak di antara dombanya, tetapi anak itu memakai kulit domba dan lolos.
statement.en: Tartalo searched for the boy among his sheep, but the boy put on a sheepskin and escaped.

claims.quote: The young one wasn't able to take off the ring, so, when he arrived to the edge of a cliff, he cut off his finger, and since Tartalo was near, he decided to throw it down the cliff. Tartalo, following the ring's shouting, fell off the cliff.

statement.id: Cincin itu berteriak memberi tahu tempatnya dan tidak dapat dilepas, maka di tepi tebing si anak memotong jarinya dan melemparkannya ke bawah; Tartalo mengikuti teriakan cincin itu dan jatuh dari tebing.
statement.en: The ring shouted out his whereabouts and would not come off, so at a cliff edge the boy cut off his finger and threw it down; Tartalo followed the ring's shouts and fell off the cliff.

claims.quote: Un personnage appelé Tartari était attesté au-delà de la Gascogne, rive droite de la Garonne, dans l'Agenais

statement.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Prancis, tokoh bernama Tartari juga dikenal di luar Gascogne, di Agenais di tepi kanan Garonne.
statement.en: According to the French article, a figure called Tartari was known beyond Gascony, in the Agenais on the right bank of the Garonne.

claims.quote: Les caractéristiques et les aventures qu'on lui prête correspondent d'assez près à celles du cyclope Polyphème. Comme lui il vit dans une caverne, il élève des moutons

statement.id: Ciri dan petualangannya cukup dekat dengan Kiklops Polifemos: seperti dia, Tartalo tinggal di gua dan beternak domba.
statement.en: His traits and adventures closely match those of the Cyclops Polyphemus: like him he lives in a cave and keeps sheep.

claims.quote: Anxo or Ancho is however explained as an alternate name for Basajaun by some sources.

statement.id: Sebagian sumber menyebut Anxo atau Ancho sebagai nama lain Basajaun.
statement.en: Some sources explain Anxo or Ancho as another name for Basajaun.

claims.quote: Su tamaño es descomunal, al igual que su apetito, y su entretenimiento favorito era tirar piedras de un monte a otro. Cuenta la leyenda que debido a este entretenimiento se crearon varias construcciones existentes hoy en día.

statement.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Spanyol, ukuran dan nafsu makannya sangat besar, dan kegemarannya melempar batu dari satu gunung ke gunung lain konon menghasilkan beberapa bangunan yang masih ada.
statement.en: According to the Spanish article, his size and appetite are enormous, and his favourite pastime of hurling stones from mountain to mountain is said to have created several structures still standing.
