display_name.id: The Laidly Worm of Spindleston Heugh
display_name.en: The Laidly Worm of Spindleston Heugh

short_description.id: Laidly Worm dari Spindleston Heugh adalah balada Northumbria tentang seorang putri yang diubah menjadi naga oleh ibu tirinya yang penyihir.
short_description.en: The Laidly Worm of Spindleston Heugh is a Northumbrian ballad about a princess turned into a dragon by her witch stepmother.

long_description.id: The Laidly Worm of Spindleston Heugh, juga The Laidly Worm of Bamborough, adalah balada Northumbria tentang seorang putri yang diubah menjadi naga, "laidly worm" (naga buruk rupa). Di Kerajaan Northumbria, seorang raja baik di Kastel Bamburgh menikahi penyihir cantik tetapi kejam setelah istrinya wafat. Saat putranya Childe Wynd berada di seberang laut, penyihir itu, iri pada kecantikan Putri Margaret, mengubahnya menjadi naga.
long_description.en: The Laidly Worm of Spindleston Heugh, also The Laidly Worm of Bamborough, is a Northumbrian ballad of a princess changed into a dragon, the 'laidly worm' (loathsome serpent) of the title. In the Kingdom of Northumbria a good king at Bamburgh Castle weds a lovely but cruel witch after his wife dies. While his son Childe Wynd is overseas, the witch, envious of Princess Margaret's beauty, turns her into a dragon.

long_description.id: Sang pangeran pulang dan, alih-alih melawan naga itu, menciumnya tiga kali, sehingga sang putri kembali ke wujud aslinya; ia lalu mengubah ratu penyihir menjadi katak dan menjadi raja. Balada ini pertama diterbitkan pada 1778, konon disalin Pendeta Robert Lambe dari naskah Latin tahun 1270, tetapi kini dianggap pemalsuan Lambe yang memakai kisah setempat. Dalam versi Joseph Jacobs, naga itu ditenangkan dengan tujuh sapi per hari.
long_description.en: The prince returns and, rather than fighting the dragon, kisses it three times, and the princess regains her own shape; afterwards he changes the witch-queen into a toad and takes the throne. The ballad was first printed in 1778, supposedly copied by the Reverend Robert Lambe from a Latin manuscript of 1270, but is now thought to be Lambe's forgery drawing on local tales. In Joseph Jacobs's version the dragon is pacified with seven cows a day.

famous_for.en: Stepmother turned toad.

did_you_know.id: Dalam balada ini, sang pangeran memulihkan saudarinya bukan dengan bertarung, melainkan dengan mencium naga itu tiga kali.
did_you_know.en: In this ballad the prince restores his sister not by fighting but by kissing the dragon three times.

short_description.id: Elang berkepala tiga adalah elang mitologis dan heraldik yang muncul dalam kitab apokrif Ezra, dongeng Chechnya, cerita rakyat Yakut, dan heraldik.
short_description.en: The three-headed eagle is a mythological and heraldic eagle found in the apocryphal Ezra, a Chechen fairy tale, Yakut folklore and heraldry.

long_description.id: Elang berkepala tiga adalah elang mitologis atau heraldik, semacam versi tambahan dari elang berkepala dua. Dalam kitab apokrif Ezra Latin, imam besar Ezra memimpikan elang dengan dua belas sayap dan tiga kepala yang naik dari laut. Dalam dongeng Chechnya ia lawan mengerikan yang dibunuh sang pahlawan, dan dalam cerita rakyat Yakut serta Dolgan dikenal elang berkepala dua atau tiga bernama Öksökö.
long_description.en: The three-headed eagle is a mythological or heraldic eagle, an augmented double-headed eagle. In the apocryphal Latin Ezra, the high priest Ezra dreams of an eagle with twelve wings and three heads rising from the sea. In a Chechen fairy tale it is a monstrous foe slain by the hero, and Yakut and Dolgan folklore know a two- or three-headed eagle named Öksökö.

long_description.id: Dalam heraldik ia hewan lambang yang langka: ia menjadi lambang Reinmar von Zweter dalam Codex Manesse (sekitar 1300), dan tongkat kerajaan Tsar Mikhail I dari Rusia dihiasi elang berkepala tiga.
long_description.en: In heraldry it is a rare charge: it serves as the arms of Reinmar von Zweter in the Codex Manesse (c. 1300), and one adorned the sceptre of Tsar Michael I of Russia.

origin.id: Berbagai budaya, dari kitab apokrif hingga cerita rakyat Chechnya dan Yakut.
origin.en: Many cultures, from apocrypha to Chechen and Yakut folklore.

role.id: Lawan mengerikan dalam dongeng dan lambang heraldik.
role.en: A monstrous foe in tales and a heraldic emblem.

famous_for.id: Mimpi Ezra tentang elang dari laut.
famous_for.en: Ezra's dream of the eagle from the sea.

did_you_know.id: Tongkat kerajaan Tsar Mikhail I dihiasi elang berkepala tiga.
did_you_know.en: Tsar Michael I's sceptre bore a three-headed eagle.

note.id: Elang berkepala tiga adalah versi tambahannya.
note.en: The three-headed eagle is its augmented version.

claims.quote: The three-headed eagle, also called triple-headed eagle, is a mythological or heraldic eagle, as it were an augmented version of the double-headed eagle.

statement.id: Elang berkepala tiga adalah elang mitologis atau heraldik, semacam versi tambahan dari elang berkepala dua.
statement.en: The three-headed eagle is a mythological or heraldic eagle, an augmented version of the double-headed eagle.

claims.quote: A three-headed eagle is mentioned in the apocryphal Latin Ezra, featuring in a dream by the high priest Ezra.

statement.id: Elang berkepala tiga disebut dalam kitab apokrif Ezra Latin, dalam mimpi imam besar Ezra.
statement.en: A three-headed eagle appears in the apocryphal Latin Ezra, in a dream of the high priest Ezra.

claims.quote: In a Chechen fairy tale, a three-headed eagle figures as a monstrous adversary to be killed by the hero.

statement.id: Dalam dongeng Chechnya, elang berkepala tiga menjadi lawan mengerikan yang harus dibunuh sang pahlawan.
statement.en: In a Chechen fairy tale a three-headed eagle is a monstrous foe the hero must kill.

claims.quote: Öksökö (Өксөку) is the name of an eagle with either two or three heads in Yakut and Dolgan folklore.

statement.id: Öksökö adalah nama elang berkepala dua atau tiga dalam cerita rakyat Yakut dan Dolgan.
statement.en: Öksökö is an eagle with two or three heads in Yakut and Dolgan folklore.

statement.en: A three-headed eagle is shown as the arms of minnesinger Reinmar von Zweter (c. 1200–1248) in the Codex Manesse (c. 1300).

statement.id: Tongkat kerajaan Tsar Mikhail I dari Rusia dihiasi elang berkepala tiga.
statement.en: The sceptre of Tsar Michael I of Russia was decorated with a three-headed eagle.

claims.quote: Der Dreiköpfige Adler, auch mit Dreifachadler bezeichnet, ist ein seltenes Wappentier in der Heraldik.

statement.id: Dalam heraldik, elang berkepala tiga adalah hewan lambang yang langka.

short_description.id: Tugarin adalah makhluk mitis dalam bylina dan dongeng Rusia yang melambangkan kejahatan dan kekejaman, berwujud mirip naga, dan menjadi lawan Alyosha Popovich.
short_description.en: Tugarin is a mythical being of Russian byliny and fairy tales who embodies evil and cruelty, takes a dragon-like form and opposes Alyosha Popovich.

long_description.id: Dalam bylina dan dongeng Rusia, Tugarin adalah sosok kejam dan jahat yang tampil menyerupai naga. Ia digambarkan sebagai raksasa dan musuh Alyosha Popovich, juga lawan Dobrynya Nikitich. Namanya beragam, antara lain Zmey Tugarin, Zmey Tugaretin, dan Zmeishche Tugarishche.
long_description.en: In Russian byliny and tales Tugarin is a cruel, wicked figure who appears in the likeness of a dragon. He is pictured as a giant and as the foe of Alyosha Popovich, and also of Dobrynya Nikitich. He goes by many names, among them Zmey Tugarin, Zmey Tugaretin and Zmeishche Tugarishche.

long_description.id: Walau disebut naga, ia sebagian besar tetap berwujud manusia dan menunggang kuda. Ia tampak bersayap dan terbang ke udara saat bertarung dengan Alyosha, meski beberapa versi menjelaskan sayap itu sebagai alat dari kertas yang dipasang pada kudanya. Ia juga sangat rakus: mampu menjejalkan satu roti bundar di tiap pipinya lalu menelan seekor angsa utuh.
long_description.en: Though called a dragon, he mostly keeps a human shape and rides a horse. He seems to have wings and rises into the air while fighting Alyosha, though some versions explain the wings away as a paper device fixed to his horse. He is also a huge glutton, able to cram a whole round loaf into each cheek and then swallow a swan whole.

long_description.id: Sebagian pengulas menganggap Tugarin melambangkan unsur api, karena dalam beberapa versi tubuhnya diselimuti ular berapi yang ia pakai sebagai senjata, dan ia mencoba mencekik Alyosha dengan asap. Namanya dikaitkan dengan khan Polovtsia Tugorkan, walau ada etimologi lain dari akar kata tug, "duka".
long_description.en: Some commentators see Tugarin as the element of fire, since in some versions his body is covered with fiery snakes used as weapons and he tries to choke Alyosha with smoke. His name has been tied to the Polovtsian khan Tugorkan, though another etymology derives it from the root tug, "grief".

short_description.id: Turul adalah burung pemangsa mitologis dalam tradisi Hungaria dan Turk, umumnya digambarkan sebagai falkon, dan menjadi lambang nasional bangsa Hungaria.
short_description.en: The Turul is a mythological bird of prey of Hungarian and Turkic tradition, usually shown as a falcon, and a national symbol of the Hungarians.

long_description.id: Turul adalah burung pemangsa mitologis dalam tradisi Hungaria dan Turk yang umumnya digambarkan sebagai falkon, dan kini menjadi lambang nasional bangsa Hungaria. Burung ini kemungkinan besar didasarkan pada falkon besar. Dalam bahasa Hungaria, turul adalah sebutan untuk satu jenis falkon, dan asal katanya kini dianggap paling mungkin dari bahasa Turk, dengan bentuk toġrïl atau toğrul yang berarti burung pemangsa sedang hingga besar dari famili Accipitridae.
long_description.en: The Turul is a mythological bird of prey of Hungarian and Turkic tradition, usually pictured as a falcon, and today a national symbol of the Hungarians. It is probably modelled on a large falcon. In Hungarian, turul named one kind of falcon, and the word is now thought most likely to be of Turkic origin, from toġrïl or toğrul, a medium to large bird of prey of the family Accipitridae.

long_description.id: Dalam legenda Emese yang tercatat dalam Gesta Hungarorum dan Chronicon Pictum, turul muncul dalam mimpi Emese ketika ia sudah hamil. Peran turul di sini adalah roh pelindung yang menjaga bayi Álmos dari bahaya, motif yang sangat mirip dengan peran Simurgh dalam epos Iran Shahnameh. Dalam mimpi kedua pemimpin suku Hungaria, elang-elang lambang bangsa Pecheneg menyerang kuda mereka, lalu turul datang menyelamatkannya.
long_description.en: Both the Gesta Hungarorum and the Chronicon Pictum preserve the tale of Emese, who sees the turul in a dream while already carrying her child. Its role there is that of a guardian spirit shielding the infant Álmos from harm, a motif very close to the Simurgh's role in the Iranian epic Shahnameh. In a second dream of the Hungarian tribal leader, eagles, the emblem of the Pechenegs, attacked their horses and the turul came to rescue them.

long_description.id: Dalam tradisi Hungaria, turul bermula sebagai lambang klan wangsa Árpád yang berkuasa pada abad ke-9 dan ke-10. Gesta Hunnorum et Hungarorum menyebut wangsa itu keturunan klan Turul, dan Gesta Hungarorum mencatat turul sebagai leluhur totemik Árpád. Sepasang cakram perak bermotif turul ditemukan di Rakamaz dari pemakaman Hungaria abad ke-10.
long_description.en: In Hungarian tradition the turul began as the clan emblem of the ruling Árpád dynasty in the 9th and 10th centuries. The Gesta Hunnorum et Hungarorum says the dynasty descended from the Turul clan, and the Gesta Hungarorum records the turul as Árpád's totemic ancestor. A pair of silver discs with a turul motif was found at Rakamaz in a 10th-century Hungarian cemetery.

long_description.id: Kini turul menjadi unsur utama lambang Angkatan Bersenjata Hungaria: burung bersayap terbentang yang mencengkeram pedang Raja Santo Stefanus. Patung turul di sebuah gunung dekat Tatabánya disebut patung burung terbesar di Eropa.
long_description.en: Today the turul is the centrepiece of the Hungarian Defence Forces emblem: a bird with outspread wings gripping the sword of King Saint Stephen. The turul statue on a mountain near Tatabánya is described as the largest bird statue in Europe.

short_description.id: Tzitzimitl adalah dewi langit Aztek yang dikaitkan dengan bintang dan kesuburan, digambarkan sebagai sosok perempuan berwujud kerangka, dan ditakuti saat gerhana matahari.
short_description.en: A Tzitzimitl is an Aztec celestial goddess linked to the stars and fertility, shown as a skeletal female figure and feared during solar eclipses.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Aztek, Tzitzimitl (jamak Tzitzimimeh) adalah dewi langit yang dikaitkan dengan bintang. Mereka digambarkan sebagai perempuan berwujud kerangka yang memakai rok bermotif tengkorak; dalam Codex Magliabechiano roknya berhias kerang. Uraian pascapenaklukan sering menyebut mereka iblis, tetapi sebutan itu belum tentu sesuai dengan fungsi mereka.
long_description.en: In Aztec mythology a Tzitzimitl (plural Tzitzimimeh) is a celestial goddess linked to the stars. They were shown as skeletal women wearing skirts with skull designs; in the Codex Magliabechiano the skirts are edged with shells. Post-conquest accounts often call them demons, but that label does not necessarily match their role.

long_description.id: Tzitzimimeh adalah dewi kesuburan yang dipuja bidan dan perempuan yang akan melahirkan. Pemimpin mereka adalah Itzpapalotl, penguasa surga Tamoanchan. Mereka berperan ganda sebagai pelindung kaum perempuan dan leluhur umat manusia.
long_description.en: The Tzitzimimeh were fertility goddesses worshipped by midwives and women in childbirth. Their leader was Itzpapalotl, ruler of the paradise Tamoanchan. They had a double role as protectors of women and ancestresses of humankind.

long_description.id: Mereka juga ditakuti. Bintang yang tampak saat gerhana matahari ditafsirkan sebagai Tzitzimimeh yang menyerang Matahari dan turun merasuki manusia. Bila upacara api baru di akhir siklus kalender 52 tahun gagal, mereka dipercaya akan memangsa manusia terakhir; mereka juga ditakuti pada lima hari sial Nemontemi.
long_description.en: They were also feared. Stars visible during a solar eclipse were read as Tzitzimimeh attacking the Sun and descending to possess people. If the new-fire rite at the end of the 52-year calendar round failed, they were expected to devour the last people; they were also feared during the five unlucky Nemontemi days.

short_description.id: Uraeus adalah gambaran kobra tegak dalam tradisi Mesir yang melambangkan kekuasaan kerajaan dan otoritas ilahi.
short_description.en: The uraeus is an upright cobra representation in Egyptian tradition symbolizing royal power and divine authority.

long_description.id: Uraeus adalah gambaran kobra tegak dalam tradisi Mesir yang melambangkan kekuasaan kerajaan dan otoritas ilahi. Uraeus merupakan lambang dewi Wadjet.
long_description.en: The uraeus is an upright cobra representation in Egyptian tradition symbolizing royal power and divine authority. The uraeus represents the goddess Wadjet.

long_description.id: Pemakaiannya pada mahkota menandakan perlindungan Wadjet terhadap firaun. Nekhbet dan Wadjet menjadi Dua Nyonya yang menjaga Mesir bersatu. Wadjet, yang dilambangkan uraeus, disebut putri Ra dan tokoh kisah Mata Ra. Ensiklopedia pendamping menyebut uraeus sebagai insignia raja berupa kobra Wadjet yang terangkat.
long_description.en: Its use on the crown signifies Wadjet’s protection of the pharaoh. Nekhbet and Wadjet become the Two Ladies protecting unified Egypt. Wadjet, represented by the uraeus, is described as Ra’s daughter and a figure in Eye of Ra stories. The accompanying encyclopedia calls the uraeus the king’s insignia in the form of Wadjet’s rearing cobra.

short_description.id: Domba Tumbuhan Tartaria adalah tumbuhan legendaris Asia Tengah yang dipercaya berbuah domba hidup yang tersambung lewat tali pusar, legenda yang berakar pada tanaman kapas.
short_description.en: The Vegetable Lamb of Tartary is a legendary plant of Central Asia believed to bear live sheep tied to it by an umbilical cord, a legend rooted in the cotton plant.

long_description.id: Domba Tumbuhan Tartaria atau Agnus scythicus adalah zoofit legendaris Asia Tengah yang dipercaya berbuah domba. Domba itu terhubung ke tumbuhan oleh tangkai seperti tali pusar, merumput di sekitarnya, dan mati bila rumput habis. Ia dipercaya berdarah, bertulang, dan berdaging seperti domba; darahnya manis seperti madu, wolnya dipakai untuk pakaian, dan hanya serigala yang memangsanya.
long_description.en: The Vegetable Lamb of Tartary or Agnus scythicus is a legendary zoophyte of Central Asia believed to bear sheep. The lamb, tied to the plant by a cord-like stalk, grazes around it and dies when the grass runs out. It was thought to have blood, bones and flesh like a lamb; its blood was sweet as honey, its wool made into clothes, and only wolves preyed on it.

long_description.id: Legenda ini berakar pada kapas, yang belum dikenal di Eropa utara; Herodotos sudah menulis tentang pohon berbuah wol di India, dan Yeduah dalam cerita rakyat Yahudi tercatat sejak 436 M. Odorico sekitar 1314 menulis tentang melon yang melahirkan anak domba, Thomas Browne menyebutnya Boramez, dan nama barometz berasal dari kata Tatar untuk anak domba. Pada masa Renaisans ia banyak dibahas dalam teks filsafat dan botani.
long_description.en: The legend is rooted in cotton, then unknown in northern Europe; Herodotus already wrote of wool-bearing trees in India, and the Yeduah of Jewish folklore is recorded from AD 436. Odoric around 1314 wrote of a lamb-bearing melon, Thomas Browne called it the Boramez, and the name barometz comes from the Tatar for little lamb. In the Renaissance it was much discussed in philosophical and botanical texts.

famous_for.en: The lamb on its umbilical stalk.

note.en: A similar plant-animal of Jewish folklore.

statement.en: The Vegetable Lamb of Tartary (Latin Agnus scythicus or Planta Tartarica Barometz) is a legendary zoophyte of Central Asia believed to bear sheep as fruit; the sheep, tied to the plant by an umbilical cord, grazed around it, and when the foliage was gone both died.

short_description.id: Vishap adalah naga dalam mitologi Armenia yang erat kaitannya dengan air, biasanya digambarkan sebagai ular bersayap, dan musuh dewa Vahagn.
short_description.en: The vishap is a dragon of Armenian mythology closely tied to water, usually shown as a winged serpent, and the foe of the god Vahagn.

long_description.id: Vishap adalah naga dalam mitologi Armenia yang erat kaitannya dengan air, mirip Leviatan. Ia biasanya digambarkan sebagai ular bersayap atau gabungan bagian berbagai hewan. Namanya mungkin berasal dari istilah Iran kuno vi-šāpa, "yang bergetah beracun", yang dipakai untuk ular.
long_description.en: In Armenian myth the vishap is a water-linked dragon comparable to the Leviathan. Artists usually show it as a winged snake or as a blend of parts from several animals. Its name may go back to an old Iranian term, vi-šāpa, "having poisonous juices", applied to snakes.

long_description.id: Gunung Ararat adalah kediaman utama vishap; sifat vulkanik puncaknya dan gempa-gempanya mungkin mengilhami kaitan itu. Kadang bersama anak-anaknya, vishap mencuri bayi dan menggantinya dengan roh jahat kecil dari keturunannya sendiri. Menurut kepercayaan kuno, ia naik ke langit atau turun ke bumi sambil menimbulkan badai petir, angin puting, dan menelan matahari sehingga terjadi gerhana.
long_description.en: Mount Ararat was the vishap's chief home, perhaps because of the peak's volcanic nature and earthquakes. Sometimes with its young, the vishap stole infants and left a small evil spirit of its own brood in their place. Ancient belief had it rise to the sky or come down to earth, raising thunderstorms and whirlwinds and swallowing the sun to cause an eclipse.

long_description.id: Di sejumlah negeri Timur naga ini dipuja sebagai lambang air, kesuburan, dan kekayaan, lalu menjadi lambang kekuasaan yang menakutkan. Menurut legenda kuno, ia bertarung dengan Vahagn Pembunuh Naga, dan di Yerevan berdiri patung Vahagn karya Karlen Nurijanyan dan Nerses Charkhchyan.
long_description.en: In several Eastern lands the dragon was worshipped as a symbol of water, fertility and wealth, and it later became a fearsome symbol of power. Ancient legend has it fight Vahagn the Dragon Slayer, and a statue of Vahagn by Karlen Nurijanyan and Nerses Charkhchyan stands in Yerevan.

famous_for.en: It was fought by Vahagn the Dragon Slayer.

short_description.id: Vitore adalah ular ilahi penjaga rumah dalam mitologi Albania, terkait dengan nasib, keberuntungan, jiwa leluhur, dan pemujaan perapian.
short_description.en: Vitore is the divine household serpent of Albanian mythology, linked with fate, good fortune, the ancestors' souls and the cult of the hearth.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi dan cerita rakyat Albania, Vitore adalah ular ilahi penjaga rumah yang terkait dengan nasib manusia, keberuntungan, dan jiwa para leluhur. Ia erat dengan pemujaan perapian dan terutama dianggap pelindung keluarga dan rumah. Namanya ditafsirkan berasal dari kata untuk alat tenun, sehingga berarti "perempuan pemintal", terkait dengan menenun nasib.
long_description.en: In Albanian mythology and folklore Vitore is a divine household serpent linked with human destiny, good fortune and the souls of the ancestors. She is closely tied to the cult of the hearth and is above all the guardian of family and house. Her name is interpreted as coming from the word for a loom, meaning "a woman who spins", linked to the weaving of fate.

long_description.id: Vitorja biasanya digambarkan sebagai ular kecil berwarna-warni bertanduk emas yang baik hati, tetapi dalam sebagian tradisi sebagai perempuan tua. Bila ia tinggal di dinding rumah, ia membawa keberuntungan dan dihormati penghuni, dan desisannya menandakan peristiwa penting keluarga. Ular adalah totem hewan orang Albania, dan siluet ular diukir di dinding dan pintu rumah untuk keberuntungan.
long_description.en: Vitorja is usually described as a small, colourful, benign golden-horned serpent, but in some traditions as an old woman. When she lives in a house's walls she brings luck and is respected by the household, and her whispering announces important family events. The serpent is an animal totem of the Albanians, and snake silhouettes are carved on walls and doors for good fortune.

cultural_context.id: Vitore mencerminkan kepercayaan bahwa jiwa leluhur menjelma dalam ular rumah dan terkait pemujaan perapian; siluet ular diukir di rumah sebagai penangkal mata jahat.
cultural_context.en: Vitore reflects the belief that ancestral souls take form in household serpents, tied to the cult of the hearth; snake silhouettes are carved on houses against the evil eye.

claims.quote: The serpent is an animal totem of the Albanians, especially in the north. The belief of the personification of the souls of the ancestors in household serpents has been handed down from prehistoric times.

statement.id: Ular adalah totem hewan orang Albania, terutama di utara, dan kepercayaan bahwa jiwa leluhur menjelma dalam ular rumah diwariskan sejak zaman prasejarah.
statement.en: The serpent is an animal totem of the Albanians, especially in the north, and the belief that ancestral souls are personified in household serpents has come down from prehistoric times.

claims.quote: Vitorja is usually described as a small, colourful and benign golden horned serpent. However, in some traditions Vitorja is described also as an old woman, a mythological figure similar to Nëna e Vatrës. Vitorja is also identified with Fatia in southern folklore and Ora in central and northern folklore.

statement.id: Vitorja biasanya digambarkan sebagai ular kecil berwarna-warni yang baik hati dan bertanduk emas, tetapi dalam sebagian tradisi juga sebagai perempuan tua mirip Nëna e Vatrës; ia juga disamakan dengan Fatia dalam folklor selatan dan Ora dalam folklor tengah dan utara.
statement.en: Vitorja is usually described as a small, colourful, benign golden-horned serpent, but in some traditions also as an old woman similar to Nëna e Vatrës; she is also identified with Fatia in southern folklore and Ora in central and northern folklore.

claims.quote: The cult of the household serpent is implemented in the Albanian traditional art: the snake silouhette commonly appears carved on the walls and doors of Albanian houses for good fortune and to ward off the evil eye.

statement.id: Pemujaan ular rumah tampak dalam seni tradisional Albania: siluet ular sering diukir di dinding dan pintu rumah untuk keberuntungan dan penangkal mata jahat.
statement.en: The household serpent cult appears in Albanian traditional art: a snake silhouette is often carved on house walls and doors for good fortune and against the evil eye.

claims.quote: Si gjarpër, kur Vitorja banon në muret e një shtëpie, besohet se sjell fat, kështu që banorët e trajtojnë me shumë respekt. Pëshpëritja e saj lajmëron ngjarje të rëndësishme për familjen.

statement.id: Sebagai ular, bila Vitorja tinggal di dinding rumah ia dipercaya membawa keberuntungan sehingga penghuni memperlakukannya dengan sangat hormat, dan desisannya menandakan peristiwa penting bagi keluarga.
statement.en: As a serpent, when Vitorja lives in a house's walls she is believed to bring luck, so the household treats her with great respect, and her whispering announces important family events.

short_description.id: Vodyanoy adalah roh air dalam mitologi Slavia, biasanya lelaki tua berjanggut hijau yang bisa menenggelamkan orang, tetapi juga dapat memberi tangkapan ikan berlimpah.
short_description.en: The vodyanoy is a water spirit of Slavic mythology, usually an old man with a green beard who may drown people but can also grant rich catches of fish.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Slavia, vodyanoy (secara harfiah "yang dari air") adalah roh air. Dalam dongeng Ceko dan Slowakia ia disebut vodník, dan dalam dongeng Ukraina vodyanyk; di Rusia ia kadang dijuluki dedushka vodyanoy, "Kakek Air". Ia dikatakan tinggal di lubuk atau pusaran sungai, kolam, atau danau, dan terutama suka hidup di dekat kincir air.
long_description.en: In Slavic mythology the vodyanoy (literally "he from the water") is a water spirit. Czech and Slovak fairy tales call him vodník, Ukrainian ones vodyanyk; in Russia he is sometimes called dedushka vodyanoy, "Water-Grandfather". He is said to live in a deep pool or whirlpool of a river, pond or lake, and to favour spots near a watermill.

long_description.id: Rupanya digambarkan berbeda-beda: lelaki telanjang berperut buncit dan berkepala botak bertopi dan bersabuk alang-alang, lelaki tua berambut dan berjanggut hijau, atau katak yang menyerupai manusia; perbedaan ini dijelaskan oleh kemampuannya berubah wujud. Janggut hijaunya memutih saat bulan menyusut, karena ia yang abadi menua atau menjadi muda lagi mengikuti fase bulan. Ia dapat muncul sebagai ikan raksasa berlumut, sebatang kayu, bahkan batang pohon bersayap kecil yang terbang di atas air.
long_description.en: Accounts of his looks differ: a naked, pot-bellied, bald man with a hat and belt of reeds, an old man with green hair and beard, or a man-like frog; the variety is put down to his shapeshifting. His green beard whitens as the moon wanes, since the immortal vodyanoy ages or grows young with the moon's phases. He may appear as a huge mossy fish, a log, or even a small-winged flying tree trunk skimming the water.

long_description.id: Saat marah ia menjebol bendungan, menghanyutkan kincir air, dan menenggelamkan manusia serta hewan, sehingga nelayan, penggiling, dan peternak lebah memberinya persembahan; kadang ia menyeret orang ke rumahnya di bawah air untuk dijadikan budak. Ketika kincir air dibangun, harus dikorbankan babi, sapi, domba, bahkan manusia atau ayam untuk menenangkannya. Sebaliknya, nelayan bisa mendapat tangkapan berlimpah darinya, misalnya setelah mengembalikan seorang anak yang tak sengaja terjaring.
long_description.en: When angry he breaks dams, washes away mills and drowns people and animals, so fishermen, millers and bee-keepers offer him sacrifices; at times he drags people to his underwater home as slaves. When a watermill was built, a pig, cattle, a sheep, even a human or a chicken had to be sacrificed to calm him. Fishermen, on the other hand, could receive bountiful catches from him, for instance after returning a child caught by accident in their nets.

long_description.id: Vodyanoy menguasai semua ikan dan makhluk air, dan ia memilih ikan lele besar sebagai tunggangan. Ia mengambil istri dari peri air atau gadis-gadis malang yang tenggelam, termasuk rusalka menurut Afanasyev. Ada pula penguasa para vodyanoy, Tsar Vodyanik, lelaki tua bersenjata gada yang bisa naik ke langit di atas awan hitam dan menciptakan sungai serta danau baru.
long_description.en: The vodyanoy owns all fish and water creatures and chooses the wels catfish as his mount. He takes wives from water-nymphs or drowned, unhappy girls, including the rusalka according to Afanasyev. The vodyanoys also have a ruler, the Tsar Vodyanik, an old man with a club who can rise to the sky on a black cloud and create new rivers and lakes.

claims.quote: In Slavic mythology, vodyanoy (Russian: водяной , IPA ... lit. '[he] from the water' or 'watery') is a water spirit. In Czech and Slovak fairy tales, he is called vodník (or in Germanized form: Hastrman ), and often referred to as Wassermann in German sources. In Ukrainian fairy tales, he is called “водяник“ (vodyanyk).

statement.id: Dalam mitologi Slavia, vodyanoy (водяной, harfiah "yang dari air" atau "berair") adalah roh air; dalam dongeng Ceko dan Slowakia ia disebut vodník (Hastrman), dan dalam dongeng Ukraina vodyanyk.
statement.en: In Slavic mythology the vodyanoy (водяной, literally "he from the water" or "watery") is a water spirit; Czech and Slovak tales call him vodník (Hastrman), Ukrainian tales vodyanyk.

claims.quote: He may appear to be a naked man with a pot belly (and bald-headed) wearing a hat and belt of reeds and rushes, conflicting with other accounts ascribing him green hair and a long green beard, while many depictions restore him as an anthropormophic frog. The varying look has been attributed in commentary to his shape-shifting ability.

statement.id: Ia bisa tampil sebagai lelaki telanjang berperut buncit dan botak bertopi serta bersabuk alang-alang, sementara kisah lain memberinya rambut hijau dan janggut hijau panjang, dan banyak penggambaran menjadikannya katak berwujud manusia; perbedaan ini dikaitkan dengan kemampuannya berubah wujud.
statement.en: He may appear as a naked, pot-bellied, bald man with a hat and belt of reeds, while other accounts give him green hair and a long green beard and many depictions show him as a man-like frog; the variety is attributed to his shape-shifting.

claims.quote: When angered, the vodyanoy breaks dams, washes down water mills, and drowns people and animals. Consequently, fishermen, millers, and also bee-keepers make sacrifices to appease him. The vodyanoy would sometimes drag people down to his underwater dwelling to serve him as slaves.

statement.id: Saat marah, vodyanoy menjebol bendungan, menghanyutkan kincir air, dan menenggelamkan manusia serta hewan, sehingga nelayan, penggiling, dan peternak lebah memberinya persembahan; kadang ia menyeret orang ke kediamannya di bawah air untuk dijadikan budak.
statement.en: When angered the vodyanoy breaks dams, washes away mills and drowns people and animals, so fishermen, millers and bee-keepers sacrifice to appease him; he sometimes drags people to his underwater dwelling as slaves.

claims.quote: In Russia, the vodyanoy is sometimes called the dedushka vodyanoy (Дѣдушка-водяной , "Water-Grandfather") or vodyanik (водяник ).

statement.id: Di Rusia vodyanoy kadang disebut dedushka vodyanoy ("Kakek Air") atau vodyanik.
statement.en: In Russia the vodyanoy is sometimes called dedushka vodyanoy ("Water-Grandfather") or vodyanik.

claims.quote: He is said to dwell in a slough (омут ), kettle hole (Котловина ), or a whirlpool of a river, pond or lake, and liked especially to live near a watermill.

statement.id: Ia dikatakan tinggal di lubuk, cekungan, atau pusaran sungai, kolam, atau danau, dan terutama suka tinggal di dekat kincir air.
statement.en: He is said to dwell in a slough, kettle hole or whirlpool of a river, pond or lake, and especially liked to live near a watermill.

claims.quote: He has the capability of shape-shifting, which has been suggested as an explanation of its varied descriptions.

statement.id: Ia mampu berubah wujud, dan hal ini diajukan sebagai penjelasan atas gambaran rupanya yang beragam.
statement.en: He can shape-shift, which has been suggested to explain his varied descriptions.

claims.quote: When a watermill is built, a sacrifice of pig, cattle, sheep, or even human (or a chicken) must be made to appease the vodyanik.

statement.id: Ketika kincir air dibangun, harus dipersembahkan babi, sapi, domba, bahkan manusia (atau ayam) untuk menenangkan vodyanik.
statement.en: When a watermill is built, a pig, cattle, sheep or even a human (or a chicken) must be sacrificed to appease the vodyanik.

claims.quote: The fisherman can also benefit from the boon of the vodyanoy, receiving a bountiful harvest in their fishing nets. He may receive this reward after returning a child which was accidentally netted.

statement.id: Nelayan juga bisa mendapat anugerah vodyanoy berupa tangkapan berlimpah di jaringnya, misalnya setelah mengembalikan anak yang tak sengaja terjaring.
statement.en: A fisherman can also gain the vodyanoy's boon of a bountiful catch, for example after returning a child accidentally netted.

claims.quote: The vodyanik "owns" all the fish and aquatic creatures, and his control over them explains his ability to deliver fish. The vodyanik selects in particular the sheatfish (сом ; Silurus glanis, aka "wels catfish") as his mount to ride on.

statement.id: Vodyanik "memiliki" semua ikan dan makhluk air, dan kuasa itu menjelaskan kemampuannya memberi ikan; ia terutama memilih ikan lele besar (wels catfish) sebagai tunggangan.
statement.en: The vodyanik "owns" all fish and aquatic creatures, which explains his ability to deliver fish; he especially chooses the wels catfish as his mount.

claims.quote: He is known to take on a wife (or wives), and espouses "water-nymphs or drowned and unhappy girls who have been cursed by their fathers or mothers". According to Afanasyev, the "water-nymph" ("water-maiden") is known by various names in Russia, including the rusalka.

statement.id: Ia beristri satu atau lebih, yaitu peri air atau gadis malang yang tenggelam dan dikutuk ayah atau ibunya; menurut Afanasyev, peri air itu dikenal di Rusia dengan berbagai nama, termasuk rusalka.
statement.en: He takes a wife or wives: water-nymphs or drowned, unhappy girls cursed by their parents; according to Afanasyev the water-nymph is known in Russia by various names, including rusalka.

claims.quote: It is believed that vodyanoys have a ruler: the Tsar Vodyanik, or the Vodyan Tsar. He is described as an old man armed with a club, who can rise to the sky sitting on a black cloud and create new rivers and lakes.

statement.id: Para vodyanoy dipercaya punya penguasa, Tsar Vodyanik, lelaki tua bersenjata gada yang dapat naik ke langit di atas awan hitam dan menciptakan sungai serta danau baru.
statement.en: Vodyanoys are believed to have a ruler, the Tsar Vodyanik, an old man with a club who can rise to the sky on a black cloud and create new rivers and lakes.

claims.quote: The farmer fording his livestock will make a sign of cross (emblem of Perun's weapon) over the river as protection from this happening.

statement.id: Petani yang menyeberangkan ternaknya membuat tanda salib di atas sungai sebagai perlindungan agar ternaknya tidak ditunggangi vodyanik.
statement.en: A farmer fording his livestock makes a sign of the cross over the river as protection against this.

claims.quote: He is also described as an old man with green hair and (long) green beard The green beard turns white with when the moon wanes, as the immortal Vodyanoy ages or rejuvenates with the phases of the moon.

statement.id: Ia juga digambarkan sebagai lelaki tua berambut dan berjanggut hijau panjang; janggutnya memutih saat bulan menyusut, karena vodyanoy yang abadi menua atau menjadi muda lagi mengikuti fase bulan.
statement.en: He is also described as an old man with green hair and a long green beard, which whitens as the moon wanes, as the immortal vodyanoy ages or rejuvenates with the moon's phases.

claims.quote: He can appear as a giant moss-covered fish, a log or even a flying tree-trunk with small-wings, skimming over the water's surface.

statement.id: Ia dapat muncul sebagai ikan raksasa berlumut, sebatang kayu, bahkan batang pohon terbang bersayap kecil yang meluncur di atas permukaan air.
statement.en: He can appear as a giant moss-covered fish, a log or even a small-winged flying tree trunk skimming the water.

claims.quote: The Czech and Slovak vodníci (plural of vodník) can also take on an appearance of ordinary humans, but often with water dripping from their clothing, which makes their false identity easily discernable.

statement.id: Vodník Ceko dan Slowakia juga bisa tampil sebagai manusia biasa, tetapi pakaiannya sering meneteskan air sehingga penyamarannya mudah dikenali.
statement.en: Czech and Slovak vodníci can also look like ordinary humans, but water often drips from their clothes, making the disguise easy to spot.

claims.quote: Vodyanoy dipercaya sebagai penyebab orang tenggelam.

statement.id: Vodyanoy dipercaya menjadi penyebab orang tenggelam.
statement.en: The vodyanoy was believed to cause people to drown.

short_description.id: Water horse (kuda air) adalah makhluk mitos yang muncul dalam berbagai bentuk dalam cerita rakyat Kelt dan Nordik, seperti kelpie, each-uisge, dan bäckahästen.
short_description.en: The water horse is a mythical creature found in many forms in Celtic and Nordic folklore, such as the kelpie, each-uisge and bäckahästen.

long_description.id: Water horse (juga waterhorse) adalah makhluk mitos yang muncul dalam berbagai bentuk dalam cerita rakyat Kelt (Celtic) dan Nordik (Nordic). Wujud dalam tradisi Kelt antara lain Ceffyl Dŵr dari Wales (Welsh), each uisce dari Irlandia (Irish), serta each-uisge dan kelpie dari Skotlandia (Scottish). Dalam cerita rakyat Nordik, kuda air adalah wujud yang diambil nixie, yang dalam bahasa Swedia (Swedish) disebut bäckahästen ("kuda sungai kecil") dan dalam bahasa Faroe (Faroese) nykur.
long_description.en: The water horse (also waterhorse) is a mythical being appearing in many guises in Celtic and Nordic folklore. Celtic forms include the Welsh Ceffyl Dŵr, the Irish each uisce, and the Scottish each-uisge and kelpie. In Nordic lore the water horse is a shape the nixie takes, called bäckahästen ('the brook horse') in Swedish and nykur in Faroese.

long_description.id: Istilah "water horse" mulanya nama bagi kelpie, dan juga dipakai sebagai julukan monster danau seperti Ogopogo dan Nessie. Penggunaan "water horse" dan "kelpie" sering membingungkan: sebagian menganggapnya sinonim, sementara yang lain membedakan kuda air sebagai penghuni danau (loch) dan kelpie sebagai penghuni air deras seperti sungai, arungan, dan air terjun. Menurut artikel de, kuda air dikenal dari berbagai budaya dan zaman, termasuk Denmark, Yunani, Irlandia, dan Portugal, dan gagasan roh sungai berwujud kuda mungkin berasal dari kurban kuda di perairan.
long_description.en: 'Water horse' was first a name for the kelpie and has also served as a nickname for lake monsters such as Ogopogo and Nessie. The terms 'water horse' and 'kelpie' are easily confused: some treat them as the same, while others make the water horse a dweller of lochs and the kelpie a creature of rough water such as rivers, fords and waterfalls. According to the de article water horses are known from many cultures and eras, including Denmark, Greece, Ireland and Portugal, and the idea of horse-shaped river spirits may go back to sacrificing horses in water.

famous_for.en: Shape of the nixie.

did_you_know.id: Gagasan roh sungai berwujud kuda mungkin berasal dari praktik kuno mengorbankan kuda di perairan.
did_you_know.en: The idea of horse-shaped river spirits may go back to the ancient practice of sacrificing horses in water.

short_description.id: Naga Wawel (Smok Wawelski) adalah naga terkenal dalam legenda Polandia yang tinggal di gua di bawah Bukit Wawel dan meneror kota Kraków sampai dibunuh dengan umpan berisi belerang.
short_description.en: The Wawel Dragon (Smok Wawelski) is a famous dragon of Polish legend who lived in a cave beneath Wawel Hill and plagued Kraków until killed with a sulfur-filled bait.

long_description.id: Naga Wawel adalah naga terkenal dalam legenda Polandia. Kisah tertua tentangnya berasal dari abad ke-13, dalam karya yang dikaitkan dengan Wincenty Kadłubek. Menurut catatan itu, naga pemakan manusia tersebut mengganggu kota Kraków yang didirikan Raja Krak, dan ditenangkan dengan jatah ternak setiap minggu.
long_description.en: The Wawel Dragon is a famous dragon of Polish legend. The oldest known telling dates from the 13th century, in a work attributed to Wincenty Kadłubek. In that account the man-eating beast troubled the city of Kraków founded by King Krak and was kept calm with a weekly share of cattle.

long_description.id: Dalam versi tertua, putra-putra raja mengalahkannya dengan memberinya kulit sapi berisi belerang yang membara sehingga naga mati terbakar; lalu putra yang lebih muda membunuh kakaknya agar mendapat pujian sendirian, dan akhirnya diusir. Kronik abad ke-15 karya Jan Długosz menukar peran kedua pangeran dan menyebut Raja Krak sendiri sebagai perancang siasat; naga itu menyemburkan api sesaat sebelum mati.
long_description.en: In the oldest version the king's sons defeat it by feeding it a cattle skin packed with smouldering sulfur, so the dragon dies in flames; the younger son then kills his brother to take all the credit and is later banished. Jan Długosz's 15th-century chronicle swaps the princes' roles and credits King Krak himself with the plan; the dragon breathes fire just before it dies.

long_description.id: Kronika Polska karya Marcin Bielski (1597) memberi jasa itu kepada Skub atau Skuba, seorang tukang sepatu. Dalam versi ini naga tidak dapat menelan umpan belerang dan terus minum air sampai mati, lalu si tukang sepatu diberi hadiah besar. Versi populer lain menyebut seorang magang tukang sepatu bernama Dratewka yang mengisi bangkai domba dengan belerang; naga minum di Sungai Vistula sampai perutnya pecah, dan Dratewka menikahi putri raja.
long_description.en: Marcin Bielski's Kronika Polska (1597) gives the credit to Skub or Skuba, a cobbler. In this version the dragon cannot swallow the sulfur bait and drinks water until it dies, and the shoemaker is richly rewarded. Another popular version names a young shoemaker's apprentice, Dratewka, who stuffs a dead lamb with sulfur; the dragon drinks from the Vistula until its belly bursts, and Dratewka marries the king's daughter.

long_description.id: Naga itu dikatakan tinggal di Smocza Jama, gua naga di bawah Bukit Wawel di tepi Sungai Vistula. Dalam kebanyakan versi populer, ia lebih suka memangsa gadis muda dan hanya bisa ditenangkan dengan persembahan seorang gadis setiap bulan. Pada tahun 1970 sebuah patung logam naga ini karya Bronisław Chromy dipasang di depan gua; patung itu menyemburkan api dari lubang hidungnya.
long_description.en: The dragon is said to have lived in Smocza Jama, the dragon's cave beneath Wawel Hill on the banks of the Vistula. In most popular versions it preferred to eat young girls and could only be soothed by a monthly offering of a girl. In 1970 a metal sculpture of the dragon by Bronisław Chromy was set up before the cave; it breathes fire from its nostrils.

short_description.id: Volkolak adalah manusia serigala dalam mitologi Slavia: penyihir yang sengaja menjadi serigala, orang yang terlahir atau dikutuk berubah wujud, dan korban sihir.
short_description.en: The volkolak is the werewolf of Slavic mythology: a sorcerer who becomes a wolf at will, a person born or cursed to shapeshift, or a victim of witchcraft.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Slavia, manusia serigala atau volkolak adalah manusia yang untuk sementara berwujud serigala; ia tampak seperti serigala biasa, tetap berakal manusia, tetapi tidak dapat berbicara. Kepercayaan ini kuno dan dikenal di semua bangsa Slavia, paling rinci di Belarus, Polandia, dan Ukraina; di Rusia istilah volkolak hanya tercatat di selatan, dan Slavia Selatan mencampurnya dengan vampir.
long_description.en: In Slavic mythology the werewolf or volkolak is a person who temporarily becomes a wolf; it looks like an ordinary wolf and keeps a human mind but cannot speak. The belief is ancient and known to all Slavic peoples, most fully among Belarusians, Poles and Ukrainians; among Russians the word volkolak is recorded only in the south, and South Slavic beliefs merge it with the vampire.

long_description.id: Penyihir menjadi serigala dengan mantra dan dengan melompati atau berguling melewati benda bertuah, misalnya pisau yang ditancapkan ke tanah, lalu kembali dengan mengulang secara terbalik. Ada pula yang terlahir atau dikutuk berubah wujud berkala, tidak terkendali dan menyerang ternak serta orang. Korban sihir, seperti rombongan pernikahan dalam kisah populer, menderita dan merindukan hidup manusia.
long_description.en: Sorcerers become wolves by spells and by leaping or tumbling over charmed objects such as knives stuck in the ground, returning by doing it in reverse. Others are born or cursed to change periodically, uncontrolled and attacking livestock and people. Victims of witchcraft, like the wedding party of a popular tale, suffer and long for human life.

long_description.id: Mitos ini mungkin berakar pada kepercayaan totem dan ritus inisiasi pemuda.
long_description.en: The myth may be rooted in totemic beliefs and youth initiation rites.

who.en: A person who turns into a wolf.

description.id: Dengan mantra dan melompati benda bertuah.
description.en: Through spells and leaping over charmed objects.

description.id: Penyihir yang sengaja menjadi serigala untuk mencelakai orang.
description.en: A sorcerer who becomes a wolf on purpose to do harm.

description.id: Orang yang lahir cenderung berubah wujud karena perbuatan orang tua atau dosanya sendiri.
description.en: A person born prone to shapeshifting through parents' deeds or their own sins.

description.id: Orang yang diubah menjadi serigala oleh penyihir sebagai balas dendam.
description.en: A person turned into a wolf by a witch in revenge.

summary.id: Dalam kisah populer, seorang penyihir mengubah seluruh rombongan pernikahan menjadi serigala.
summary.en: In a popular tale a sorcerer turns a whole wedding party into wolves.

claims.quote: In Slavic mythology, a werewolf is a human-shapeshifter who temporarily takes the form of a wolf. Werewolves were often described as ordinary wolves, though some accounts noted peculiarities in appearance or behavior that hinted at their human origin. Werewolves retain human intelligence but cannot speak.

statement.id: Dalam mitologi Slavia, manusia serigala adalah manusia pengubah wujud yang untuk sementara berwujud serigala; ia sering digambarkan seperti serigala biasa dengan beberapa keanehan yang menandakan asal manusianya, tetap berakal manusia tetapi tidak dapat berbicara.
statement.en: In Slavic mythology a werewolf is a human shapeshifter who temporarily takes wolf form; often described as an ordinary wolf with some oddities betraying its human origin, it keeps human intelligence but cannot speak.

claims.quote: The concept is ancient and appears to varying degrees among all Slavic peoples, with the most detailed accounts among Belarusians, Poles, and Ukrainians. In Russian folklore, the character is often simply called a shapeshifter, sharing clear similarities with the werewolf.

statement.id: Konsep ini kuno dan dikenal di semua bangsa Slavia, paling rinci di kalangan orang Belarus, Polandia, dan Ukraina; dalam cerita rakyat Rusia tokoh ini sering disebut pengubah wujud saja.
statement.en: The idea is ancient and found among all Slavic peoples, most fully among Belarusians, Poles and Ukrainians; in Russian folklore the figure is often simply called a shapeshifter.

claims.quote: Among Russians, the term volkolak is recorded only in southern regions

statement.id: Di kalangan orang Rusia, istilah volkolak hanya tercatat di wilayah selatan.
statement.en: Among Russians the term volkolak is recorded only in southern regions.

claims.quote: Ваўкалак, ваўкалака — чалавек, ператвораны ў ваўка, пярэварацень.

statement.id: Dalam bahasa Belarus, vaŭkalak atau vaŭkalaka adalah manusia yang diubah menjadi serigala, sang pengubah wujud.
statement.en: In Belarusian, the vaŭkalak or vaŭkalaka is a person turned into a wolf, a shapeshifter.

claims.quote: It was believed that sorcerers could transform into wolves by reciting spells and performing actions such as leaping, stepping over, tumbling through, or passing through magically imbued objects, or draping them over themselves.

statement.id: Penyihir dipercaya dapat menjadi serigala dengan membaca mantra lalu melompati, melangkahi, berguling melewati, atau menerobos benda bertuah, atau menyampirkannya ke tubuh.
statement.en: Sorcerers were believed to turn into wolves by reciting spells and leaping over, stepping over, tumbling through or passing through charmed objects, or draping them over themselves.

claims.quote: To revert to human form, sorcerers typically needed to repeat the actions in reverse. Sorcerers voluntarily became werewolves to cause harm to others.

statement.id: Untuk kembali menjadi manusia, penyihir mengulang tindakan itu secara terbalik; mereka menjadi manusia serigala dengan sengaja untuk mencelakai orang lain.
statement.en: To turn back into humans, sorcerers repeated the actions in reverse; they became werewolves on purpose to harm others.

claims.quote: Ператварэнне па ўласнай волі адбываецца шляхам перакульвання праз уторкнутыя вастрыём уверх у зямлю нажы (іх колькасць у розных паданнях падаецца ад аднаго да дванаццаці — 1, 5, 7, 12).

statement.id: Menurut kepercayaan Belarus, perubahan sukarela dilakukan dengan berjungkir balik melewati pisau yang ditancapkan ke tanah dengan ujung ke atas, berjumlah antara 1 dan 12 menurut versinya (1, 5, 7, 12).
statement.en: In Belarusian belief, a willed change is made by somersaulting over knives stuck point-up in the ground, from one to twelve in different tales (1, 5, 7, 12).

claims.quote: Some beliefs described people born with a predisposition to periodic shapeshifting due to their parents' actions or as punishment for their own sins. Such werewolves were thought to exhibit zoomorphic traits in human form, such as hair resembling wolf fur.

statement.id: Sebagian kepercayaan menyebut orang yang sejak lahir cenderung berubah wujud secara berkala karena perbuatan orang tuanya atau sebagai hukuman atas dosanya sendiri; dalam wujud manusia mereka punya ciri hewan seperti rambut mirip bulu serigala.
statement.en: Some beliefs told of people born prone to periodic shapeshifting because of their parents' deeds or as punishment for their own sins; in human form they showed animal traits such as wolf-like hair.

claims.quote: These werewolves were believed to lack control in wolf form, attacking livestock and even humans, including loved ones, and were sometimes associated with cannibalism. Ancient beliefs linked werewolves to celestial events like eclipses.

statement.id: Manusia serigala jenis ini dipercaya tidak dapat mengendalikan diri dalam wujud serigala, menyerang ternak bahkan manusia, termasuk orang terkasih, dan kadang dikaitkan dengan kanibalisme; kepercayaan kuno juga mengaitkannya dengan gerhana.
statement.en: Such werewolves were thought to lose control in wolf form, attacking livestock and even people, loved ones included, and were sometimes tied to cannibalism; ancient beliefs also linked them with eclipses.

claims.quote: Folk beliefs also held that sorcerers or witches could transform a person into a wolf, often as an act of revenge, by casting spells on a wolf skin, belt, or enchanted door, among other methods. A popular narrative involved transforming an entire wedding party into wolves.

statement.id: Penyihir laki-laki atau perempuan juga dipercaya dapat mengubah seseorang menjadi serigala, sering sebagai balas dendam, dengan memantrai kulit serigala, sabuk, atau pintu; kisah populer menceritakan seluruh rombongan pernikahan diubah menjadi serigala.
statement.en: Sorcerers or witches were also believed able to turn a person into a wolf, often in revenge, by bewitching a wolf skin, a belt or a door; a popular tale has a whole wedding party turned into wolves.

claims.quote: Involuntary werewolves suffered fear and despair, longing for human life and avoiding true wolves. They were thought to avoid carrion and raw meat, subsisting on foraged food or stolen human provisions.

statement.id: Manusia serigala yang terpaksa menderita ketakutan dan putus asa, merindukan hidup sebagai manusia, menjauhi serigala sejati, dan menghindari bangkai serta daging mentah.
statement.en: Involuntary werewolves suffered fear and despair, longed for human life, avoided real wolves and shunned carrion and raw meat.

claims.quote: The myth likely originated from ancient totemic beliefs and rites of youthful initiation. The werewolf image may have been influenced by observations of people with physical or mental disorders or of old and sick wolves.

statement.id: Mitos ini kemungkinan berasal dari kepercayaan totem kuno dan ritus inisiasi pemuda, dan citranya mungkin dipengaruhi pengamatan terhadap orang dengan gangguan fisik atau jiwa atau serigala tua dan sakit.
statement.en: The myth probably grew from ancient totemic beliefs and youth initiation rites, and its image may reflect observations of people with physical or mental disorders or of old, sick wolves.

claims.quote: Южнославянские представления смешивают волколаков с упырями (вампирами).

statement.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Rusia, kepercayaan Slavia Selatan mencampuradukkan volkolak dengan upir (vampir).
statement.en: According to the Russian article, South Slavic beliefs conflate volkolaks with upirs (vampires).

short_description.id: Naga putih (Y Ddraig Wen) adalah lambang dalam mitologi Wales yang dikaitkan dengan bangsa Anglo-Saxon, musuh naga merah bangsa Briton.
short_description.en: The white dragon (Y Ddraig Wen) is a symbol of Welsh myth associated with the Anglo-Saxons, foe of the red dragon of the Britons.

long_description.id: Naga putih (Wales/Welsh: Y Ddraig Wen) adalah lambang dalam mitologi Wales yang dikaitkan dengan bangsa Anglo-Saxon. Penggunaan tertuanya sebagai lambang Anglo-Saxon terdapat dalam Historia Brittonum: di Dinas Emrys, raja Briton Vortigern mencoba membangun benteng, tetapi setiap malam temboknya runtuh. Seorang anak tanpa ayah memberi tahu raja tentang dua naga di bawah bukit; setelah digali, keduanya bertarung dan naga merah akhirnya mengalahkan naga putih. Anak itu menjelaskan bahwa naga putih melambangkan bangsa Saxon dan naga merah bangsa Briton (Celtic Britons).
long_description.en: The white dragon (Welsh Y Ddraig Wen) is a symbol in Welsh myth tied to the Anglo-Saxons. Its earliest use as their emblem is in the Historia Brittonum: at Dinas Emrys the British king Vortigern tries to build a fort, but every night its walls fall down. A fatherless boy tells the king of two dragons under the hill; once dug up they fight, and the red dragon finally defeats the white. The boy explains that the white dragon stands for the Saxons and the red for the Celtic Britons.

long_description.id: Kisah ini diulang dalam History of the Kings of Britain karya Geoffrey of Monmouth (sekitar 1136), yang menjadikan anak itu Merlin muda; Historia Brittonum dan karya Geoffrey adalah satu-satunya teks abad pertengahan yang memakai naga putih sebagai lambang bangsa Inggris. Kisah serupa naga putih dan merah juga ada dalam Lludd and Llefelys, tanpa makna Briton atau Saxon. Dalam terjemahan Giles atas Geoffrey (Old English Chronicles, Gutenberg), Merlin bernubuat: "celakalah naga merah", karena sarangnya akan direbut naga putih, "yang melambangkan bangsa Saxon".
long_description.en: The story is retold in Geoffrey of Monmouth's History of the Kings of Britain (c. 1136), where the boy becomes the young Merlin; the Historia Brittonum and Geoffrey are the only medieval texts using the white dragon as a symbol of the English. A similar tale of white and red dragons appears in Lludd and Llefelys, without the Briton or Saxon meaning. In Giles's translation of Geoffrey (Old English Chronicles, Gutenberg), Merlin prophesies 'woe to the red dragon', whose lairs the white dragon, 'which signifies the Saxons', will seize.

famous_for.en: Merlin's prophecy.

did_you_know.id: Dalam Historia Brittonum, dua naga ditemukan di bawah bukit Dinas Emrys, menjelaskan mengapa tembok benteng Vortigern selalu runtuh.
did_you_know.en: In the Historia Brittonum two dragons found under the hill of Dinas Emrys explained why Vortigern's fort walls kept falling.

description.id: Bukit tempat dua naga ditemukan.
description.en: Hill where the dragons were found.

note.en: The red dragon, foe of the white.

claims.quote: The white dragon (Welsh: Y Ddraig Wen ) is a symbol associated in Welsh mythology with the Anglo-Saxons. Origin of tradition [edit] The earliest usage of the white dragon as a symbol of the Anglo-Saxons is found in the Historia Brittonum.

statement.id: Naga putih (Wales/Welsh: Y Ddraig Wen) lambang mitologi Wales untuk Anglo-Saxon; tertua dalam Historia Brittonum; di Britania Raya.
statement.en: The white dragon (Welsh Y Ddraig Wen) is a Welsh symbol of the Anglo-Saxons; earliest in the Historia Brittonum.

claims.quote: The boy tells the king of the two dragons. Vortigern excavates the hill, freeing the dragons. They continue their fight and the red dragon finally defeats the white dragon. The boy tells Vortigern that the white dragon symbolises the Saxons and that the red dragon symbolises the Celtic Britons.

statement.id: Di Dinas Emrys, Vortigern (raja Briton, Britons) menggali bukit; naga merah (Welsh dragon) mengalahkan naga putih; putih = Saxon (Saxons), merah = Briton (Celtic Britons).
statement.en: At Dinas Emrys Vortigern digs up the hill; the red dragon defeats the white; white = Saxons, red = Celtic Britons.

claims.quote: The story is repeated in Geoffrey of Monmouth's fictional History of the Kings of Britain (c. 1136). In this telling the boy is identified as the young Merlin. The Historia Brittonum and History of the Kings of Britain are the only medieval texts to use the white dragon as a symbol of the English.

statement.id: Diulang Geoffrey of Monmouth (History of the Kings of Britain, sekitar 1136), anak itu Merlin; satu-satunya teks abad pertengahan, lambang bangsa Inggris (English).
statement.en: Retold by Geoffrey of Monmouth (History of the Kings of Britain, c. 1136) with the boy as Merlin; the only medieval texts using it for the English.

claims.quote: A similar story of white and red dragons fighting is found in the medieval romance Lludd and Llefelys, although in this case the dragons are not used to symbolize Britons or Saxons.

statement.id: Kisah serupa dalam Lludd and Llefelys, tanpa makna Briton (Britons) atau Saxon (Saxons).
statement.en: A similar story in Lludd and Llefelys, without Briton or Saxon meaning.

claims.quote: the two serpents are two dragons; the red serpent is your dragon, but the white serpent is the dragon of the people who occupy several provinces and districts of Britain, even almost from sea to sea

statement.id: Terjemahan Giles atas Nennius: ular putih naga bangsa yang menduduki Britania (Britain); ular merah naga raja.
statement.en: Giles's translation of Nennius: the white serpent is the dragon of the people occupying Britain; the red is the king's.

claims.quote: "Woe to the red dragon, for his banishment hasteneth on. His lurking holes shall be seized by the white dragon, which signifies the Saxons whom you invited over; but the red denotes the British nation, which shall be oppressed by the white.

statement.id: Nubuat Merlin (Old English Chronicles, Gutenberg; Giles): celakalah naga merah (Woe to the red dragon); naga putih melambangkan Saxon (Saxons).
statement.en: Merlin's prophecy (Giles): woe to the red dragon; the white dragon signifies the Saxons.

short_description.id: Wild haggis adalah makhluk rekaan jenaka dalam cerita rakyat Skotlandia, konon asli Dataran Tinggi Skotlandia dan menjadi sumber hidangan haggis.
short_description.en: The wild haggis is a humorous fictional creature of Scottish folklore, said to be native to the Highlands and the source of the dish haggis.

long_description.id: Wild haggis (dengan nama taksonomi jenaka Haggis scoticus) adalah makhluk rekaan cerita rakyat Skotlandia (Scottish folklore) yang konon asli Dataran Tinggi Skotlandia (Scottish Highlands). Secara bercanda ia diklaim sebagai sumber haggis, hidangan tradisional Skotlandia yang sebenarnya dibuat dari jeroan domba seperti jantung, paru-paru, dan hati. Menurut sebagian sumber, kaki kiri dan kanannya berbeda panjang, seperti sidehill gouger dan dahu, sehingga ia dapat berlari cepat mengelilingi gunung dan lereng terjal habitatnya, tetapi hanya ke satu arah.
long_description.en: The wild haggis (jokingly classified as Haggis scoticus) is a made-up creature of Scottish folklore, supposedly native to the Scottish Highlands. It is claimed in jest to be where haggis comes from, though that traditional Scottish dish is really made from sheep's innards such as heart, lungs and liver. Some say its left and right legs differ in length, like those of the sidehill gouger and the dahu, so it can race round the steep mountains and slopes it lives on, but only one way.

long_description.id: Konon ada dua varietas haggis, satu berkaki kiri lebih panjang dan satu berkaki kanan lebih panjang, yang berlari searah atau berlawanan arah jarum jam mengelilingi gunung. Keduanya hidup damai tetapi tak dapat kawin silang di alam liar, karena jantan harus berbalik menghadap arah yang sama dengan betina dan kehilangan keseimbangan. Menurut survei daring yang dipesan produsen haggis Hall's of Broxburn pada 2003, sepertiga pengunjung AS ke Skotlandia percaya wild haggis makhluk nyata. Menurut artikel de, ia digambarkan sebagai hewan kecil berbulu mirip persilangan kelinci dan tupai.
long_description.en: There are said to be two varieties, one with longer left legs and one with longer right legs, running clockwise or anticlockwise round a mountain. They live in peace but cannot interbreed in the wild, since a male would have to turn to face the female's way and lose his balance. In an online survey commissioned by haggis maker Hall's of Broxburn in 2003, a third of US visitors to Scotland believed the wild haggis was real. According to the de article it is pictured as a small furry animal like a cross between a rabbit and a squirrel.

famous_for.en: Runs one way only.

did_you_know.id: Pada 2003 sepertiga pengunjung AS ke Skotlandia dalam sebuah survei percaya wild haggis adalah makhluk nyata.
did_you_know.en: In a 2003 survey a third of US visitors to Scotland believed the wild haggis was a real creature.

note.id: Hewan rekaan dengan kaki tak sama panjang.
note.en: Fictional animal with uneven legs.
Similar fictional animal.

claims.quote: Wild haggis (given the humorous taxonomic designation Haggis scoticus) is a fictional creature of Scottish folklore, said to be native to the Scottish Highlands. It is comically claimed to be the source of haggis, a traditional Scottish dish that is in fact made from the innards of sheep (including heart, lungs, and liver).

statement.id: Wild haggis (Haggis scoticus) makhluk rekaan cerita rakyat Skotlandia (Scottish folklore), Dataran Tinggi Skotlandia (Scottish Highlands), sumber haggis secara bercanda; di Britania Raya.
statement.en: The wild haggis (Haggis scoticus) is a fictional creature of Scottish folklore from the Scottish Highlands, jokingly the source of haggis.

claims.quote: According to some sources, the wild haggis's left and right legs are of different lengths (like the sidehill gouger and the dahu), allowing it to run quickly around the steep mountains and hillsides which make up its natural habitat, but only in one direction.

statement.id: Kaki kiri dan kanan berbeda panjang (seperti sidehill gouger dan dahu, Dahu, Sidehill gouger), berlari di gunung hanya satu arah.
statement.en: Its legs differ in length (like the sidehill gouger and dahu), running round mountains one way only.

claims.quote: The two varieties coexist peacefully but are unable to interbreed in the wild because in order for the male of one variety to mate with a female of the other, he must turn to face in the same direction as his intended mate, causing him to lose his balance before he can mount her.

statement.id: Dua varietas tak bisa kawin silang karena jantan kehilangan keseimbangan.
statement.en: The two varieties cannot interbreed because the male loses his balance.

claims.quote: According to an online survey commissioned by haggis manufacturers Hall's of Broxburn, released on 26 November 2003, one-third of U.S. visitors to Scotland believed the wild haggis to be a real creature.

statement.id: Survei Hall's of Broxburn 2003: sepertiga pengunjung AS (U.S.) ke Skotlandia (Scotland) percaya ia nyata.
statement.en: A 2003 Hall's of Broxburn survey: a third of U.S. visitors to Scotland believed it real.

claims.quote: Das Wilde Haggis (humoristischer wissenschaftlicher Name: Haggis scoticus) ist ein fiktives kleines Säugetier der schottischen Folklore, das angeblich in den Highlands beheimatet ist.

statement.id: Wildes Haggis (Haggis scoticus) mamalia kecil rekaan (fiktives kleines Säugetier) folklore Skotlandia (schottischen), di Highlands.
statement.en: The Wildes Haggis (Haggis scoticus) is a fictional small mammal (fiktives kleines Säugetier) of Scottish (schottischen) folklore, said to live in the Highlands.

claims.quote: Das Wilde Haggis, eine in Schottland endemische Art, ist ein kleines, pelziges Tier, das einer Kreuzung aus Kaninchen und Eichhörnchen ähneln soll.

statement.id: Hewan kecil berbulu mirip persilangan kelinci (Kaninchen) dan tupai (Eichhörnchen), endemik Skotlandia (Schottland).
statement.en: A small furry animal like a cross of rabbit (Kaninchen) and squirrel (Eichhörnchen), endemic to Scotland (Schottland).

claims.quote: It is further claimed that there are two varieties of haggis, one with longer left legs and the other with longer right legs. The former variety can run clockwise around a mountain (as seen from above) while the latter can run anticlockwise.

statement.id: Dua varietas: kaki kiri atau kaki kanan lebih panjang, lari searah atau berlawanan jarum jam.
statement.en: Two varieties: longer left or right legs, running clockwise or anticlockwise.

short_description.id: Will-o'-the-wisp adalah fenomena cahaya hantu di malam hari yang dalam cerita rakyat dikaitkan dengan arwah atau peri penyesat musafir di rawa-rawa.
short_description.en: The will-o'-the-wisp is an atmospheric ghost light in folklore attributed to spirits or fairies that mislead travelers in marshes.

long_description.id: Will-o'-the-wisp, yang juga dikenal sebagai ignis fatuus, adalah penampakan cahaya hantu di malam hari, terutama di atas rawa atau lahan basah. Cerita rakyat sering mengaitkannya dengan hantu, peri, atau roh alam yang menampakkan atau menyembunyikan arah jalan. Sosok ini digambarkan menari atau melayang hingga kemudian memudar saat didekati.
long_description.en: The will-o'-the-wisp, also called ignis fatuus, is an atmospheric ghost light seen at night, particularly over bogs or marshes. Folklore associates it with ghosts, fairies, or elemental spirits that reveal or conceal paths. It is depicted as dancing or flowing until fading when approached.

long_description.id: Secara etimologi, istilah ini merujuk pada lentera jerami yang dibawa oleh sosok bernama Will, serupa dengan sebutan jack-o'-lantern. Cerita rakyat mencatat nama-nama padanan seperti feu follet, Irrlicht, sebutan hinkypunk, serta Ellylldan.
long_description.en: Etymologically, the term stems from a straw torch associated with Will, akin to jack-o'-lantern. Folklore records corresponding names such as feu follet, Irrlicht, hinkypunk, and Ellylldan.

long_description.id: Dalam tradisi Skotlandia, fenomena ini sering digambarkan sebagai roh jahil atau hantu yang memikat musafir ke tempat berbahaya hingga menemui ajal, meski beberapa kisah mengaitkannya dengan petunjuk menuju harta terpendam. Beberapa keyakinan menyebut roh-roh ini adalah jiwa yang tidak diterima di Surga maupun Neraka sehingga terpaksa mengembara selamanya.
long_description.en: In Scottish traditions, these lights are often depicted as mischievous spirits or ghosts luring travelers off safe paths to their doom, though rare tales associate them with guiding to vast treasure. Some believe they represent souls rejected by both Heaven and Hell, doomed to wander.

literal_meaning.id: ikatan jerami yang dipakai sebagai obor
literal_meaning.en: a twist of straw used as a torch

learning_questions.id: Mengapa cahaya rawa di berbagai belahan dunia hampir selalu dihubungkan dengan makhluk gaib penyesat jalan?
learning_questions.en: Why are marsh lights across different world cultures almost consistently linked to deceptive supernatural beings?

claims.quote: In folklore, a will-o'-the-wisp, or will-o'-wisp (Latin: ignis fatuus, "foolish flame"), is an atmospheric ghost light seen by travellers at night, especially over bogs, swamps, or marshes.

statement.id: Will-o'-the-wisp atau ignis fatuus adalah cahaya hantu atmosfer yang dilihat musafir di malam hari di atas rawa atau lahan basah.
statement.en: A will-o'-the-wisp or ignis fatuus is an atmospheric ghost light seen by travellers at night, especially over bogs, swamps, or marshes.

claims.quote: In folklore, will-o'-the-wisps are typically attributed as ghosts, fairies or elemental spirits meant to reveal (or conceal) a path or direction.

statement.id: Will-o'-the-wisp biasanya dianggap sebagai hantu, peri, atau roh alam penunjuk atau penyembunyi jalan.
statement.en: Will-o'-the-wisps are typically attributed as ghosts, fairies or elemental spirits meant to reveal or conceal a path or direction.

claims.quote: These wisps are portrayed as dancing or flowing in a static form, until noticed or followed, in which case they visually fade or disappear.

statement.id: Cahaya ini digambarkan menari atau melayang statis hingga memudar atau lenyap saat diikuti.
statement.en: These wisps are portrayed as dancing or flowing in a static form, until noticed or followed, in which case they visually fade or disappear.

claims.quote: The term will-o'-the-wisp comes from wisp, a bundle of sticks or paper sometimes used as a torch and the name 'Will', thus meaning 'Will of the torch'.

statement.id: Istilah will-o'-the-wisp berasal dari kata wisp yang berarti ikatan kayu atau kertas untuk obor, dan nama Will.
statement.en: The term will-o'-the-wisp comes from wisp, a bundle of sticks or paper used as a torch, and the name Will.

claims.quote: The term jack-o'-lantern ('Jack of the lantern') originally referred to a will-o'-the-wisp.

statement.id: Istilah jack-o'-lantern awalnya merujuk pada will-o'-the-wisp.
statement.en: The term jack-o'-lantern originally referred to a will-o'-the-wisp.

claims.quote: Equivalents of the will-o'-the-wisps appear in European folklore by various names, e.g., ignis fatuus in Latin, feu follet in French, Irrlicht or Irrwisch in Germany, dwaallicht in The Netherlands and fuoco fatuo in Italy.

statement.id: Padanan will-o'-the-wisp muncul dalam cerita rakyat Eropa dengan berbagai nama, seperti ignis fatuus, feu follet, Irrlicht, dwaallicht, dan fuoco fatuo.
statement.en: Equivalents of will-o'-the-wisps appear in European folklore under names such as ignis fatuus, feu follet, Irrlicht, dwaallicht, and fuoco fatuo.

claims.quote: The phenomenon is known in the United Kingdom by a variety of names, including jack-o'-lantern, friar's lantern, and hinkypunk, and is said to mislead and/or guide travellers by resembling a flickering lamp or lantern.

statement.id: Di Britania Raya fenomena ini dikenal dengan berbagai nama termasuk jack-o'-lantern, friar's lantern, dan hinkypunk.
statement.en: The phenomenon is known in the United Kingdom by various names including jack-o'-lantern, friar's lantern, and hinkypunk.

claims.quote: In Scottish folklore, will-o’-the-wisps are variously depicted either as mischievous spirits (typically fairies), or even the ghosts of the dead, eager to lead travellers off their path and into their death.

statement.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Skotlandia, will-o'-the-wisp digambarkan sebagai roh jahil atau hantu orang mati yang memikat pengelana keluar dari jalur menuju kematian.
statement.en: In Scottish folklore, will-o'-the-wisps are depicted as mischievous spirits or ghosts of the dead eager to lead travellers off path and to death.

claims.quote: The lights typically appear close to a bog, marsh, or swamp, places where straying off the beaten path can become dangerous – or even deadly.

statement.id: Cahaya tersebut biasanya muncul dekat rawa atau paya di mana tersesat dari jalan setapak bisa berbahaya atau mematikan.
statement.en: The lights typically appear close to a bog, marsh, or swamp where straying off path can become dangerous or deadly.

claims.quote: Few myths, however, show the will-o’-the-wisps leading those brave enough to follow the light in the middle of the dark night to a vast treasure, and riches beyond comprehension.

statement.id: Beberapa mitos menggambarkan will-o'-the-wisp memandu orang yang berani mengikuti cahaya menuju harta karun besar.
statement.en: Few myths show the will-o'-the-wisps leading those brave enough to follow the light in the dark night to vast treasure.

claims.quote: Some believe that the spirits behind the will-o’-the-wisps were souls who could enter neither Heaven nor Hell, and were thus forced to wander the earth forever.

statement.id: Sebagian percaya roh will-o'-the-wisp adalah jiwa yang tidak dapat masuk Surga maupun Neraka dan terpaksa mengembara selamanya.
statement.en: Some believe the spirits behind will-o'-the-wisps were souls unable to enter Heaven or Hell, forced to wander the earth forever.

claims.quote: Uniquely, in Sweden, the will-o’-the-wisp is a manifestation of an unbaptised soul, who tries to lead travellers into bodies of water, in hopes of being baptised.

statement.id: Di Swedia will-o'-the-wisp dipandang sebagai perwujudan jiwa yang belum dibaptis yang menuntun musafir ke perairan demi dibaptis.
statement.en: In Sweden, the will-o'-the-wisp is a manifestation of an unbaptised soul trying to lead travellers into water in hopes of baptism.

claims.quote: Will-o'-the-Wisp is the most common English designation for a family of fairy-beings characterized by their fiery appearance and their tendency to lead nighttime wayfarers astray.

statement.id: Will-o'-the-Wisp adalah sebutan bahasa Inggris paling umum bagi keluarga makhluk peri berpenampilan api yang suka menyesatkan pejalan malam.
statement.en: Will-o'-the-Wisp is the most common English designation for fairy-beings characterized by fiery appearance and misleading wayfarers.

claims.quote: The term wisp refers to a twist of straw, used as a torch.

statement.id: Istilah wisp merujuk pada pilinan jerami yang digunakan sebagai obor.
statement.en: The term wisp refers to a twist of straw, used as a torch.

claims.quote: Other names for these apparitions include Hobby-Lantern, Jack-o'-Lantern, Jenny-Burnt-Tale, Kitty-Candlestick, Peg-a-Lantern, and many more.

statement.id: Nama lain untuk penampakan ini mencakup Hobby-Lantern, Jack-o'-Lantern, Jenny-Burnt-Tale, Kitty-Candlestick, dan Peg-a-Lantern.
statement.en: Other names for these apparitions include Hobby-Lantern, Jack-o'-Lantern, Jenny-Burnt-Tale, Kitty-Candlestick, and Peg-a-Lantern.

claims.quote: The Ellylldan is a species of elf exactly corresponding to the English will-o'-wisp.

statement.id: Ellylldan adalah jenis peri Wales yang berpadanan persis dengan will-o'-wisp Inggris.
statement.en: The Ellylldan is a species of elf exactly corresponding to the English will-o'-wisp.
